title.zh: 新唐書巻四十九上 志第三十九上 百官四上
title.en: 新唐書巻四十九上 志第三十九上 百官四上
title.raw: 新唐書巻四十九上 志第三十九上 百官四上

sentences.zh: 十六衞左右衞上將軍各一人，從二品；

translations.literal: Of the Sixteen Guards, the Senior Generals of the Left and Right Guards — one each, secondary second rank;
translations.idiomatic: Among the Sixteen Guards, the Left and Right Guards each had one Senior General of secondary second rank;

sentences.zh: 大將軍各一人，正三品；

translations.literal: Grand Generals — one each, upper third rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each also had one Grand General of upper third rank;

sentences.zh: 將軍各二人，從三品。

translations.literal: Generals — two each, secondary third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each had two Generals of secondary third rank.

sentences.zh: 掌宮禁宿衞，凡五府及外府皆總制焉。

translations.literal: They managed palace-gate security and overnight guard service; all five inner guard offices and the outer guard commands were under their general control.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw palace security and night watches, exercising overall authority over all five inner guard offices and the outer commands.

sentences.zh: 凡五府三衞及折衝府驍騎番上者，受其名簿而配以職。

translations.literal: For those rotating to duty from the five guard offices, the Three Guards, and valiant cavalry of the assault-and-repulse commands, they received name rolls and assigned posts.
translations.idiomatic: They received the rosters of men rotating to palace duty from the five inner offices, the Three Guards, and valiant cavalry of the assault-and-repulse commands, and assigned them their posts.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御正殿，則守諸門及内廂宿衞仗。

translations.literal: When the emperor held court in the main hall, they guarded all gates and the inner quarters for overnight guard service and ceremonial arms.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor presided in the main audience hall, they guarded the gates and inner precincts, standing overnight watch and bearing ceremonial arms.

sentences.zh: 非上日，亦將軍一人押仗，將軍缺，以中郎將代將軍，掌貳上將軍之事。

translations.literal: On non-audience days as well, one General supervised the ceremonial guard; if no General was available, a Colonel substituted, assisting the Senior General.
translations.idiomatic: Even on days without an imperial audience, one General supervised the guard formation; when that post was vacant, a Colonel served in his place as deputy to the Senior General.

sentences.zh: 左右驍衞、左右武衞、左右威衞、左右領軍、左右金吾、左右監門衞上將軍以下，品同。

translations.literal: Below the Senior Generals of the Left and Right Valiant Guards, Martial Guards, Awesome Guards, Army-leader Guards, Gold Crow Guards, and Gate-keeping Guards — ranks were the same.
translations.idiomatic: The rank structure below the Senior Generals was identical for the Left and Right Valiant, Martial, Awesome, Army-leader, Gold Crow, and Gate-keeping Guards.

sentences.zh: 武德五年，改左右翊衞曰左右衞府，左右驍騎衞曰左右驍騎府，左右屯衞曰左右威衞，左右禦衞曰左右領軍衞，左右備身府曰左右府，唯左右武衞府、左右監門府、左右候衞，仍隋不改。

translations.literal: In Wude 5, the Left and Right Assist Guards were renamed Left and Right Guard Offices; Left and Right Valiant Cavalry Guards to Left and Right Valiant Cavalry Offices; Left and Right Garrison Guards to Left and Right Awesome Guards; Left and Right Imperial Guards to Left and Right Army-leader Guards; the Bodyguard Office to the Left and Right Office — only the Left and Right Martial Guard Office, Gate-keeping Office, and Escort Guards kept Sui names unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 5 the Left and Right Assist Guards became the Left and Right Guard Offices; valiant cavalry guards became valiant cavalry offices; garrison guards became awesome guards; imperial guards became army-leader guards; and the bodyguard office became simply the left and right office — only the martial guard, gate-keeping, and escort guard offices retained their Sui titles.

sentences.zh: 顯慶五年，改左右府曰左右千牛府。

translations.literal: In Xianqing 5, the Left and Right Offices were renamed Left and Right Thousand-Ox Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 5 the Left and Right Offices were renamed the Left and Right Thousand-Ox Offices.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，左右衞府、驍衞府、武衞府，皆省「府」字，左右威衞曰左右武威衞，左右領軍衞曰左右戎衞，左右候衞曰左右金吾衞，左右監門府曰左右監門衞，左右千牛府曰左右奉宸衞，後又曰左右千牛衞。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2, the characters "Office" were dropped from the Left and Right Guard, Valiant Cavalry, and Martial Guard Offices; Left and Right Awesome Guards became Left and Right Martial Awesome Guards; Left and Right Army-leader Guards became Left and Right Military Guards; Left and Right Escort Guards became Left and Right Gold Crow Guards; Left and Right Gate-keeping Offices became Left and Right Gate-keeping Guards; Left and Right Thousand-Ox Offices became Left and Right Imperial Attendant Guards — later again called Left and Right Thousand-Ox Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the word "Office" was dropped from the guard, valiant cavalry, and martial guard titles; awesome guards became martial awesome guards; army-leader guards became military guards; escort guards became gold crow guards; gate-keeping offices became gate-keeping guards; and thousand-ox offices became imperial attendant guards — a name later reverted to thousand-ox guards.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，改左右戎衞曰領軍衞。

translations.literal: In Xianheng 1, the Left and Right Military Guards were renamed Army-leader Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng 1 the Left and Right Military Guards were restored to the name Army-leader Guards.

sentences.zh: 武后光宅元年，改左右驍衞曰左右武威，左右武衞曰左右鷹揚衞，左右威衞曰左右豹韜衞，左右領軍衞曰左右玉鈐衞。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's first year of Guangzhai, the Left and Right Valiant Guards became Left and Right Martial Awesome Guards; Left and Right Martial Guards became Left and Right Soaring Eagle Guards; Left and Right Awesome Guards became Left and Right Leopard Strategy Guards; Left and Right Army-leader Guards became Left and Right Jade Seal Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangzhai under Empress Wu, the valiant guards were renamed martial awesome guards; martial guards became soaring eagle guards; awesome guards became leopard strategy guards; and army-leader guards became jade seal guards.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，初置十六衞上將軍。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan 2, Senior Generals of the Sixteen Guards were first established.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2 the post of Senior General was first created for each of the Sixteen Guards.

sentences.zh: 左右衞有録事一人，府一人，史二人，亭長八人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Guards each had one clerk, one office assistant, two scribes, eight station chiefs, and four gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Guards each employed one clerk, one office assistant, two scribes, eight station chiefs, and four gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 長史各一人，從六品上。

translations.literal: Chief Administrators — one each, upper secondary sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard had one Chief Administrator of upper secondary sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌判諸曹、五府、外府稟祿，卒伍、軍團之名數，器械、車馬之多少，小事得專達，毎歳秋，贊大將軍考課。

translations.literal: They adjudicated matters of the various bureaus and managed stipends for the five and outer guard offices, the roster counts of soldiers and units, and the quantities of equipment and horses; they could report directly on minor matters, and each autumn assisted the Grand General in performance reviews.
translations.idiomatic: They handled bureau business and oversaw stipends for the five inner and outer guard offices, troop and unit rosters, and inventories of arms and horses; on minor matters they could act on their own authority, and each autumn they assisted the Grand General in annual evaluations.

sentences.zh: 録事參軍事各一人，正八品上。

translations.literal: Recording Secretaries — one each, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard had one Recording Secretary of upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌受諸曹及五府、外府之事，句稽抄目，印給紙筆。

translations.literal: They received matters from the various bureaus and the five and outer guard offices, checked and copied records, and issued paper and writing brushes.
translations.idiomatic: They received business from the bureaus and from the five inner and outer guard offices, audited and copied documents, and distributed paper and writing supplies.

sentences.zh: 倉曹參軍事各二人，正八品下。

translations.literal: Granary Bureau Secretaries — two each, lower eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard had two Granary Bureau Secretaries of lower eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌五府文官勳考、假使、祿俸、公廨、田園、食料、醫藥、過所。

translations.literal: They managed merit evaluations, temporary assignments, salaries, government offices, estates, rations, medicine, and travel permits for civil officials of the five guard offices.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw merit records, temporary postings, salaries, official quarters, estates, rations, medical care, and travel permits for the civil staff of the five inner guard offices.

sentences.zh: 自倉曹以下同品。

translations.literal: From the Granary Bureau downward, ranks were the same.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaus below the Granary Bureau shared the same rank structure.

sentences.zh: 有府二人，史四人。

translations.literal: There were two office assistants and four scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Each bureau had two office assistants and four scribes.

sentences.zh: 兵曹，府四人，史七人。

translations.literal: The Military Bureau had four office assistants and seven scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau employed four office assistants and seven scribes.

sentences.zh: 騎曹，府二人，史四人。

translations.literal: The Cavalry Bureau had two office assistants and four scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Cavalry Bureau had two office assistants and four scribes.

sentences.zh: 冑曹，府三人，史三人。

translations.literal: The Armor Bureau had three office assistants and three scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Armor Bureau had three office assistants and three scribes.

sentences.zh: 武后長安初，改鎧曹曰冑曹，中宗卽位復舊，先天元年又曰冑曹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Empress Wu's Chang'an era, the Armor Bureau was renamed the Helmet Bureau; when Emperor Zhongzong took the throne the old name was restored; in the first year of Xiantian it was again called the Helmet Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Empress Wu's Chang'an reign the Armor Bureau was renamed the Helmet Bureau; Emperor Zhongzong restored the old title on his accession; and in Xiantian 1 it was again called the Helmet Bureau.

sentences.zh: 開元初，諸衞司倉、司兵、騎兵參軍，改曰倉曹、兵曹、騎曹、冑曹參軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, the guard bureaus' granary, military, cavalry, and armor secretaries were renamed Granary, Military, Cavalry, and Helmet Bureau Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era the guard granary, military, cavalry, and armor secretaries were retitled Granary, Military, Cavalry, and Helmet Bureau Secretaries.

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事各二人，掌五府武官宿衞番第，受其名數，而大將軍配焉。

translations.literal: Military Bureau Secretaries — two each — managed the rotation schedules of military officials on overnight guard duty in the five guard offices, received their name counts, and the Grand General assigned them.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard had two Military Bureau Secretaries who managed the rotation rosters of military officers on palace guard duty in the five inner offices; they received the name lists and the Grand General made the assignments.

sentences.zh: 騎曹參軍事各一人，掌外府雜畜簿帳、牧養。

translations.literal: Cavalry Bureau Secretaries — one each — managed the ledgers and pasturing of miscellaneous livestock of the outer guard commands.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard had one Cavalry Bureau Secretary who kept the livestock records and supervised the pasturing of horses and other animals in the outer commands.

sentences.zh: 凡府馬承直，以遠近分七番，月一易之。

translations.literal: For all guard-command horses on permanent duty, they were divided into seven watches by distance, changed once a month.
translations.idiomatic: Horses on standing duty at the guard commands were divided into seven watches according to distance and rotated monthly.

sentences.zh: 以敕出宮城者，給馬。

translations.literal: Those leaving the palace city by imperial edict were provided horses.
translations.idiomatic: Officials departing the palace precinct on imperial orders were issued horses.

sentences.zh: 冑曹參軍事各一人，掌兵械、公廨興繕、罰讁。

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau Secretaries — one each — managed weapons and armor, construction and repair of government offices, and punishments and reprimands.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard had one Helmet Bureau Secretary who oversaw arms and armor, the construction and repair of official buildings, and disciplinary penalties.

sentences.zh: 大朝會行從，則受黃質甲鎧、弓矢於衞尉。

translations.literal: At great court assemblies and processions, they received yellow-quality armor and bows and arrows from the Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At major court assemblies and imperial processions they drew yellow ceremonial armor, bows, and arrows from the Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 奉車都尉，掌馭副車。

translations.literal: Chamberlain of the Imperial Carriage managed driving the secondary carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Chamberlain of the Imperial Carriage was responsible for driving the secondary imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 有其名而無其人，大陳設則它官攝。

translations.literal: The title existed but there was no permanent appointee; at major ceremonies other officials served in the role.
translations.idiomatic: The post existed in name only; at grand ceremonies other officials were assigned to fill it.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉無定員，與奉車都尉皆從五品下。

translations.literal: Chamberlains of the Imperial Son-in-Law had no fixed quota; both they and the Chamberlains of the Imperial Carriage were lower secondary fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chamberlains of the Imperial Son-in-Law had no fixed number of posts; both they and the Chamberlains of the Imperial Carriage held lower secondary fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 司階各二人，正六品上；

translations.literal: Stairway Officers — two each, upper sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each guard had two Stairway Officers of upper sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 中候各三人，正七品下；

translations.literal: Middle Escorts — three each, lower seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: Three Middle Escorts each of lower seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 司戈各五人，正八品下；

translations.literal: Halberd Officers — five each, lower eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Five Halberd Officers each of lower eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 執戟各五人，正九品下；

translations.literal: Halberd Bearers — five each, lower ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Five Halberd Bearers each of lower ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 長上各二十五人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Senior Guards — twenty-five each, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five Senior Guards each of lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 武后天授二年，置諸衞司階、中候、司戈、執戟，謂之四色官。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's second year of Tianshou, Stairway Officers, Middle Escorts, Halberd Officers, and Halberd Bearers were established in all guards — called the Four-Colored Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshou 2 under Empress Wu the Stairway Officer, Middle Escort, Halberd Officer, and Halberd Bearer posts were created in every guard — collectively known as the Four-Colored Offices.

sentences.zh: 親衞之府一：曰親府。

translations.literal: The Personal Guard had one office: called the Personal Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Personal Guard comprised one office, called the Personal Office.

sentences.zh: 勳衞之府二：一曰勳一府，二曰勳二府。

translations.literal: The Merit Guard had two offices: the first called Merit First Office, the second Merit Second Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Merit Guard had two offices: Merit First and Merit Second.

sentences.zh: 翊衞之府二：一曰翊一府，二曰翊二府。

translations.literal: The Assist Guard had two offices: the first called Assist First Office, the second Assist Second Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Assist Guard had two offices: Assist First and Assist Second.

sentences.zh: 凡五府。

translations.literal: Five offices in all.
translations.idiomatic: Five inner guard offices in all.

sentences.zh: 毎府，中郎將一人，正四品下；

translations.literal: In each office, one Colonel, lower fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one Colonel of lower fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 左右郎將一人，正五品上；

translations.literal: One Left and one Right Vice Colonel, upper fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: One Left and one Right Vice Colonel each of upper fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 親衞，正七品上；

translations.literal: Personal Guards, upper seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: Personal Guards held upper seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 勳衞，從七品上；

translations.literal: Merit Guards, upper secondary seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: Merit Guards held upper secondary seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 翊衞，正八品上。

translations.literal: Assist Guards, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Assist Guards held upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 總四千九百六十三人。

translations.literal: Four thousand nine hundred sixty-three persons in total.
translations.idiomatic: The total strength was 4,963 men.

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事各一人，正九品上；

translations.literal: Military Bureau Secretaries — one each, upper ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one Military Bureau Secretary of upper ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 校尉各五人，正六品上。

translations.literal: Captains — five each, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had five Captains of upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 毎校尉有旅帥二人，從六品上；

translations.literal: Each Captain had two Brigade Commanders, upper secondary sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Under each Captain were two Brigade Commanders of upper secondary sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 毎旅帥各有隊正二十人，正七品上，副隊正二十人，正七品下。

translations.literal: Each Brigade Commander had twenty Squad Leaders of upper seventh rank and twenty Deputy Squad Leaders of lower seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each Brigade Commander commanded twenty Squad Leaders of upper seventh rank and twenty Deputy Squad Leaders of lower seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 五府中郎將掌領校尉、旅帥、親衞、勳衞之屬宿衞者，而總其府事；

translations.literal: The Colonels of the five guard offices commanded the Captains, Brigade Commanders, and subordinates of the Personal and Merit Guards on overnight guard duty, and managed all affairs of their offices;
translations.idiomatic: The Colonels of the five inner offices commanded the Captains, Brigade Commanders, and Personal and Merit Guards on palace watch, and oversaw all business of their offices;

sentences.zh: 左右郎將貳焉。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Vice Colonels assisted them.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Vice Colonels served as their deputies.

sentences.zh: 番上者，以名簿上于大將軍而配以職。

translations.literal: Those on rotation submitted name rolls to the Grand General and were assigned posts.
translations.idiomatic: Men rotating to palace duty submitted their rosters to the Grand General, who assigned their posts.

sentences.zh: 武德、貞觀世重資蔭，二品、三品子，補親衞；

translations.literal: In the Wude and Zhenguan eras hereditary privilege was valued; sons of second- and third-rank officials were appointed to the Personal Guard;
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude and Zhenguan periods hereditary privilege weighed heavily: sons of second- and third-rank officials entered the Personal Guard;

sentences.zh: 二品曾孫、三品孫、四品子、職事官五品子若孫、勳官三品以上有封及國公子，補勳衞及率府親衞；

translations.literal: Great-grandsons of second-rank officials, grandsons of third-rank officials, sons of fourth-rank officials, sons or grandsons of fifth-rank functional officials, merit officials of third rank and above with enfeoffments, and sons of princes of the realm were appointed to the Merit Guard and Personal Guard of the Guard Command;
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandsons of second-rank ministers, grandsons of third-rank ministers, sons of fourth-rank officials, sons or grandsons of fifth-rank officeholders, ennobled merit officials of third rank and above, and imperial princes' sons entered the Merit Guard or the Guard Command's Personal Guard;

sentences.zh: 四品孫、五品及上柱國子，補翊衞及率府勳衞；

translations.literal: Grandsons of fourth-rank officials, fifth-rank officials, and sons of Upper Pillar of State were appointed to the Assist Guard and Merit Guard of the Guard Command;
translations.idiomatic: Grandsons of fourth-rank officials, fifth-rank officials themselves, and sons of Upper Pillars of State entered the Assist Guard or the Guard Command's Merit Guard;

sentences.zh: 勳官二品及縣男以上、散官五品以上子若孫，補諸衞及率府翊衞。

translations.literal: Merit officials of second rank and district barons and above, and sons or grandsons of honorary officials of fifth rank and above, were appointed to the Assist Guards of the various guards and Guard Command.
translations.idiomatic: Second-rank merit officials and holders of district baron rank and above, together with sons or grandsons of fifth-rank honorary officials, entered the Assist Guards of the guard commands and Guard Command.

sentences.zh: 王府執仗親事、執乘親事，毎月番上者數千人，宿衞内廡及城門，給稟食。

translations.literal: Palace attendants bearing arms and attendants managing carriages from princely establishments — several thousand rotating monthly — guarded the inner corridors and city gates overnight and received grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand princely household attendants bearing arms or managing carriages rotated to duty each month, standing watch in the inner corridors and at the city gates and receiving grain rations.

sentences.zh: 執扇三衞三百人，擇少壯肩膊齊、儀容整美者，本衞印臂，送殿中省肄習，仗下，毎番三衞一人，爲太僕寺引輅。

translations.literal: Three hundred Fan-bearing Three Guards were selected for youth, strength, even shoulders, and handsome appearance; their home guard stamped their arms and sent them to the Palace Directorate for training; after the guard formation was dismissed, one Three Guard from each watch served as carriage guide for the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred fan-bearing Three Guards were chosen for youth, strength, even shoulders, and fine appearance; their home guard stamped their arms and sent them to the Palace Directorate for drill — and after each guard formation one Three Guard from each watch guided the imperial carriage for the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 其後入官路艱，三衞非權勢子弟輒退番，柱國子有白首不得進者；

translations.literal: Later the path to office grew difficult; Three Guards who were not sons of powerful families were repeatedly removed from rotation, and sons of Pillars of State grew white-haired without advancement;
translations.idiomatic: Later the road to office grew steep: Three Guards lacking powerful family connections were repeatedly bumped from rotation, and sons of Pillars of State could grow old without ever advancing;

sentences.zh: 流外雖鄙，不數年給祿稟。

translations.literal: Though men from outside the regular ranks were lowly, within a few years they received salaries and rations.
translations.idiomatic: Men from outside the regular hierarchy, however humble, received salaries and rations within a few years.

sentences.zh: 故三衞益賤，人罕趨之。

translations.literal: Therefore the Three Guards grew ever more degraded, and few sought the path.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Guards thus fell ever further in esteem, and few aspired to enter them.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府一人，史三人。

translations.literal: There was one clerk, one office assistant, and three scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Each inner office had one clerk, one office assistant, and three scribes.

sentences.zh: 唐親衞、勳衞置驃騎將軍、車騎將軍，翊衞置車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Tang's Personal and Merit Guards had Commanders of Fast Cavalry and Commanders of Chariots and Cavalry; the Assist Guard had Commanders of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang the Personal and Merit Guards were headed by Commanders of Fast Cavalry and Commanders of Chariots and Cavalry; the Assist Guard had a Commander of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 武德七年，改驃騎將軍爲中郎將，車騎將軍皆爲郎將，分左右，以親衞曰一府，勳衞、翊衞曰二府，謂之三府衞。

translations.literal: In Wude 7, Commanders of Fast Cavalry were renamed Colonels; Commanders of Chariots and Cavalry all became Vice Colonels, divided into left and right; the Personal Guard was called one office, the Merit and Assist Guards two offices — called the Three-Office Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 7 Commanders of Fast Cavalry became Colonels and Commanders of Chariots and Cavalry became Vice Colonels, each divided into left and right; the Personal Guard formed one office and the Merit and Assist Guards two offices — together called the Three-Office Guards.

sentences.zh: 諸衞翊衞及率府親、勳衞，亦曰三衞。

translations.literal: The Assist Guards of the various guards and the Personal and Merit Guards of the Guard Command were also called the Three Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Assist Guards of the guard commands and the Personal and Merit Guards of the Guard Command were also collectively known as the Three Guards.

translations.literal: At the second point of the fifth watch, the drum was struck from within; all street drums echoed it, ward and market gates all opened; after three thousand beats, it ceased at the color of dawn.
translations.idiomatic: At the second point of the fifth watch the inner drum sounded, street drums answered in succession, and ward and market gates opened; after three thousand beats, the signal ceased at daybreak.

sentences.zh: 左右監門衞上將軍各一人，大將軍各一人，將軍各二人。

translations.literal: Left and Right Gate-keeping Guards — one Senior General each, one Grand General each, two Generals each.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Gate-keeping Guards each had one Senior General, one Grand General, and two Generals.

sentences.zh: 掌諸門禁衞及門籍。

translations.literal: They managed gate prohibitions, guard service, and gate registers.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw gate security, guard duty, and entry registers.

sentences.zh: 文武官九品以上，毎月送籍於引駕仗及監門衞，衞以帳報内門。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above each month sent registers to the imperial-escort guard and Gate-keeping Guards; the guards reported the ledger account to the inner gate.
translations.idiomatic: Each month, civil and military officials of rank nine and above submitted their registers to the imperial escort guard and Gate-keeping Guards, who reported the tally to the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 凡朝參、奏事、待詔官及繖扇儀仗出入者，閲其數。

translations.literal: For all attending court, presenting memorials, awaiting-edict officials, and those entering and leaving with parasols, fans, and ceremonial regalia, they checked the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: They verified the numbers of officials attending court, presenting memorials, awaiting imperial summons, and those entering or leaving with ceremonial parasols and regalia.

sentences.zh: 以物貨器用入宮者，有籍有傍。

translations.literal: For goods, merchandise, and implements brought into the palace, there were registers and pass slips.
translations.idiomatic: Items and goods brought into the palace required both registration records and pass documents.

sentences.zh: 左監門將軍判入，右監門將軍判出，月一易其籍。

translations.literal: The Left Gate-keeping General adjudicated entries, the Right Gate-keeping General adjudicated exits, and monthly they exchanged their registers.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Gate-keeping General handled entries and the Right Gate-keeping General handled exits, exchanging registers once each month.

sentences.zh: 行幸，則率屬於衙門監守。

translations.literal: On the emperor's travels, they led their subordinates to guard and keep watch at the yamen gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, they led their subordinates to stand guard at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 長史，掌判諸曹及禁門，巡視出入而司其籍、傍。

translations.literal: The Chief Administrator managed adjudication of all bureaus and prohibited gates, inspected entries and exits, and supervised their registers and pass slips.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Administrator adjudicated bureau affairs and restricted gates, inspected all comings and goings, and managed the registers and pass documents.

sentences.zh: 餘同左右衞。

translations.literal: The remainder was the same as the Left and Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: All other arrangements matched those of the Left and Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事兼掌倉曹，冑曹兼掌騎曹。

translations.literal: The Military Bureau Secretary concurrently managed the Granary Bureau; the Helmet Bureau Secretary concurrently managed the Cavalry Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau Secretary also oversaw the Granary Bureau, and the Helmet Bureau Secretary also oversaw the Cavalry Bureau.

sentences.zh: 左右翊中郞將府中郞將。

translations.literal: Left and Right Assist Colonel Offices — Colonels.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Assist Colonel Offices were headed by Colonels.

sentences.zh: 掌涖宮殿城門，皆左入右出。

translations.literal: They managed oversight of palace halls and city gates; all entered on the left and exited on the right.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised palace halls and city gates, enforcing the rule that all entered from the left and exited from the right.

sentences.zh: 中郞將各四人，長史各一人，録事參軍事各一人，兵曹參軍事各一人，冑曹參軍事各一人。

translations.literal: Colonels — four each; Chief Administrators — one each; Recording Secretaries — one each; Military Bureau Secretaries — one each; Helmet Bureau Secretaries — one each.
translations.idiomatic: Each gate-keeping guard had four Colonels, one Chief Administrator, one Recording Secretary, one Military Bureau Secretary, and one Helmet Bureau Secretary.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，史二人，亭長二人，掌固二人。

translations.literal: There were one clerk, two scribes, two station chiefs, and two gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The office had one clerk, two scribes, two station chiefs, and two gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 兵曹，府三人，史五人；

translations.literal: Military Bureau — three office assistants, five scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau had three office assistants and five scribes;

sentences.zh: 冑曹，府三人，史四人。

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau — three office assistants, four scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Helmet Bureau had three office assistants and four scribes.

sentences.zh: 監門校尉三百二十人，直長六百八十人，長入長上二十人，直長長上二十人。

translations.literal: Gate-keeping company commanders — 320; duty chiefs — 680; senior long-entry senior guards — 20; duty-chief senior guards — 20.
translations.idiomatic: There were 320 gate-keeping company commanders, 680 duty chiefs, 20 senior guards for long-entry service, and 20 senior guards among the duty chiefs.

sentences.zh: 監門校尉掌敍出入。

translations.literal: Gate-keeping company commanders managed ordering of entry and exit.
translations.idiomatic: Gate-keeping company commanders regulated the sequence of entries and exits.

sentences.zh: 唐改監門府郎將爲將軍。

translations.literal: Tang changed the Gate-keeping Office Vice Colonels to Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, the Vice Colonels of the Gate-keeping Office were renamed Generals.

sentences.zh: 左右千牛衞上將軍各一人，大將軍各一人，將軍各二人。

translations.literal: Left and Right Thousand-Ox Guards — one Senior General each, one Grand General each, two Generals each.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Thousand-Ox Guards each had one Senior General, one Grand General, and two Generals.

sentences.zh: 掌侍衞及供御兵仗。

translations.literal: They managed attendant guard service and supply of imperial military implements.
translations.idiomatic: They provided close attendance guard service and supplied the emperor's ceremonial arms.

sentences.zh: 以千牛備身左右執弓箭宿衞，以主仗守戎器。

translations.literal: Thousand-Ox bodyguards and bodyguard attendants on the left and right held bows and arrows for overnight guard service; master-of-arms guards kept military weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-Ox bodyguards and attendants on the left and right carried bows and arrows on overnight palace watch, while master-of-arms guards kept custody of ceremonial weapons.

sentences.zh: 朝日，領備身左右升殿列侍。

translations.literal: On audience days, they led the bodyguard attendants left and right to ascend the hall and stand in attendance in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: On days of imperial audience, they led the bodyguard attendants up to the hall to stand in ranked attendance.

sentences.zh: 親射，則率屬以從。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally shot, they led their subordinates to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor engaged in archery, they led their subordinates to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 胄曹參軍事，掌甲仗。

translations.literal: The Armor Bureau Secretary managed armor and implements.
translations.idiomatic: The Armor Bureau Secretary oversaw armor and ceremonial arms.

sentences.zh: 凡御仗之物二百一十有九，羽儀之物三百，自千牛以下分掌之。

translations.literal: All imperial-arm objects totaled two hundred and nineteen; ceremonial regalia objects totaled three hundred — from Thousand-Ox down they were divided to manage them.
translations.idiomatic: There were 219 types of imperial ceremonial arms and 300 types of ceremonial regalia, distributed for custody among ranks below the Thousand-Ox guards.

sentences.zh: 上日，執御弓箭者亦自備以入宿。

translations.literal: On audience days, those who held imperial bows and arrows also prepared their own equipment to enter for overnight guard.
translations.idiomatic: On audience days, archers bearing imperial bows and arrows brought their own equipment when entering for overnight duty.

sentences.zh: 主仗毎月上，則配以職，行從則兼騎曹。

translations.literal: Master-of-arms guards each month on rotation were assigned their posts; on procession travel they concurrently served the Cavalry Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Master-of-arms guards on monthly rotating duty were assigned their posts, and when traveling in procession they also served under the Cavalry Bureau.

sentences.zh: 中郎將各二人，長史各一人，録事參軍事各一人，兵曹參軍事各一人，冑曹參軍事各一人。

translations.literal: Colonels — two each; Chief Administrators — one each; Recording Secretaries — one each; Military Bureau Secretaries — one each; Helmet Bureau Secretaries — one each.
translations.idiomatic: Each thousand-ox guard had two Colonels, one Chief Administrator, one Recording Secretary, one Military Bureau Secretary, and one Helmet Bureau Secretary.

sentences.zh: 唐改備身郎將曰將軍，備身將曰中郎將，千牛左右、備身左右曰千牛備身。

translations.literal: Tang changed bodyguard Vice Colonels to Generals, bodyguard captains to Colonels, and thousand-ox left-right and bodyguard left-right to Thousand-Ox bodyguards.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, bodyguard Vice Colonels became Generals, bodyguard captains became Colonels, and the thousand-ox and bodyguard attendants on the left and right were renamed Thousand-Ox bodyguards.

sentences.zh: 初置備身主仗。

translations.literal: At first bodyguard master-of-arms guards were established.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguard master-of-arms guards were originally established at this time.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，史二人，亭長二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were one clerk, two scribes, two station chiefs, and four gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The office had one clerk, two scribes, two station chiefs, and four gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 兵曹，府一人，史二人；

translations.literal: Military Bureau — one office assistant, two scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau had one office assistant and two scribes;

sentences.zh: 冑曹，府一人，史一人。

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau — one office assistant, one scribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Helmet Bureau had one office assistant and one scribe.

sentences.zh: 千牛備身十二人，備身左右十二人，備身一百人，主仗一百五十人。

translations.literal: Thousand-Ox bodyguards — twelve; bodyguard attendants left and right — twelve; bodyguards — one hundred; master-of-arms guards — one hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve Thousand-Ox bodyguards, twelve bodyguard attendants on the left and right, one hundred bodyguards, and one hundred fifty master-of-arms guards.

sentences.zh: 千牛備身掌執御刀，服花鈿繡衣緑，執象笏，宿衞侍從。

translations.literal: Thousand-Ox bodyguards managed holding the imperial sword, wore flower-brocade embroidered green garments, held ivory tablets, and performed overnight guard service and attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-Ox bodyguards carried the imperial sword, wore green brocade embroidered with floral patterns, held ivory tablets, and served on overnight palace watch and close attendance.

sentences.zh: 備身左右掌執御弓矢，宿衞侍從。

translations.literal: Bodyguard attendants left and right managed holding imperial bows and arrows, and performed overnight guard service and attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguard attendants on the left and right carried imperial bows and arrows, serving on overnight palace watch and close attendance.

sentences.zh: 備身，掌宿衞侍從。

translations.literal: Bodyguards managed overnight guard service and attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguards performed overnight palace watch and close attendance duty.

sentences.zh: 主仗，掌守供御兵仗。

translations.literal: Master-of-arms guards managed keeping and supplying imperial military implements.
translations.idiomatic: Master-of-arms guards kept custody of and supplied the emperor's ceremonial arms.

sentences.zh: 左右翊中郞將府中郞將，掌供奉侍衞。

translations.literal: Colonels of the Left and Right Assist Colonel Offices managed supply service and attendant guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonels of the Left and Right Assist Colonel Offices oversaw ceremonial attendance and close guard service.

sentences.zh: 凡千牛及備身左右以御刀仗升殿供奉者，皆上將軍領之，中郎將佐其職。

translations.literal: All Thousand-Ox and bodyguard attendants left and right who ascended the hall with imperial swords and implements for attendance service were led by the Senior General, and Colonels assisted their duties.
translations.idiomatic: All Thousand-Ox guards and bodyguard attendants who entered the hall bearing imperial swords and arms for ceremonial service were commanded by the Senior General, with Colonels serving as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 有口敕，通事舍人承傳，聲不下聞者，中郎將宣告。

translations.literal: When there was an oral decree, the relay chamberlain transmitted it; when the voice did not reach below, the Colonel proclaimed it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor issued an oral decree, the relay chamberlain passed it down; if his voice did not carry, a Colonel repeated the announcement.

sentences.zh: 諸衞折衝都尉府諸衞折衝都尉府毎府折衝都尉一人，上府正四品上，中府從四品下，下府正五品下。

translations.literal: Assault-and-Repulse Commandant Offices of the various guards — each office had one Assault-and-Repulse Commandant; upper offices — upper fourth rank, upper grade; middle offices — secondary fourth rank, lower grade; lower offices — upper fifth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard's Assault-and-Repulse Commandant Office had one Assault-and-Repulse Commandant — upper fourth rank, upper grade in upper offices; secondary fourth rank, lower grade in middle offices; and upper fifth rank, lower grade in lower offices.

sentences.zh: 左右果毅都尉各一人，上府從五品下，中府正六品上，下府正六品下。

translations.literal: Left and Right Resolute Commandants — one each; upper offices — secondary fifth rank, lower grade; middle offices — upper sixth rank, upper grade; lower offices — upper sixth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one Left and Right Resolute Commandant — secondary fifth rank, lower grade in upper offices; upper sixth rank, upper grade in middle offices; and upper sixth rank, lower grade in lower offices.

sentences.zh: 別將各一人，上府正七品下，中府從七品上，下府從七品下。

translations.literal: Deputy Generals — one each; upper offices — upper seventh rank, lower grade; middle offices — secondary seventh rank, upper grade; lower offices — secondary seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one Deputy General — upper seventh rank, lower grade in upper offices; secondary seventh rank, upper grade in middle offices; and secondary seventh rank, lower grade in lower offices.

sentences.zh: 長史各一人，上府正七品下，中府從七品上，下府從七品下。

translations.literal: Chief Administrators — one each; upper offices — upper seventh rank, lower grade; middle offices — secondary seventh rank, upper grade; lower offices — secondary seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one Chief Administrator — upper seventh rank, lower grade in upper offices; secondary seventh rank, upper grade in middle offices; and secondary seventh rank, lower grade in lower offices.

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事各一人，上府正八品下，中府正九品下，下府從九品上。

translations.literal: Military Bureau Secretaries — one each; upper offices — upper eighth rank, lower grade; middle offices — upper ninth rank, lower grade; lower offices — secondary ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one Military Bureau Secretary — upper eighth rank, lower grade in upper offices; upper ninth rank, lower grade in middle offices; and secondary ninth rank, upper grade in lower offices.

sentences.zh: 校尉五人，從七品下。

translations.literal: Company commanders — five, secondary seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were five company commanders of secondary seventh rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 旅帥十人，從八品上。

translations.literal: Brigade leaders — ten, secondary eighth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were ten brigade leaders of secondary eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 隊正二十人，正九品下；

translations.literal: Squad chiefs — twenty, upper ninth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty squad chiefs of upper ninth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 副隊正二十人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Deputy squad chiefs — twenty, secondary ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty deputy squad chiefs of secondary ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 折衝都尉掌領屬備宿衞，師役則總戎具、資糧、點習，以三百人爲團，一校尉領之。

translations.literal: The Assault-and-Repulse Commandant managed leading subordinates in preparing overnight guard service; on military campaigns he assembled military equipment, provisions, and conducted drills — with three hundred men as a regiment, one company commander leading it.
translations.idiomatic: The Assault-and-Repulse Commandant led his subordinates in preparing for palace guard duty; on campaigns he gathered equipment and provisions, conducted drills, and organized units of three hundred men under a company commander.

sentences.zh: 捉鋪持更者，晨夜有行人必問，不應則彈弓而嚮之，復不應則旁射，又不應則射之。

translations.literal: Those holding the watch at capture posts — by day and night when travelers appeared they must be questioned; if they did not respond, a bow was drawn and aimed at them; if still no response, a shot was fired to the side; if again no response, they were shot.
translations.idiomatic: Sentry post watchmen questioned any traveler day or night; if there was no answer, they drew their bows and shouted a warning; if still unanswered, they fired a warning shot to the side; if there was still no reply, they shot to kill.

sentences.zh: 晝以排門人遠望，暮夜以持更人遠聽。

translations.literal: By day gate-bar personnel observed from afar; at dusk and night watch-holders listened from afar.
translations.idiomatic: By day, gate-bar personnel kept distant watch; at night, watchmen listened for sounds from afar.

sentences.zh: 有衆而囂，則告主帥。

translations.literal: When there was a crowd making an uproar, they reported to the commanding officer.
translations.idiomatic: If a crowd gathered and raised an outcry, they reported it to the commanding officer.

sentences.zh: 左右果毅都尉，掌貳都尉。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Resolute Commandants assisted the Assault-and-Repulse Commandant as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Resolute Commandants served as deputies to the Assault-and-Repulse Commandant.

sentences.zh: 毎府有録事一人，府一人，史二人。

translations.literal: Each office had one clerk, one office assistant, and two scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Each commandant office employed one clerk, one office assistant, and two scribes.

sentences.zh: 兵曹，府二人，史三人。

translations.literal: The Military Bureau had two office assistants and three scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau staff included two office assistants and three scribes.

sentences.zh: 毎隊正領兵五十人。

translations.literal: Each squad leader commanded fifty soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Each squad leader led a unit of fifty soldiers.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，改鷹揚郎將曰軍頭，正四品下；

translations.literal: In Wude 1, Eagle-Rising Vice Colonels were renamed Army Heads, upper fourth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1 Eagle-Rising Vice Colonels were retitled Army Heads, with a rank of upper fourth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 鷹撃郎將曰府副，正五品上；

translations.literal: Eagle-Striking Vice Colonels were renamed Office Deputies, upper fifth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Eagle-Striking Vice Colonels became Office Deputies, ranked upper fifth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 司馬曰長史，正八品下；

translations.literal: Army Supervisors were renamed Chief Administrators, upper eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Army Supervisors were redesignated Chief Administrators of upper eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 校尉，正六品下，旅帥，正七品下。

translations.literal: Colonels — upper sixth rank, lower grade; brigade commanders — upper seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Colonels held upper sixth rank, lower grade; brigade commanders held upper seventh rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 廢越騎、歩兵二校尉及察非掾。

translations.literal: The two colonels for crossbow cavalry and infantry, and the irregularity-inspection clerks, were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The crossbow-cavalry and infantry colonels, together with the irregularity-inspection clerks, were eliminated.

sentences.zh: 又改軍頭曰驃騎將軍，府副曰車騎將軍，皆爲府。

translations.literal: Army Heads were again renamed Commanders of Fast Cavalry, Office Deputies Commanders of Chariots and Cavalry — all made into offices.
translations.idiomatic: Army Heads were next renamed Commanders of Fast Cavalry and Office Deputies Commanders of Chariots and Cavalry, each organized as its own office.

sentences.zh: 諸率府置驃騎將軍五人、車騎將軍十人。

translations.literal: Guard Commands established five Commanders of Fast Cavalry and ten Commanders of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Guard Commands were staffed with five Commanders of Fast Cavalry and ten Commanders of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 二年，以車騎將軍府隸驃騎府，置十二軍，分關内諸府皆隸焉。

translations.literal: In year 2, Chariots-and-Cavalry General offices were placed under Fast-Cavalry General offices; twelve armies were established, and the various offices within the passes were all made subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Chariots-and-Cavalry offices were subordinated to Fast-Cavalry offices; twelve armies were created, and the guard commands throughout the Guanzhong region were placed under them.

sentences.zh: 毎軍，將軍一人，副一人。

translations.literal: Each army had one general and one deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one commanding general and one deputy.

sentences.zh: 至六年廢。

translations.literal: By year 6 it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The arrangement was abolished in the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 七年，改驃騎將軍府爲統軍府，車騎將軍爲別將。

translations.literal: In year 7, Fast-Cavalry General offices were renamed Army Command Offices, and Chariots-and-Cavalry Generals became Deputy Generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Fast-Cavalry offices became Army Command Offices, and Chariots-and-Cavalry Generals were renamed Deputy Generals.

sentences.zh: 八年，復置十二軍。

translations.literal: In year 8, the twelve armies were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the twelve armies were restored.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十年，改統軍府曰折衝都尉，別將曰果毅都尉。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan 10, Army Command Offices were renamed Assault-and-Repulse Commandants, and Deputy Generals Resolute Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 10 Army Command Offices became Assault-and-Repulse Commandant offices and Deputy Generals became Resolute Commandants.

sentences.zh: 軍坊置坊主一人，檢校戸口，勸課農桑，以本坊五品勳官爲之。

translations.literal: Military wards established one ward chief each to inspect household registers and encourage farming and sericulture, drawn from merit officials of fifth rank within the ward.
translations.idiomatic: Each military ward had a ward chief who checked household registers and promoted agriculture and sericulture, chosen from fifth-rank merit officials of that ward.

sentences.zh: 三輔及近畿州都督府皆置府，凡六百三十三。

translations.literal: In the Three Metropolises and proximal metropolitan prefecture military commissions, offices were all established — six hundred thirty-three in total.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were established throughout the Three Metropolises and nearby metropolitan prefectures, six hundred thirty-three in all.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，廢長史，置司馬一人，總司兵、司騎二局。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era, Chief Administrators were abolished; one Army Supervisor was established to oversee the Military and Cavalry bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui period Chief Administrators were eliminated and a single Army Supervisor was appointed to head both the Military and Cavalry bureaus.

sentences.zh: 武后垂拱中，以千二百人爲上府，千人爲中府，八百人爲下府，赤縣爲赤府，畿縣爲畿府。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's Chuigong era, twelve hundred men made an upper office, one thousand a middle office, eight hundred a lower office; red-county offices were red offices, metropolitan-county offices capital offices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu in the Chuigong era upper offices fielded twelve hundred men, middle offices one thousand, and lower offices eight hundred; offices in red counties became red offices, and those in capital counties capital offices.

sentences.zh: 聖暦元年，廢司馬，置長史、兵曹參軍事，又有別將一人，從六品下，居果毅都尉之次，其後分左右各一人，尋廢。

translations.literal: In Shengli 1, the Army Supervisor was abolished; a Chief Administrator and Military Bureau Secretary were established, and there was also one Deputy General, secondary sixth rank, lower grade, ranking below the Resolute Commandant — later one left and one right each, soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengli 1 the Army Supervisor was removed; a Chief Administrator and Military Bureau Secretary were added, together with one Deputy General of secondary sixth rank, lower grade, ranking just below the Resolute Commandant — later split into left and right posts, then abolished.

sentences.zh: 久之，復置一人，降其品。

translations.literal: After some time, one was restored, with rank lowered.
translations.idiomatic: After an interval the post was restored as a single appointment, but at reduced rank.

sentences.zh: 開元初，衞士爲武士，諸衞折衝、果毅、別將，擇有行者爲展仗押官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, guard soldiers became warrior-guards; among the various guards' assault-and-repulse, resolute, and deputy generals, those selected for conduct served as formation-display escort officers.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaiyuan era guard soldiers were renamed warrior-guards, and Assault-and-Repulse Commandants, Resolute Commandants, and Deputy Generals from the guard commands who were chosen for their bearing served as ceremonial formation escort officers.

sentences.zh: 右羽林軍十五人，左羽林軍二十五人，衣服同色。

translations.literal: Right Feathered Forest Army — fifteen; Left Feathered Forest Army — twenty-five; clothing of the same color.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen were drawn from the Right Feathered Forest Army and twenty-five from the Left, all in matching dress.

sentences.zh: 諸衞有弩手，左右驍衞各八十五人，餘衞各八十三人。

translations.literal: The various guards had crossbowmen — Left and Right Valiant Guards eighty-five each, the remaining guards eighty-three each.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard maintained crossbowmen: the Left and Right Valiant Guards eighty-five apiece, the others eighty-three apiece.

sentences.zh: 左右羽林軍大將軍各一人，正三品；

translations.literal: Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies — one Senior General each, upper third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies each had one Senior General of upper third rank;

sentences.zh: 將軍各三人，從三品。

translations.literal: Generals — three each, secondary third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had three Generals of secondary third rank.

sentences.zh: 掌統北衙禁兵，督攝左右廂飛騎儀仗。

translations.literal: They managed commanding the northern palace forbidden troops, supervising and directing the left and right wing flying-cavalry ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: They commanded the northern palace guard forces and oversaw the flying-cavalry ceremonial units on the left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 大朝會，則周衞階陛；

translations.literal: At great court assemblies, they encircled and guarded the hall steps;
translations.idiomatic: At grand court assemblies they ringed the throne steps in guard formation;

sentences.zh: 巡幸，則夾馳道爲内仗。

translations.literal: On imperial progresses, they lined both sides of the imperial road as the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: During imperial tours they flanked the imperial highway as the inner escort guard.

sentences.zh: 凡飛騎番上者，配其職。

translations.literal: All flying cavalry rotating to palace duty were assigned to these posts.
translations.idiomatic: Flying cavalry on palace rotation were assigned to these duties.

sentences.zh: 有敕上南衙者，大將軍承墨敕，白移於金吾，引駕仗官與監門奏覆，降墨敕，然後乃得入。

translations.literal: When there was an edict to ascend the southern offices, the Senior General received the black-edict, reported and transferred to the Golden Crow Guard, brought escort-ceremony officials and the gate-keeping supervisor to memorialize for confirmation, received the black-edict down, and only then was entry permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial orders required the guard to enter the southern offices, the Senior General received the written edict, notified the Golden Crow Guard, and together with escort officials and the Gate-keeping Supervisor submitted a memorial for approval; only after the edict was formally issued could they enter.

sentences.zh: 長史各一人，從六品上；

translations.literal: Chief Administrators — one each, secondary sixth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one Chief Administrator of secondary sixth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 録事參軍事各一人，正八品上；

translations.literal: Recording Secretaries — one each, upper eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one Recording Secretary of upper eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 倉曹參軍事各一人，兼總騎曹事；

translations.literal: Granary Bureau Secretaries — one each, also overseeing Cavalry Bureau affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one Granary Bureau Secretary who also oversaw Cavalry Bureau affairs;

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事各一人；

translations.literal: Military Bureau Secretaries — one each;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one Military Bureau Secretary;

sentences.zh: 冑曹參軍事各一人。

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau Secretaries — one each.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one Helmet Bureau Secretary.

sentences.zh: 自倉曹參軍以下，皆正八品下。

translations.literal: From the Granary Bureau Secretary downward, all were upper eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: From the Granary Bureau Secretary down, all held upper eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 司階各二人，正六品上；

translations.literal: Stairway Officers — two each, upper sixth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had two Stairway Officers of upper sixth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 中候各三人，正七品下；

translations.literal: Middle Escorts — three each, upper seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had three Middle Escorts of upper seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 司戈各五人，正八品上；

translations.literal: Halberd Officers — five each, upper eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had five Halberd Officers of upper eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 執戟各五人，正九品下；

translations.literal: Halberd Bearers — five each, upper ninth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had five Halberd Bearers of upper ninth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 長上各十人。

translations.literal: Senior Guards — ten each.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had ten Senior Guards.

sentences.zh: 左右翊衞中郎將府中郎將一人，正四品下；

translations.literal: Left and Right Assist Guard Colonel Offices — one Colonel each, upper fourth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each Assist Colonel Office of the Left and Right Assist Guards had one Colonel of upper fourth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 左右中郎一人，左右郎將一人，皆正五品上；

translations.literal: One Left and one Right Central Vice Colonel, one Left and one Right Vice Colonel — all upper fifth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one Left and one Right Central Vice Colonel and one Left and one Right Vice Colonel, all of upper fifth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事一人，正九品上；

translations.literal: Military Bureau Secretaries — one each, upper ninth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one Military Bureau Secretary of upper ninth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 校尉五人，旅帥十人，隊正二十人，副隊正二十人。

translations.literal: Colonels — five; brigade commanders — ten; squad leaders — twenty; deputy squad leaders — twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had five Colonels, ten brigade commanders, twenty squad leaders, and twenty deputy squad leaders.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，史二人，亭長二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There was one clerk, two scribes, two station chiefs, and four gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one clerk, two scribes, two station chiefs, and four gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 倉曹、兵曹各府二人、史四人；

translations.literal: Granary and Military Bureaus — two office assistants and four scribes each;
translations.idiomatic: The Granary and Military Bureaus each had two office assistants and four scribes;

sentences.zh: 冑曹，府、史各二人。

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau — two office assistants and two scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Helmet Bureau had two office assistants and two scribes.

sentences.zh: 左右翊中郎將府，録事一人，府一人，史二人；

translations.literal: Left and Right Assist Colonel Offices — one clerk, one office assistant, two scribes each;
translations.idiomatic: Each Left and Right Assist Colonel Office had one clerk, one office assistant, and two scribes;

sentences.zh: 倉曹、兵曹各府二人，史四人；

translations.literal: Granary and Military Bureaus — two office assistants and four scribes each;
translations.idiomatic: The Granary and Military Bureaus each had two office assistants and four scribes;

sentences.zh: 冑曹，府、史各二人。

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau — two office assistants and two scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Helmet Bureau had two office assistants and two scribes.

sentences.zh: 左右龍武軍大將軍各一人，正二品；

translations.literal: Left and Right Dragon Martial Armies — one Senior General each, secondary second rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Dragon Martial Armies each had one Senior General of secondary second rank;

sentences.zh: 統軍各一人，正三品；

translations.literal: Army Commanders — one each, upper third rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one Army Commander of upper third rank;

sentences.zh: 將軍三人，從三品。

translations.literal: Generals — three, secondary third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had three Generals of secondary third rank.

sentences.zh: 掌同羽林。

translations.literal: Their duties were the same as the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Their responsibilities matched those of the Feathered Forest Armies.

sentences.zh: 長史、録事參軍事、倉曹參軍事、兵曹參軍事、胄曹參軍事各一人，司階各二人，中候各三人，司戈、執戟各五人，長上各十人。

translations.literal: Chief Administrators, Recording Secretaries, Granary Bureau Secretaries, Military Bureau Secretaries, and Helmet Bureau Secretaries — one each; Stairway Officers — two each; Middle Escorts — three each; Halberd Officers and Halberd Bearers — five each; Senior Guards — ten each.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one Chief Administrator, one Recording Secretary, one Granary Bureau Secretary, one Military Bureau Secretary, and one Helmet Bureau Secretary; two Stairway Officers; three Middle Escorts; five Halberd Officers and five Halberd Bearers; and ten Senior Guards.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，置龍武將軍。

translations.literal: In Jingyun 1, Dragon Martial Generals were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 1 the post of Dragon Martial General was created.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，六軍各置統軍。

translations.literal: In Xingyuan 1, each of the Six Armies established Army Commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingyuan 1 Army Commanders were appointed for each of the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，龍武軍增將軍一員，有録事一人，史二人，亭長二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan 3, the Dragon Martial Army added one General; there was one clerk, two scribes, two station chiefs, and four gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 3 one General was added to the Dragon Martial Army; the staff included one clerk, two scribes, two station chiefs, and four gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 倉曹，府二人，史四人；

translations.literal: Granary Bureau — two office assistants and four scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Bureau had two office assistants and four scribes;

sentences.zh: 兵曹，府二人，史四人；

translations.literal: Military Bureau — two office assistants and four scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau had two office assistants and four scribes;

sentences.zh: 冑曹，府、史各二人。

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau — two office assistants and two scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Helmet Bureau had two office assistants and two scribes.

sentences.zh: 左右神武軍大將軍各一人，正二品；

translations.literal: Left and Right Divine Martial Armies — one Senior General each, secondary second rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Divine Martial Armies each had one Senior General of secondary second rank;

sentences.zh: 統軍各一人，正三品；

translations.literal: Army Commanders — one each, upper third rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one Army Commander of upper third rank;

sentences.zh: 將軍三人，從三品。

translations.literal: Generals — three, secondary third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had three Generals of secondary third rank.

sentences.zh: 總衙前射生兵。

translations.literal: They commanded the archer-soldiers before the yamen gate.
translations.idiomatic: They commanded the archer-soldiers stationed before the headquarters gate.

sentences.zh: 長史、録事參軍事、倉曹參軍事、兵曹參軍事、胄曹參軍事各一人，司階各二人，中候各三人，司戈、執戟各五人，長上各十人。

translations.literal: Chief Administrators, Recording Secretaries, Granary Bureau Secretaries, Military Bureau Secretaries, and Helmet Bureau Secretaries — one each; Stairway Officers — two each; Middle Escorts — three each; Halberd Officers and Halberd Bearers — five each; Senior Guards — ten each.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one Chief Administrator, one Recording Secretary, one Granary Bureau Secretary, one Military Bureau Secretary, and one Helmet Bureau Secretary; two Stairway Officers; three Middle Escorts; five Halberd Officers and five Halberd Bearers; and ten Senior Guards.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，史二人，倉曹、兵曹、冑曹府、史，皆如龍武軍。

translations.literal: There was one clerk, two scribes; Granary, Military, and Helmet Bureau office assistants and scribes — all like the Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one clerk and two scribes; Granary, Military, and Helmet Bureau assistants and scribes followed the same pattern as the Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 開元二十六年，分羽林置左右神武軍，尋廢；

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 26, the Feathered Forest was divided to establish Left and Right Divine Martial Armies, soon abolished;
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 26 detachments from the Feathered Forest were used to create the Left and Right Divine Martial Armies, which were soon abolished;

sentences.zh: 至德二年復置。

translations.literal: In Zhide 2 they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: They were restored in Zhide 2.

sentences.zh: 左右神策軍大將軍各一人，正二品；

translations.literal: Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies — one Senior General each, secondary second rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies each had one Senior General of secondary second rank;

sentences.zh: 統軍各二人，正三品；

translations.literal: Army Commanders — two each, upper third rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had two Army Commanders of upper third rank;

sentences.zh: 將軍各四人，從三品。

translations.literal: Generals — four each, secondary third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had four Generals of secondary third rank.

sentences.zh: 掌衞兵及内外八鎭兵。

translations.literal: They managed guard soldiers and the troops of the eight inner and outer garrison commands.
translations.idiomatic: They commanded the palace guards and the forces of the eight inner and outer garrison commands.

sentences.zh: 護軍中尉各一人，中護軍各一人，判官各三人，都句判官二人，句覆官各一人。

translations.literal: Protecting-Army Central Commandants — one each; Central Protecting-Army Commandants — one each; case officers — three each; chief case officers — two; review officers — one each.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one Protecting-Army Central Commandant, one Central Protecting-Army Commandant, three case officers, two chief case officers, and one review officer.

sentences.zh: 表奏官各一人，支計官各一人，孔目官各二人，驅使官各二人。

translations.literal: Memorial-drafting officers — one each; disbursement officers — one each; registry officers — two each; messenger officers — two each.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had one memorial-drafting officer, one disbursement officer, two registry officers, and two messenger officers.

sentences.zh: 自長史以下，員數如龍武軍。

translations.literal: From the Chief Administrator downward, the number of posts was like the Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: From the Chief Administrator down, staffing matched that of the Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 左右龍武、左右神武、左右神策，號六軍。

translations.literal: Left and Right Dragon Martial, Left and Right Divine Martial, Left and Right Divine Strategy — called the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Dragon Martial, Divine Martial, and Divine Strategy Armies were collectively known as the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，神策軍置大將軍、將軍，十四年置統軍，品秩同六軍。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan 2, the Divine Strategy Army established Senior Generals and Generals; in year 14 Army Commanders were established — ranks the same as the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2 the Divine Strategy Army received Senior Generals and Generals; in the fourteenth year Army Commanders were added, with ranks identical to those of the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 始，殿前左右神威軍，有大將軍二人，正二品；

translations.literal: Initially, the Hall-Front Left and Right Divine Might Armies had two Senior Generals, secondary second rank;
translations.idiomatic: At first the Hall-Front Left and Right Divine Might Armies each had two Senior Generals of secondary second rank;

sentences.zh: 統軍二人，從三品；

translations.literal: Army Commanders — two, secondary third rank;
translations.idiomatic: There were two Army Commanders of secondary third rank;

sentences.zh: 將軍二人，從五品。

translations.literal: Generals — two, secondary fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Generals of secondary fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 元和初，爲一軍，號天威軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, they became one army, called the Heavenly Might Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanhe era the two were merged into a single army called the Heavenly Might Army.

sentences.zh: 八年廢，以軍隸神策，有馬軍、歩軍將軍及指揮使等，以馬軍大將軍知軍事。

translations.literal: In year 8 it was abolished; the army was made subordinate to the Divine Strategy Army; there were cavalry-army and infantry-army generals and command commissioners, with the cavalry-army Senior General managing army affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year it was abolished and the force was placed under the Divine Strategy Army; cavalry and infantry generals and command commissioners were appointed, with a cavalry Senior General in charge of operations.

sentences.zh: 天復三年廢神策軍，四年復置神策軍。

translations.literal: In Tianfu 3 the Divine Strategy Army was abolished; in year 4 the Divine Strategy Army was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Strategy Army was abolished in Tianfu 3 and restored in Tianfu 4.

sentences.zh: 東宮官東宮三師、三少、太子賓客太子太師、太傅、太保，各一人，從一品。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace offices — the Eastern Palace Three Preceptors and Three Junior Preceptors, the Crown Prince's Guests of Honor: the Crown Prince's Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector — one each, secondary first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Among Eastern Palace offices, the Three Preceptors and Three Junior Preceptors of the Eastern Palace and the Crown Prince's Guests of Honor — the Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector — were each one in number, of secondary first rank.

sentences.zh: 掌輔導皇太子。

translations.literal: They managed guiding and instructing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: They were charged with guiding and instructing the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 毎見，迎拜殿門，三師答拜，毎門必讓，三師坐，太子乃坐。

translations.literal: At each audience, they welcomed and bowed at the hall gate; the Three Preceptors returned bows; at each gate they must yield; when the Three Preceptors sat, then the crown prince sat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they attended the crown prince, they greeted him with obeisance at the palace gate and the Three Preceptors returned the courtesy; at every gate they yielded precedence; the crown prince did not sit until the Three Preceptors were seated.

sentences.zh: 與三師書，前名惶恐，後名惶恐再拜。

translations.literal: When writing to the Three Preceptors, before the name write "trembling with awe," after the name "trembling with awe, bowing twice."
translations.idiomatic: In letters to the Three Preceptors one wrote "trembling with awe" before the name and "trembling with awe, bowing twice" after it.

sentences.zh: 太子出，則乘路備鹵簿以從。

translations.literal: When the crown prince went out, he rode the imperial carriage with full ceremonial guard following.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince went abroad he rode the state carriage with full ceremonial escort.

sentences.zh: 少師、少傅、少保，各一人，從二品。

translations.literal: Junior Preceptors, Junior Tutors, and Junior Protectors — one each, secondary second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Junior Preceptor, Junior Tutor, and Junior Protector were each one in number, of secondary second rank.

sentences.zh: 掌曉三師德行，以諭皇太子，奉太子以觀三師之道德。

translations.literal: They managed explaining the Three Preceptors' conduct and character to instruct the crown prince, presenting the crown prince to observe the Three Preceptors' virtue and morality.
translations.idiomatic: They explained the Three Preceptors' conduct and character to the crown prince, presenting him to observe their moral example.

sentences.zh: 自太師以下唯其人，不必備。

translations.literal: From the Grand Preceptor downward, only when there was a suitable person — not necessarily all filled.
translations.idiomatic: From the Grand Preceptor down, appointments were made only when a worthy person was available — the posts need not all be filled.

sentences.zh: 先天元年開府，置令、丞各一人，隸詹事府。

translations.literal: In Xiantian 1 offices were opened; one director and one aide were established, subordinate to the Grand Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantian 1 separate offices were opened with one director and one aide each, subordinate to the Grand Steward of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋廢。

translations.literal: Soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 太子賓客四人，正三品。

translations.literal: Crown Prince's Guests of Honor — four, upper third rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Guests of Honor to the Crown Prince, of upper third rank.

sentences.zh: 掌侍從規諫，贊相禮儀，宴會則上齒。

translations.literal: They managed attendance and service, remonstrance, assisting ceremonial propriety; at banquets they took senior seats.
translations.idiomatic: They attended the crown prince in service, offered remonstrance, and assisted in ceremonial propriety; at banquets they took seats of honor.

sentences.zh: 侍讀，無常員，掌講導經學。

translations.literal: Reading Instructors — no fixed quota; they managed lecturing on and guiding the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Instructors had no fixed establishment; they lectured on the classics and guided the crown prince in their study.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十八年，以宰相兼賓客。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan 18, chancellors also served concurrently as Guests of Honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Zhenguan, chancellors were also appointed to serve concurrently as Guests of Honor.

sentences.zh: 開元中，定員四人。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan, the quota was fixed at four.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era the establishment was fixed at four posts.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，晉王府有侍讀，及爲太子，亦置焉。

translations.literal: In Taizong's time there were Reading Instructors in the Prince of Jin's household; when he became crown prince, the office was also established there.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, Reading Instructors served in the Prince of Jin's household; when he became crown prince, the post was retained in the Eastern Palace as well.

sentences.zh: 其後，或置或否。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was sometimes established and sometimes not.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the office was sometimes filled and sometimes left vacant.

sentences.zh: 開元初，十王宅引辭學工書者入教，亦爲侍讀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, the Ten Princes' Residence brought in scholars of letters skilled in calligraphy to teach — they also served as Reading Instructors.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaiyuan, the Ten Princes' Residence recruited literary scholars skilled in calligraphy to instruct the princes; they too held the title of Reading Instructor.

sentences.zh: 詹事府太子詹事一人，正三品；

translations.literal: Grand Steward's Office: one Grand Steward of the Crown Prince, upper third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Steward's Office had one Grand Steward of the Crown Prince, of upper third rank;

sentences.zh: 少詹事一人，正四品上。

translations.literal: one Vice Grand Steward, upper fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and one Vice Grand Steward, of upper fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌統三寺、十率府之政，少詹事爲之貳。

translations.literal: They managed and oversaw the administration of the three courts and ten command offices; the Vice Grand Steward served as second-in-command.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Steward directed the administration of the three courts and ten command offices, with the Vice Grand Steward as deputy.

sentences.zh: 皇太子書稱令，庶子以下署名奉行，書案、畫日。

translations.literal: When the crown prince issued documents they were called "orders"; from the Junior Tutors downward officials signed to execute, recorded the case file, and dated it.
translations.idiomatic: Documents issued by the crown prince were styled "orders"; from the Junior Tutors down, officials signed to carry them out, filed the record, and marked the date.

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正六品上。

translations.literal: Aides — two, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two aides of upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌判府事，知文武官簿、假使。

translations.literal: They adjudicated office affairs and managed the ledgers of civil and military officials and temporary assignments.
translations.idiomatic: They decided routine business of the office and kept the registers of civil and military personnel and temporary appointments.

sentences.zh: 凡敕令及尙書省、二坊符牒下東宮諸司者，皆發焉。

translations.literal: All edicts and orders, and documents from the Department of State Affairs and the two palace lodges dispatched to Eastern Palace offices, were issued from here.
translations.idiomatic: Every imperial edict and order, and every dispatch from the Department of State Affairs or the two palace lodges to Eastern Palace offices, was routed through this office.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，從七品上；

translations.literal: Chief clerk — one, upper seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: There was one chief clerk of upper seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 録事二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Recording Secretaries — two, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two Recording Secretaries of lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 隋廢詹事府。

translations.literal: The Sui abolished the Grand Steward's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui the Grand Steward's Office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 武德初復置。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored at the beginning of the Wude era.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年曰端尹府，詹事曰端尹，少詹事曰少尹。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 it was called the Endpoint Chief's Office; the Grand Steward was called Endpoint Chief, the Vice Grand Steward Junior Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the office was renamed the Endpoint Chief's Office; the Grand Steward became the Endpoint Chief and the Vice Grand Steward the Junior Chief.

sentences.zh: 武后光宅元年改曰宮尹府，詹事曰宮尹，少詹事曰少尹。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's first year of Guangzhai it was renamed the Palace Chief's Office; the Grand Steward was called Palace Chief, the Vice Grand Steward Junior Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangzhai under Empress Wu it was renamed the Palace Chief's Office; the Grand Steward was styled Palace Chief and the Vice Grand Steward Junior Chief.

sentences.zh: 有令史九人，書令史十八人。

translations.literal: There were nine clerks and eighteen scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included nine clerks and eighteen scribes.

sentences.zh: 司直二人，正七品上。

translations.literal: Rectifiers — two, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Rectifiers of upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌糾劾宮寮及率府之兵。

translations.literal: They investigated and impeached palace staff and the troops of the command offices.
translations.idiomatic: They investigated and censured palace officials and the soldiers of the command offices.

sentences.zh: 皇太子朝，則分知東西班。

translations.literal: When the crown prince attended court, they divided supervision between the eastern and western ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince attended court, they split oversight between the eastern and western formations.

sentences.zh: 監國，則詹事、庶子爲三司使，司直一人與司議郎、舍人分日受理啓狀。

translations.literal: When the crown prince governed the realm, the Grand Steward and Junior Tutors served as commissioners of the Three Offices; one Rectifier together with Petition Examiners and Attendants received petitions on alternating days.
translations.idiomatic: During a regency the Grand Steward and Junior Tutors acted as commissioners of the Three Offices; one Rectifier, together with Petition Examiners and Attendants, took petitions on rotation.

sentences.zh: 太子出，則分察鹵簿之内。

translations.literal: When the crown prince went abroad, they divided inspection within the ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince went out, they divided inspection duties within the ceremonial escort.

sentences.zh: 有令史一人，書令史二人，亭長四人，掌固六人。

translations.literal: There was one clerk, two scribes, four station chiefs, and six gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one clerk, two scribes, four station chiefs, and six gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 左春坊左庶子二人，正四品上；

translations.literal: Left Spring Palace: two Left Junior Tutors, upper fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Spring Palace had two Left Junior Tutors of upper fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 中允二人，正五品下。

translations.literal: Palace Attendants — two, lower fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two Palace Attendants of lower fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌侍從贊相，駮正啓奏。

translations.literal: They managed attendance and ceremonial assistance, and corrected petitions.
translations.idiomatic: They attended the crown prince, assisted in ceremony, and reviewed petitions for errors.

sentences.zh: 總司經、典膳、藥藏、内直、典設、宮門六局。

translations.literal: They had overall charge of the six bureaus: Classics, Palace Provisions, Pharmacy, Inner Household, Equipment, and Palace Gates.
