translations.idiomatic: They oversaw the six bureaus — the Classics Bureau, Palace Provisions Bureau, Pharmacy Bureau, Inner Household Bureau, Equipment Bureau, and Palace Gate Bureau.

sentences.zh: 皇太子出，則版奏外辦、中嚴；

translations.literal: When the crown prince went out, they announced with the tablet board, made outer preparations, and imposed inner strictness;
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince departed, they made the tablet announcement, completed the outer preparations, and enforced inner security;

sentences.zh: 入則解嚴。

translations.literal: on entering, strictness was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: on his return, security was relaxed.

sentences.zh: 凡令書下，則與中允、司議郎等畫諾、覆審，留所畫以爲案，更寫印署，注令諾，送詹事府。

translations.literal: Whenever an order document was issued, they together with Palace Attendants, Petition Examiners, and others affixed approval marks, re-examined it, retained the marked copy as the case file, copied and sealed it again, noted approval of the order, and forwarded it to the Grand Steward's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an order was issued, they joined Palace Attendants, Petition Examiners, and others in affixing approval, conducting a final review, keeping the marked copy on file, making a fresh copy with seals, noting assent to the order, and forwarding it to the Grand Steward's Office.

sentences.zh: 司議郎二人，正六品上。

translations.literal: Petition Examiners — two, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Petition Examiners of upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌侍從規諫，駮正啓奏。

translations.literal: They managed attendance, remonstrance, and correction of petitions.
translations.idiomatic: They attended the crown prince, offered remonstrance, and corrected petitions.

sentences.zh: 凡皇太子出入、朝謁、從祀、釋奠、講學、監國之命，可傳於史冊者，録爲記注；

translations.literal: All matters of the crown prince's coming and going, court audiences, accompanying sacrifice, libation offerings, lectures, and regency that could be recorded in the historical chronicle were entered as annalistic notes;
translations.idiomatic: Events worthy of the historical record — the crown prince's movements, court audiences, accompanying sacrifices, libation rites, lectures, and regency orders — were entered as annalistic notes;

sentences.zh: 宮坊祥眚，官長除拜、薨卒，歳終則録送史舘。

translations.literal: Auspicious and inauspicious events in the palace lodges, appointments and dismissals of chief officials, and deaths — at year's end these were copied and sent to the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: together with omens and portents in the palace lodges, appointments and dismissals of senior officials, and deaths, all of which were copied at year's end and sent to the History Office.

sentences.zh: 左諭德一人，正四品下。

translations.literal: Left Mentor of Virtue — one, lower fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Left Mentor of Virtue of lower fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌諭皇太子以道德，隨事諷贊。

translations.literal: They admonished the crown prince in virtue and morality, offering counsel and praise on each occasion.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed the crown prince in moral conduct, offering counsel and encouragement as occasions arose.

sentences.zh: 皇太子朝宮臣，則列侍左階，出入騎從。

translations.literal: When the crown prince attended court with palace officials, they stood in attendance on the left steps and rode in his escort when he went in and out.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince received palace officials in audience, they stood in attendance on the left stairway and rode in escort when he went abroad.

sentences.zh: 左贊善大夫五人，正五品上。

translations.literal: Left Commissioners of Good Conduct — five, upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were five Left Commissioners of Good Conduct of upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌傳令，諷過失，贊禮儀，以經教授諸郡王。

translations.literal: They transmitted orders, counseled against faults, assisted in ceremonial propriety, and taught the classics to the various imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: They relayed orders, admonished against misconduct, assisted in ritual propriety, and taught the classics to the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 録事二人，從八品下；

translations.literal: Recording Secretaries — two, lower eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: There were two Recording Secretaries of lower eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 主事三人，從九品下。

translations.literal: case officers — three, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and three case officers of lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 隋有内允。

translations.literal: The Sui had Inner Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui dynasty had the post of Inner Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武德三年改曰中舍人，隸門下坊。

translations.literal: In Wude 3 the title was changed to Palace Secretaries, subordinate to the Gate-Down Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3 the title was changed to Palace Secretary and the office was placed under the Gate-Down Lodge.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初曰中允，十八年置司議郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan they were called Palace Attendants; in year 18 Petition Examiners were established.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenguan the title became Palace Attendant; in the eighteenth year Petition Examiners were added.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，避皇太子名，復改中允曰内允。

translations.literal: In Yonghui 3, to avoid the crown prince's personal name, the title Palace Attendant was again changed to Inner Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 3, to avoid the crown prince's personal name, Palace Attendants were again renamed Inner Attendants.

sentences.zh: 太子廢，復舊。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, the former titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed, the earlier titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改門下坊曰左春坊，左庶子曰左中護，中允曰左贊善大夫，司議郎分左右，置左右諭德各一人。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 the Gate-Down Lodge was renamed the Left Spring Palace; Left Junior Tutors became Left Central Protectors; Palace Attendants became Left Commissioners of Good Conduct; Petition Examiners were divided into left and right; one Left and one Right Mentor of Virtue were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the Gate-Down Lodge became the Left Spring Palace; Left Junior Tutors were renamed Left Central Protectors, Palace Attendants became Left Commissioners of Good Conduct, Petition Examiners were split into left and right sections, and one Left and one Right Mentor of Virtue were appointed.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，皆復舊，司議郎不分左右，其後諭德廢而司議郎復分。

translations.literal: In Xianheng 1 all titles were restored; Petition Examiners were no longer divided left and right; thereafter the Mentors of Virtue were abolished and Petition Examiners were again divided.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng 1 the old titles were all restored and Petition Examiners were no longer divided; later the Mentors of Virtue were abolished and the left-right division of Petition Examiners was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳四年，置左右贊善大夫各十人，以同姓爲之。

translations.literal: In Yifeng 4 ten Left and ten Right Commissioners of Good Conduct were established, filled by men of the imperial surname.
translations.idiomatic: In Yifeng 4 ten Left and ten Right Commissioners of Good Conduct were appointed, all drawn from the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，始兼用庶姓，改門下坊曰左春坊，復置諭德，庶子以比侍中，中允以比門下侍郎，司議郎以比給事中，贊善大夫以比諫議大夫，諭德以比散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In Jingyun 2 commoners' surnames were first also used; the Gate-Down Lodge was renamed the Left Spring Palace; Mentors of Virtue were restored; Junior Tutors were ranked like Vice Grand Councilors; Palace Attendants like Vice Gate Ministers; Petition Examiners like Drafting Attendants; Commissioners of Good Conduct like Remonstrance Officers; Mentors of Virtue like Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 2 commoners were first admitted as well; the Gate-Down Lodge was renamed the Left Spring Palace and Mentors of Virtue restored; Junior Tutors were ranked equivalent to Vice Grand Councilors, Palace Attendants to Vice Gate Ministers, Petition Examiners to Drafting Attendants, Commissioners of Good Conduct to Remonstrance Officers, and Mentors of Virtue to Regular Attendants of the Loose Retinue.

sentences.zh: 右坊，則庶子以比中書令，中舍人以比中書侍郎，太子監國則庶子比尙書令。

translations.literal: In the Right Lodge, Junior Tutors were ranked like Grand Councilors of the Secretariat; Palace Secretaries like Vice Secretaries; when the crown prince governed the realm, Junior Tutors were ranked like the Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Right Lodge, Junior Tutors were ranked equivalent to Grand Councilors of the Secretariat and Palace Secretaries to Vice Secretaries; during a regency Junior Tutors were ranked equivalent to the Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 有令史六人，書令史十二人，傳令四人，掌儀二人，贊者三人，亭長三人，掌固十人。

translations.literal: There were six clerks, twelve scribes, four order transmitters, two ceremonial attendants, three announcers, three station chiefs, and ten gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included six clerks, twelve scribes, four order transmitters, two ceremonial attendants, three announcers, three station chiefs, and ten gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 崇文舘學士二人，掌經籍圖書，教授諸生，課試舉送如弘文舘。

translations.literal: Academicians of the Palace of Exalted Literature — two; they managed classics and books, instructed students, and conducted examinations and recommendations like the Hall of Promoted Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Two Academicians of the Palace of Exalted Literature managed the classics and library collections, instructed students, and conducted examinations and recommendations on the model of the Hall of Promoted Literature.

sentences.zh: 校書郎二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Collators — two, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Collators of lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌校理書籍。

translations.literal: They managed collating and organizing books.
translations.idiomatic: They collated and organized the book collections.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十三年置崇賢舘。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan 13 the Palace of Exalted Worthies was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace of Exalted Worthies was founded in the thirteenth year of Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，置學生二十人。

translations.literal: In Xianqing 1 twenty students were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 1 an enrollment of twenty students was fixed.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，避太子名，改曰崇文舘。

translations.literal: In Shangyuan 2, to avoid the crown prince's personal name, the name was changed to Palace of Exalted Literature.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 2, to avoid the crown prince's personal name, it was renamed the Palace of Exalted Literature.

sentences.zh: 有學士、直學士及讎校，皆無常員，無其人則庶子領舘事。

translations.literal: There were academicians, resident academicians, and collators — all without fixed quota; when none were appointed, the Junior Tutor oversaw the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians, resident academicians, and collators had no fixed establishment; when none were in post, a Junior Tutor supervised the palace.

sentences.zh: 開元七年，改讎校曰校書郎。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 7 collators were renamed Collators.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 7 the title of collator was changed to Collator.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，以宰相爲學士，總舘事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan chancellors served as academicians and oversaw the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qianyuan chancellors were appointed academicians and put in charge of the palace.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年，隸左春坊。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan 8 it was made subordinate to the Left Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 8 it was placed under the Left Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 有舘生十五人，書直一人，令史二人，書令史二人，典書二人，搨書手二人，楷書手十人，熟紙匠一人，裝潢匠二人，筆匠一人。

translations.literal: There were fifteen hall students, one document attendant, two clerks, two scribes, two book custodians, two rubbing copyists, ten regular-script copyists, one paper-preparation craftsman, two binding craftsmen, and one brush craftsman.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included fifteen hall students, one document attendant, two clerks, two scribes, two book custodians, two rubbing copyists, ten regular-script copyists, one paper-preparation craftsman, two binding craftsmen, and one brush craftsman.

sentences.zh: 司經局洗馬二人，從五品下。

translations.literal: Classics Bureau: two Groom Commissioners, lower fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Classics Bureau had two Groom Commissioners of lower fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌經籍，出入侍從。

translations.literal: They managed the classics and attended the crown prince in going in and out.
translations.idiomatic: They kept the classics and attended the crown prince whenever he went abroad.

sentences.zh: 圖書上東宮者，皆受而藏之。

translations.literal: All books and documents sent to the Eastern Palace were received and stored.
translations.idiomatic: Every book and document dispatched to the Eastern Palace was received and placed in storage.

sentences.zh: 文學三人，正六品下。

translations.literal: Literary Officers — three, lower sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were three Literary Officers of lower sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 分知經籍，侍奉文章。

translations.literal: They divided supervision of the classics and attended to literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: They shared oversight of the classics and assisted with literary composition.

sentences.zh: 校書四人，正九品下；

translations.literal: Collators — four, lower ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: There were four Collators of lower ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 正字二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Standardizers — two, upper ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two Standardizers of upper ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌校刊經史。

translations.literal: They managed collating and editing the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: They collated and edited the classics and historical texts.

sentences.zh: 唐改太子正書曰正字。

translations.literal: The Tang changed the crown prince's Correctors of Writing to Standardizers.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang the crown prince's Correctors of Writing were renamed Standardizers.

sentences.zh: 龍朔三年，改司經局曰桂坊，罷隸左春坊，領崇賢舘，比御史臺；

translations.literal: In Longshuo 3 the Classics Bureau was renamed the Laurel Lodge, ceased being subordinate to the Left Spring Palace, oversaw the Palace of Exalted Worthies, and was ranked like the Censorate;
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 3 the Classics Bureau became the Laurel Lodge, was detached from the Left Spring Palace, took charge of the Palace of Exalted Worthies, and was ranked on a par with the Censorate;

sentences.zh: 以詹事一人爲令，比御史大夫，司直二人比侍御史，以洗馬爲司經大夫。

translations.literal: one Grand Steward served as director, ranked like the Censor-in-Chief; two Rectifiers were ranked like Attending Censors; the Groom Commissioner became Director of the Classics Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: one Grand Steward served as director with rank equivalent to the Censor-in-Chief; two Rectifiers were ranked like Attending Censors; and the Groom Commissioner became Director of the Classics Bureau.

sentences.zh: 置文學四人，録事一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Four Literary Officers and one Recording Secretary, lower ninth rank, were established.
translations.idiomatic: Four Literary Officers and one Recording Secretary of lower ninth rank were added.

sentences.zh: 三年，改司經大夫曰桂坊大夫，糾正違失。

translations.literal: In the third year the Director of the Classics Bureau was renamed Laurel Lodge Director, correcting violations and errors.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Director of the Classics Bureau was renamed Laurel Lodge Director, with authority to correct misconduct and errors.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，復隸左春坊，省録事。

translations.literal: In Xianheng 1 it was again subordinate to the Left Spring Palace and the Recording Secretary was eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng 1 it was again placed under the Left Spring Palace and the Recording Secretary post was abolished.

sentences.zh: 有書令史二人，書吏二人，典書四人，楷書二十五人，掌固六人，裝潢匠二人，熟紙匠、筆匠各一人。

translations.literal: There were two scribes, two document clerks, four book custodians, twenty-five regular-script copyists, six gate wardens, two binding craftsmen, and one paper-preparation craftsman and one brush craftsman each.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included two scribes, two document clerks, four book custodians, twenty-five regular-script copyists, six gate wardens, two binding craftsmen, and one paper-preparation craftsman and one brush craftsman.

sentences.zh: 典膳局典膳郎二人，從六品下；

translations.literal: Palace Provisions Bureau: two Provisions Officers, lower sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Provisions Bureau had two Provisions Officers of lower sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正八品上。

translations.literal: aides — two, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two aides of upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌進膳、嘗食，丞爲之貳。

translations.literal: They managed presenting meals and tasting food; the aides served as second-in-command.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised the presentation of meals and the tasting of food, with aides as deputies.

sentences.zh: 毎夕，更直於廚。

translations.literal: Each evening they rotated night duty in the kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Each night they took turns standing watch in the kitchen.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改典膳監曰典膳郎。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 Supervisors of Provisions were renamed Provisions Officers.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the title of Provisions Supervisor was changed to Provisions Officer.

sentences.zh: 有書令史二人，書吏四人，主食六人，典食二百人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were two scribes, four document clerks, six chief food attendants, two hundred food attendants, and four gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included two scribes, four document clerks, six chief food attendants, two hundred food attendants, and four gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 藥藏局藥藏郎二人，從六品下；

translations.literal: Pharmacy Bureau: two Pharmacy Officers, lower sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Pharmacy Bureau had two Pharmacy Officers of lower sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正八品上。

translations.literal: aides — two, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two aides of upper eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌和醫藥，丞爲之貳。

translations.literal: They managed compounding medicines; the aides served as second-in-command.
translations.idiomatic: They compounded medicines, with aides as deputies.

sentences.zh: 皇太子有疾，侍醫診候議方。

translations.literal: When the crown prince fell ill, attendant physicians examined him and deliberated prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was ill, attendant physicians examined him and drafted prescriptions.

sentences.zh: 藥將進，宮臣涖嘗，如尙藥局之職。

translations.literal: When medicines were about to be administered, palace officials attended to taste them, as in the duties of the Palace Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: Before any medicine was given, palace officials tasted it on the spot, following the practice of the Palace Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 有書令史一人，書吏二人，侍醫四人，典藥二人，藥童六人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There was one scribe, two document clerks, four attendant physicians, two pharmacy attendants, six pharmacy boys, and four gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one scribe, two document clerks, four attendant physicians, two pharmacy attendants, six pharmacy boys, and four gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 内直局内直郎二人，從六品下；

translations.literal: Inner Household Bureau: two Inner Household Officers, lower sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Household Bureau had two Inner Household Officers of lower sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正八品下。

translations.literal: aides — two, lower eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two aides of lower eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌符璽、衣服、繖扇、几案、筆硯、垣牆。

translations.literal: They managed seals, clothing, parasols and fans, desks, writing implements, and walls.
translations.idiomatic: They kept charge of seals, garments, parasols and fans, desks, writing materials, and palace walls.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改監曰内直郎，副監曰丞。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 the title Supervisor was changed to Inner Household Officer and Deputy Supervisor to aide.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 Supervisors were renamed Inner Household Officers and Deputy Supervisors became aides.

sentences.zh: 有令史一人，書吏三人，典服十二人，典扇八人，典翰八人，掌固六人。

translations.literal: There was one clerk, three document clerks, twelve robe custodians, eight fan custodians, eight writing-material custodians, and six gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one clerk, three document clerks, twelve robe custodians, eight fan custodians, eight writing-material custodians, and six gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 武德中，有典璽四人，開元中廢。

translations.literal: During Wude there were four Seal Custodians; in Kaiyuan they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era there were four Seal Custodians; they were abolished during Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 典設局典設郎四人，從六品下；

translations.literal: Equipment Bureau: four Equipment Officers, lower sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Equipment Bureau had four Equipment Officers of lower sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正八品下。

translations.literal: aides — two, lower eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two aides of lower eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌湯沐、燈燭、汛掃、鋪設。

translations.literal: They managed bathing, lamp candles, washing and sweeping, and laying out furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised bathing arrangements, lamps and candles, cleaning, and the setting out of furnishings.

sentences.zh: 凡皇太子散齋別殿、致齋正殿，前一日設幄坐于東序及室内，張帷前楹。

translations.literal: Whenever the crown prince performed preliminary fasting in a side hall or formal fasting in the main hall, the day before they set up curtain seats on the eastern side and within the chamber, hanging curtains before the front pillars.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince undertook preliminary fasting in a side hall or formal fasting in the main hall, they prepared curtained seats on the east side and within the inner chamber the day before, hanging drapery before the front pillars.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改齋帥局曰典設局，齋帥曰郎。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 the Fasting Supervisors Bureau was renamed the Equipment Bureau and Fasting Supervisors were called Officers.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the Fasting Supervisors Bureau became the Equipment Bureau, and its supervisors were retitled Equipment Officers.

sentences.zh: 有書令史二人，書吏四人，幕士二百四十五人，掌固十二人。

translations.literal: There were two scribes, four document clerks, two hundred forty-five tent attendants, and twelve gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included two scribes, four document clerks, two hundred forty-five tent attendants, and twelve gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 宮門局宮門郎二人，從六品下；

translations.literal: Palace Gate Bureau: two Palace Gate Officers, lower sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Gate Bureau had two Palace Gate Officers of lower sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正八品下。

translations.literal: aides — two, lower eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two aides of lower eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌宮門管籥。

translations.literal: They managed palace gates and keys.
translations.idiomatic: They controlled palace gates and keys.

sentences.zh: 凡夜漏盡，撃漏鼓而開；

translations.literal: When the night clepsydra ran out, they struck the clepsydra drum to open;
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the night watch they sounded the clepsydra drum to open the gates;

sentences.zh: 夜漏上水一刻，撃漏鼓而閉。

translations.literal: one quarter after the night clepsydra began filling, they struck the clepsydra drum to close.
translations.idiomatic: one quarter after the night clepsydra was reset, they sounded it again to close them.

sentences.zh: 歳終行儺，則先一刻而啓。

translations.literal: At year's end when the exorcism rite was performed, they opened one quarter early.
translations.idiomatic: At the year-end exorcism rite the gates opened a quarter watch early.

sentences.zh: 皇太子不在，則闔正門；

translations.literal: When the crown prince was absent, they closed the main gate;
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was away, they shut the main gate;

sentences.zh: 還仗，如常。

translations.literal: upon his return with his guard, as usual.
translations.idiomatic: upon his return with his escort, normal procedures resumed.

sentences.zh: 凡宮中，明時不鼓。

translations.literal: Within the palace, during daylight no drum was struck.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace grounds no clepsydra drum was sounded during daylight hours.

sentences.zh: 龍朔三年，改宮門監曰宮門郎。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 3 the title Gate Supervisor was changed to Palace Gate Officer.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 3 Gate Supervisors were renamed Palace Gate Officers.

sentences.zh: 有書令史一人，書吏二人，門僕百人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There was one scribe, two document clerks, one hundred gate servants, and four gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one scribe, two document clerks, one hundred gate servants, and four gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 右春坊右庶子二人，正四品下；

translations.literal: Right Spring Palace: two Right Junior Tutors, lower fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Right Spring Palace had two Right Junior Tutors of lower fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 中舍人二人，正五品下。

translations.literal: two Palace Secretaries, lower fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two Palace Secretaries of lower fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌侍從、獻納、啓奏，中舍人爲之貳。

translations.literal: They managed attendance in service, memorial submission, and petitions; Palace Secretaries served as second-in-command.
translations.idiomatic: They handled personal attendance, the submission of memorials, and petitions, with Palace Secretaries as deputies.

sentences.zh: 皇太子監國，下令書則畫日，至春坊則庶子宣傳，中舍人奉行。

translations.literal: When the crown prince governed the realm, upon issuing order documents the date was marked; upon reaching the Spring Palace Junior Tutors proclaimed and transmitted them, and Palace Secretaries executed them.
translations.idiomatic: During a regency, order documents bore the date when issued; at the Spring Palace Junior Tutors proclaimed and relayed them, and Palace Secretaries carried them out.

sentences.zh: 太子舍人四人，正六品上。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Attendants — four, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Crown Prince Attendants of upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌行令書、表啓。

translations.literal: They managed issuing order documents, memorials, and petitions.
translations.idiomatic: They drafted and transmitted order documents, memorials, and petitions.

sentences.zh: 諸臣上皇太子，大事以牋，小事以啓，其封題皆上右春坊通事舍人以進。

translations.literal: When all officials addressed the crown prince, major matters used formal letters, minor matters petitions; the sealed superscriptions all went up to the Right Spring Palace Communications Attendants to be forwarded.
translations.idiomatic: When officials addressed the crown prince, major matters were submitted as formal letters and minor ones as petitions; all sealed submissions were routed through the Communications Attendants of the Right Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人八人，正七品下。

translations.literal: Communications Attendants — eight, lower seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were eight Communications Attendants of lower seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌導宮臣辭見，承令勞問。

translations.literal: They managed guiding palace officials at farewell audiences, and receiving orders to offer condolences or inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: They escorted palace officials at farewell audiences and, on order, conveyed the crown prince's condolences and inquiries.

sentences.zh: 右諭德一人，右贊善大夫五人，録事一人，主事二人，品皆如左春坊。

translations.literal: one Right Mentor of Virtue, five Right Commissioners of Good Conduct, one Recording Secretary, two case officers — all ranks as in the Left Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Right Mentor of Virtue, five Right Commissioners of Good Conduct, one Recording Secretary, and two case officers — all of the same ranks as their counterparts in the Left Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 隋内舍人隸典書坊。

translations.literal: Under the Sui, Inner Attendants were subordinate to the Classics Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, Inner Attendants served under the Classics Lodge.

sentences.zh: 武德初改曰中舍人，管記舍人曰太子舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude the title was changed to Palace Secretary; Attendants who managed records were called Crown Prince Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wude the title became Palace Secretary, and record-keeping attendants were renamed Crown Prince Attendants.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，避太子名，復改中舍人曰内舍人。

translations.literal: In Yonghui 1, to avoid the crown prince's personal name, Palace Secretaries were again changed to Inner Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 1, to avoid the crown prince's personal name, Palace Secretaries were again renamed Inner Attendants.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改典書坊曰右春坊，右庶子曰右中護，中舍人曰右贊善大夫，舍人曰右司議郎。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 the Classics Lodge was renamed the Right Spring Palace; Right Junior Tutors became Right Central Protectors; Palace Secretaries became Right Commissioners of Good Conduct; Attendants became Right Petition Examiners.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the Classics Lodge became the Right Spring Palace; Right Junior Tutors were renamed Right Central Protectors, Palace Secretaries became Right Commissioners of Good Conduct, and Attendants became Right Petition Examiners.

sentences.zh: 有令史九人，書令史十八人，傳令四人，典謁四人，亭長六人，掌固十人。

translations.literal: There were nine clerks, eighteen scribes, four order transmitters, four reception attendants, six station chiefs, and ten gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included nine clerks, eighteen scribes, four order transmitters, four reception attendants, six station chiefs, and ten gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 家令寺家令一人，從四品上。

translations.literal: Household Steward's Office: one Household Steward, upper secondary fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Household Steward's Office had one Household Steward of upper secondary fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌飲膳、倉儲。

translations.literal: They managed drinks and food, and granary storage.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw food and drink and managed the granaries.

sentences.zh: 總食官、典倉、司藏三署。

translations.literal: They had overall charge of the three offices: Food Officials, Granary, and Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the three subordinate offices — the Food Officials Bureau, the Granary Bureau, and the Treasury Bureau.

sentences.zh: 皇太子出入，則乘軺車爲導；

translations.literal: When the crown prince went in and out, he rode in a light carriage as guide;
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince went abroad, the Household Steward rode ahead in a light carriage as guide;

sentences.zh: 祭祀、賓客，則供酒食；

translations.literal: at sacrifices and when receiving guests, they supplied wine and food;
translations.idiomatic: at sacrifices and for guests he provided food and wine;

sentences.zh: 賜予，則奉金玉、貨幣。

translations.literal: for gifts and grants, they presented gold, jade, and currency.
translations.idiomatic: for bestowals he presented gold, jade, and currency.

sentences.zh: 凡牀几、茵席、器物，非取於將作、少府者，皆供焉。

translations.literal: All beds, tables, mats, and utensils not sourced from the Directorate of Imperial Construction or the Palace Ateliers were supplied by them.
translations.idiomatic: All beds, tables, mats, and utensils not drawn from the Directorate of Imperial Construction or the Palace Ateliers were furnished by this office.

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從七品下，掌判寺事。

translations.literal: Aides — two, lower secondary seventh rank; they managed and adjudicated office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Two aides of lower secondary seventh rank assisted in adjudicating the office's affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡三署出納，皆刺於詹事。

translations.literal: All receipts and disbursements of the three offices were reported to the Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: All receipts and disbursements of the three subordinate offices were reported to the Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 莊宅、田園，審肥塉爲收斂之數。

translations.literal: For estates and gardens they assessed fertile and barren land to determine yield quotas.
translations.idiomatic: For estates and gardens they assessed the fertility of the soil to set collection quotas.

sentences.zh: 宮、朝、坊、府土木營繕，則下於司藏。

translations.literal: Palace, court, lodge, and office construction and repairs were assigned to the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Construction and repairs for the palace, court, lodges, and offices were assigned to the Treasury Bureau.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk — one, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one chief clerk of lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 唐改司府令曰家令。

translations.literal: In Tang the Steward of the Palace Office was renamed Household Steward.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang renamed the Steward of the Palace Office to Household Steward.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改家令寺曰宮府寺，家令曰大夫。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 the Household Steward's Office was renamed the Palace Household Office and the Household Steward was called Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the Household Steward's Office became the Palace Household Office, and the Household Steward was styled Director.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府十人，史二十人，亭長四人，掌固四人，雜匠百人。

translations.literal: There was one recording secretary, ten office attendants, twenty clerks, four station chiefs, four gate wardens, and one hundred miscellaneous artisans.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one recording secretary, ten office attendants, twenty clerks, four station chiefs, four gate wardens, and one hundred miscellaneous artisans.

sentences.zh: 食官署令一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: Food Officials Office: one director, lower secondary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Food Officials Bureau had one director of lower secondary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: aides — two, lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two aides of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌飲膳、酒醴。

translations.literal: They managed drinks, food, and fermented beverages.
translations.idiomatic: They managed food, drink, and fermented beverages.

sentences.zh: 凡四時供送設食皆顓焉。

translations.literal: All seasonal provision and serving of meals was their sole charge.
translations.idiomatic: They had exclusive charge of seasonal provisions and the service of meals.

sentences.zh: 供六品以下元日、寒食、冬至食於家令廚者。

translations.literal: They supplied New Year's Day, Cold Food Festival, and Winter Solstice meals from the Household Steward's kitchen for officials of sixth rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: They provided New Year's, Cold Food Festival, and Winter Solstice meals from the Household Steward's kitchen for officials of sixth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 有府二人，史四人，掌膳四人，供膳百四十人，奉觶三十人。

translations.literal: There were two office attendants, four clerks, four food superintendents, one hundred forty food servers, and thirty cup-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included two office attendants, four clerks, four food superintendents, one hundred forty food servers, and thirty cup-bearers.

sentences.zh: 典倉署令一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: Granary Office: one director, lower secondary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Bureau had one director of lower secondary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: aides — two, lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two aides of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌九穀、䤈醢、庶羞、器皿、燈燭。

translations.literal: They managed the nine grains, fermented sauces and pickles, various delicacies, utensils, and lamp candles.
translations.idiomatic: They managed grain stores, fermented sauces and pickles, various delicacies, utensils, and lamps and candles.

sentences.zh: 凡園圃樹藝，皆受令焉。

translations.literal: All garden and orchard cultivation received orders from them.
translations.idiomatic: All garden and orchard cultivation came under their direction.

sentences.zh: 毎月籍出納上於寺，歳終上詹事府。

translations.literal: Each month they registered receipts and disbursements and reported to the office; at year's end they reported to the Grand Steward's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Each month they recorded receipts and disbursements and reported to the Household Steward's Office; at year's end they forwarded accounts to the Grand Steward's Office.

sentences.zh: 給戸奴婢、番戸、雜戸資糧衣服。

translations.literal: They supplied grain rations and clothing to registered households, tributary households, and miscellaneous households of slaves and servants.
translations.idiomatic: They issued rations and clothing to registered household slaves and servants, tributary households, and miscellaneous service households.

sentences.zh: 有府三人，史五人，園丞二人，史二人。

translations.literal: There were three office attendants, five clerks, two garden aides, and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included three office attendants, five clerks, two garden aides, and two additional clerks.

sentences.zh: 司藏署令一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: Treasury Office: one director, lower secondary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Treasury Bureau had one director of lower secondary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: aides — two, lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two aides of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌庫藏財貨出納、營繕。

translations.literal: They managed treasury stores, the receipt and disbursement of goods and wealth, and construction and repairs.
translations.idiomatic: They managed storehouses, the receipt and disbursement of goods and funds, and construction and repairs.

sentences.zh: 有府三人，史四人，計史一人。

translations.literal: There were three office attendants, four clerks, and one accounting clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included three office attendants, four clerks, and one accounting clerk.

sentences.zh: 率更寺令一人，從四品上。

translations.literal: Court of Palace Regulators: one director, upper secondary fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Palace Regulators had one director of upper secondary fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌宗族次序、禮樂、刑罰及漏刻之政。

translations.literal: They managed clan precedence, rites and music, punishments, and clepsydra policy.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw clan precedence, rites and music, punishments, and the regulation of the clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 太子釋奠、講學、齒冑，則總其儀；

translations.literal: When the crown prince performed the sacrificial offering, lectured, or donned armor by rank, they had overall charge of the ceremony;
translations.idiomatic: For the crown prince's sacrificial offerings, lectures, and rank-order investitures with armor, he directed the ceremonial arrangements;

sentences.zh: 出入，乘軺車爲導，居家令之次。

translations.literal: going in and out, he rode in a light carriage as guide, ranking next after the Household Steward.
translations.idiomatic: when the crown prince went abroad he rode ahead in a light carriage as guide, ranking immediately below the Household Steward.

sentences.zh: 坊、寺、府有罪者，論罰，庶人杖以下，皆送大理。

translations.literal: For offenders in lodges, courts, and offices who were sentenced, commoners receiving beating with the rod or lesser punishments were all sent to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders in the lodges, courts, and offices who were sentenced — commoners receiving beating with the rod or lesser punishments — were all remitted to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 皇太子未立，判斷於大理。

translations.literal: When no crown prince had been installed, judgment was referred to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When no crown prince had been appointed, cases were adjudicated by the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 丞一人，從七品上。

translations.literal: Aide — one, upper secondary seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one aide of upper secondary seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌貳令事。

translations.literal: They served as second-in-command to the director.
translations.idiomatic: He served as the director's deputy.

sentences.zh: 宮臣有犯理於率更者，躬問蔽罪而上於詹事。

translations.literal: When palace officials had offenses adjudicated by the Court of Palace Regulators, the director personally inquired, concealed the sentence, and reported upward to the Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: When palace officials were tried by the Court of Palace Regulators, the director personally heard the case, withheld the sentence, and reported to the Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk — one, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one chief clerk of lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌印句。

translations.literal: They managed seals and case annotations.
translations.idiomatic: He managed seals and the annotation of case records.

sentences.zh: 凡宗族不序，禮儀不節，音律不諧，漏刻不審，刑名不法，皆舉而正之。

translations.literal: Whenever clan order was disordered, ritual propriety unrestrained, pitch and tone discordant, clepsydra inexact, or criminal nomenclature unlawful — all were reported and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Any disorder in clan precedence, lapse in ritual propriety, discord in pitch, inaccuracy in the clepsydra, or irregularity in criminal nomenclature was reported and set right.

sentences.zh: 決囚，則與丞同涖。

translations.literal: When prisoners were sentenced, he together with the aide jointly presided.
translations.idiomatic: When sentences were pronounced, the chief clerk joined the aide in presiding.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改曰司更寺，令曰司更大夫。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 it was renamed the Court of Time Regulation; the director was called Director of Time Regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 it was renamed the Court of Time Regulation, and the director was styled Director of Time Regulation.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府三人，史四人，漏刻博士三人，掌漏六人，漏童二十人，典鍾、典鼓各十二人，亭長四人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There was one recording secretary, three office attendants, four clerks, three clepsydra masters, six clepsydra keepers, twenty clepsydra boys, twelve bell custodians and twelve drum custodians each, four station chiefs, and four gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one recording secretary, three office attendants, four clerks, three clepsydra masters, six clepsydra keepers, twenty clepsydra boys, twelve bell custodians, twelve drum custodians, four station chiefs, and four gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 漏刻博士掌教漏刻。

translations.literal: Clepsydra masters managed instruction in clepsydra operation.
translations.idiomatic: Clepsydra masters trained staff in clepsydra operation.

sentences.zh: 僕寺僕一人，從四品上。

translations.literal: Transport Steward's Office: one Transport Steward, upper secondary fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Transport Steward's Office had one Transport Steward of upper secondary fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌車輿、乘騎、儀仗、喪葬，總廄牧署。

translations.literal: They managed carriages, riding mounts, ritual regalia, and funeral affairs, having overall charge of the Stable and Pasturage Office.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw carriages, riding mounts, ceremonial regalia, and funeral arrangements, and directed the Stable and Pasturage Bureau.

sentences.zh: 太子出，則率廄牧令進路，親馭。

translations.literal: When the crown prince went out, he led the Stable and Pasturage director to advance the route and personally drove.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince went abroad, the Transport Steward led the director of the Stable and Pasturage Bureau to clear the route and drove the carriage himself.

sentences.zh: 丞一人，從七品上。

translations.literal: Aide — one, upper secondary seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one aide of upper secondary seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌判寺事。

translations.literal: They managed and adjudicated office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted in adjudicating the office's affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡馬畜芻粟，歳以季夏上於詹事，以時出入而節其數。

translations.literal: All horses, livestock, and fodder — each year in the last month of summer were reported to the Grand Steward; disbursements were timed and their quantities regulated.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the fourth month of summer he reported horse, livestock, and fodder accounts to the Grand Steward, regulating timely disbursements and controlling quantities.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk — one, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one chief clerk of lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌廄牧畜養、車騎駕馭、儀仗。

translations.literal: They managed stable pasturage and livestock rearing, carriage and cavalry driving, and ritual regalia.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw stables and pasturage, carriage and cavalry teams, and ceremonial regalia.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改曰馭僕寺，僕曰大夫。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 it was renamed the Carriage Steward's Office; the Steward was called Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 it was renamed the Carriage Steward's Office, and the Transport Steward was styled Director.

sentences.zh: 有進馬十一人，録事一人，府三人，史五人，亭長三人，掌固三人。

translations.literal: There were eleven horse presenters, one recording secretary, three office attendants, five clerks, three station chiefs, and three gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included eleven horse presenters, one recording secretary, three office attendants, five clerks, three station chiefs, and three gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 廏牧署令一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: Stable and Pasturage Office: one director, lower secondary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Stable and Pasturage Bureau had one director of lower secondary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: aides — two, lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two aides of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌車馬、閑廏、牧畜。

translations.literal: They managed horses and carriages, reserved stables, and pastured livestock.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw horses and carriages, reserved stables, and the pasturing of livestock.

sentences.zh: 皇太子出，則率典乘先期習路馬，率駕士馭車乘，旣出，進路，式路車於西閤外，南向以俟。

translations.literal: When the crown prince went out, the director led Carriage Custodians to drill route horses beforehand, led drivers to manage carriages; once he had gone out and advanced the route, he positioned the route carriage outside the western gate wing, facing south to wait.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince went abroad, the director beforehand led Carriage Custodians to exercise the route horses and drivers to ready the carriages; once the crown prince had departed, he cleared the route and placed the route carriage outside the western gate wing, facing south in waiting.

sentences.zh: 凡羣牧隸東宮者，皆受其職事。

translations.literal: All herd pasturage subordinate to the Eastern Palace received orders and duties from them.
translations.idiomatic: All herd pasturage under the Eastern Palace fell under their authority.

sentences.zh: 典乘四人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Carriage Custodians — four, lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Carriage Custodians of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 有府三人，史六人，翼馭十人，駕士十五人，掌閑六百人，獸醫十人，主酪三十人。

translations.literal: There were three office attendants, six clerks, ten auxiliary drivers, fifteen drivers, six hundred stable keepers, ten veterinary physicians, and thirty dairy stewards.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included three office attendants, six clerks, ten auxiliary drivers, fifteen carriage drivers, six hundred stable keepers, ten veterinary physicians, and thirty dairy stewards.

sentences.zh: 翼馭掌調馬執馭。

translations.literal: Auxiliary drivers managed training horses and holding reins.
translations.idiomatic: Auxiliary drivers trained horses and managed the reins.

sentences.zh: 太子左右率府率各一人，正四品上；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Left and Right Command Offices: one Commander each, upper fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's Left and Right Command Offices each had one Commander of upper fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 副率各二人，從四品上。

translations.literal: Vice Commanders — two each, upper secondary fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two Vice Commanders each of upper secondary fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌兵仗、儀衞。

translations.literal: They managed weapons and ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: They managed arms and ceremonial guard duty.

sentences.zh: 凡諸曹及三府、外府皆隸焉。

translations.literal: All the various bureaus and the three offices and outer offices were subordinate thereto.
translations.idiomatic: Every bureau, the three guard offices, and the outer offices fell under the Guard Command Office.

sentences.zh: 元日、冬至，皇太子朝宮臣、諸方使，則率衞府之屬爲衞。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day and the Winter Solstice, when the crown prince held court with palace officials and envoys from the regions, he led the subordinates of the guard command offices as guard.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day and the Winter Solstice, when the Crown Prince received palace officials and regional envoys in audience, the Commanders led their guard-command subordinates as escort.

sentences.zh: 毎月三府三衞及五府超乘番上者，配以職。

translations.literal: Each month those on rotation from the three offices, three guards, and five offices who served as supernumerary carriage attendants were assigned duties.
translations.idiomatic: Each month men rotating to duty from the three offices, the Three Guards, and the five guard offices — including supernumerary carriage attendants — were assigned their posts.

sentences.zh: 武德五年，改左右侍率曰左右衞率府，左右武侍衞率曰左右宗衞率府，左右宮門將曰左右監門率府。

translations.literal: In Wude 5, Left and Right Attendant Commanders were renamed Left and Right Guard Command Offices; Left and Right Valiant Attendant Commanders to Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Command Offices; Left and Right Palace Gate Generals to Left and Right Gate-keeping Guard Command Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 5 the Left and Right Attendant Commanders became the Left and Right Guard Command Offices; the Left and Right Valiant Attendant Commanders became the Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Command Offices; and the Left and Right Palace Gate Generals became the Left and Right Gate-keeping Guard Command Offices.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改左右衞率府曰左右典戎衞，左右宗衞率府曰左右司禦率府，左右虞候率府曰左右淸道衞，左右内率府曰左右奉裕衞，左右監門率府曰左右崇掖衞。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2, Left and Right Guard Command Offices were renamed Left and Right Model Military Guards; Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Command Offices to Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Commands; Left and Right Patrol Command Offices to Left and Right Clearway Guards; Left and Right Inner Command Offices to Left and Right Provider of Abundance Guards; Left and Right Gate-keeping Guard Command Offices to Left and Right Honored Flank Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the Left and Right Guard Command Offices became the Left and Right Model Military Guards; the Ceremonial Guard Command Offices became Ceremonial Guard Commands; the Patrol Command Offices became Clearway Guards; the Inner Command Offices became Provider of Abundance Guards; and the Gate-keeping Guard Command Offices became Honored Flank Guards.

sentences.zh: 武后垂拱中，改左右監門率府曰左右鶴禁衞。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's Chuigong period, Left and Right Gate-keeping Guard Command Offices were renamed Left and Right Crane Forbidden Guards.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's Chuigong reign the Left and Right Gate-keeping Guard Command Offices were renamed the Left and Right Crane Forbidden Guards.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，改左右司禦率府曰左右宗衞府，左右淸道衞曰左右虞候率府。

translations.literal: In Shenlong 1, Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Commands were renamed Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Offices; Left and Right Clearway Guards to Left and Right Patrol Command Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 1 the Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Commands became Ceremonial Guard Offices, and the Left and Right Clearway Guards became Patrol Command Offices.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，左右宗衞府復曰左右司禦率府。

translations.literal: In Jingyun 2, the Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Offices again became Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Commands.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 2 the Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Offices were restored as Ceremonial Guard Commands.

sentences.zh: 開元初，左右虞候率府復曰左右淸道率府。

translations.literal: In early Kaiyuan, Left and Right Patrol Command Offices again became Left and Right Clearway Guard Commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan period the Left and Right Patrol Command Offices were again renamed Clearway Guard Commands.

sentences.zh: 長史各一人，正七品上。

translations.literal: Chief Administrators — one each, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each command had one Chief Administrator of upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌判諸曹府。

translations.literal: They adjudicated all bureau offices.
translations.idiomatic: They adjudicated the business of every bureau office.

sentences.zh: 季秋以屬官功狀上於率，而爲考課。

translations.literal: In the last month of autumn they submitted subordinate officials' merit records to the Commander for performance evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Each autumn the Chief Administrators submitted their subordinates' merit records to the Commander for annual evaluation.

sentences.zh: 録事參軍事各一人，從八品上；

translations.literal: Recording Secretaries — one each, upper secondary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each command had one Recording Secretary of upper secondary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 倉曹參軍事、兵曹參軍事、胄曹參軍事、騎曹參軍事各一人，從八品下。

translations.literal: Granary Bureau Secretaries, Military Bureau Secretaries, Helmet Bureau Secretaries, and Cavalry Bureau Secretaries — one each, lower secondary eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each command had one Granary Bureau Secretary, one Military Bureau Secretary, one Helmet Bureau Secretary, and one Cavalry Bureau Secretary, all of lower secondary eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 倉曹掌文官簿書，兵曹掌武官簿書，冑曹掌器械、公廨營繕。

translations.literal: The Granary Bureau managed civil officials' registers; the Military Bureau managed military officials' registers; the Helmet Bureau managed equipment and the construction and repair of government offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Bureau kept the civil staff registers; the Military Bureau kept the military staff registers; and the Helmet Bureau oversaw arms and the construction and repair of official buildings.

sentences.zh: 司階各一人，從六品上；

translations.literal: Stairway Officers — one each, upper secondary sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each command had one Stairway Officer of upper secondary sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 中候各二人，從七品下；

translations.literal: Middle Escorts — two each, lower secondary seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: Two Middle Escorts each of lower secondary seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 司戈各二人，從八品上；

translations.literal: Halberd Officers — two each, upper secondary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Two Halberd Officers each of upper secondary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 執戟各三人，散長上各十人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Halberd Bearers — three each; Senior Guards at large — ten each, lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Three Halberd Bearers each; ten Senior Guards at large each of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 左右司禦、淸道、監門、内率府，自率以下品同。

translations.literal: For the Left and Right Ceremonial, Clearway, Gate-keeping, and Inner Guard Commands, from the Commander downward ranks were the same.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ceremonial, Clearway, Gate-keeping, and Inner Guard Commands, ranks from the Commander down matched those of the Guard Command Office.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府一人，史一人。

translations.literal: There were one clerk, one office assistant, and one scribe.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one clerk, one office assistant, and one scribe.

sentences.zh: 倉曹，府一人，史二人；

translations.literal: Granary Bureau — one office assistant, two scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Bureau had one office assistant and two scribes;

sentences.zh: 兵曹、冑曹，各府二人，史三人；

translations.literal: Military Bureau and Helmet Bureau — two office assistants and three scribes each;
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau and Helmet Bureau each had two office assistants and three scribes;

sentences.zh: 騎曹，府五人，史七人。

translations.literal: Cavalry Bureau — five office assistants, seven scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Cavalry Bureau had five office assistants and seven scribes.

sentences.zh: 亭長、掌固各二人。

translations.literal: Station chiefs and gate wardens — two each.
translations.idiomatic: There were two station chiefs and two gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 親府、勳府、翊府三府毎府中郎將各一人，從四品上；

translations.literal: The Personal, Merit, and Assist Offices — in each office one Colonel, upper secondary fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Personal, Merit, and Assist Offices each had one Colonel of upper secondary fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 左右郎將各一人，正五品下。

translations.literal: One Left and one Right Vice Colonel each, lower fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and one Left and one Right Vice Colonel each of lower fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 中郎將、郎將，掌其府校尉、旅帥及親、勳、翊衞之屬宿衞，而總其事。

translations.literal: The Colonels and Vice Colonels commanded the Captains, Brigade Commanders, and subordinates of the Personal, Merit, and Assist Guards on overnight guard duty, and managed all affairs of their offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonels and Vice Colonels commanded the Captains, Brigade Commanders, and Personal, Merit, and Assist Guards on palace watch, and oversaw all business of their offices.

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事各一人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Military Bureau Secretaries — one each, upper secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one Military Bureau Secretary of upper secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌判句。

translations.literal: They managed seals and case annotations.
translations.idiomatic: They managed seals and the annotation of case records.

sentences.zh: 大朝會及皇太子出，則從鹵簿而涖其儀。

translations.literal: At great court assemblies and when the crown prince went out, they followed the ceremonial guard and presided over the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: During grand court assemblies and when the Crown Prince went abroad, they joined the ceremonial procession and directed the ritual arrangements.

sentences.zh: 親衞從七品上，勳衞正八品上，翊衞從八品上，員皆亡。

translations.literal: Personal Guards, lower secondary seventh rank; Merit Guards, upper eighth rank; Assist Guards, upper secondary eighth rank — all posts vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Personal Guards held lower secondary seventh rank; Merit Guards upper eighth rank; Assist Guards upper secondary eighth rank — all posts were vacant.

sentences.zh: 校尉各五人，從六品上；

translations.literal: Captains — five each, upper secondary sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Five Captains each of upper secondary sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 旅帥各十人，正七品下；

translations.literal: Brigade Commanders — ten each, lower seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: Ten Brigade Commanders each of lower seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 隊正各二十人，從八品上。

translations.literal: Squad Leaders — twenty each, upper secondary eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty Squad Leaders each of upper secondary eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，改功曹曰親衞，義曹曰勳衞，良曹曰翊衞，置三府，有録事一人，府、史各一人。

translations.literal: In Wude 1, the Merit Bureau was renamed Personal Guard, the Righteousness Bureau Merit Guard, the Good Bureau Assist Guard; three offices were established, with one clerk, one office assistant, and one scribe each.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1 the Merit Bureau became the Personal Guard, the Righteousness Bureau the Merit Guard, and the Good Bureau the Assist Guard; three offices were created, each with one clerk, one office assistant, and one scribe.

sentences.zh: 太子左右司禦率府率各一人，正四品上；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Commands: one Commander each, upper fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's Left and Right Ceremonial Guard Commands each had one Commander of upper fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 副率各二人，從四品上。

translations.literal: Vice Commanders — two each, upper secondary fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two Vice Commanders each of upper secondary fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌同左右衞。

translations.literal: Their duties were the same as the Left and Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Their responsibilities matched those of the Left and Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 凡諸曹及外府旅賁番上者隸焉。

translations.literal: All bureaus and escort guards of the outer offices on rotation were subordinate thereto.
translations.idiomatic: Every bureau and every escort guard of the outer offices rotating to duty came under their authority.

sentences.zh: 長史各一人，正七品上；

translations.literal: Chief Administrators — one each, upper seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each command had one Chief Administrator of upper seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 録事參軍事各一人，從八品上；

translations.literal: Recording Secretaries — one each, upper secondary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: one Recording Secretary each of upper secondary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 倉曹參軍事、兵曹參軍事、胄曹參軍事、騎曹參軍事，各一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: Granary Bureau Secretaries, Military Bureau Secretaries, Helmet Bureau Secretaries, and Cavalry Bureau Secretaries — one each, lower secondary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: one Granary Bureau Secretary, one Military Bureau Secretary, one Helmet Bureau Secretary, and one Cavalry Bureau Secretary each of lower secondary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 司階各一人，中候各二人，司戈各二人，執戟各三人。

translations.literal: Stairway Officers — one each; Middle Escorts — two each; Halberd Officers — two each; Halberd Bearers — three each.
translations.idiomatic: one Stairway Officer, two Middle Escorts, two Halberd Officers, and three Halberd Bearers each.

sentences.zh: 親衞、勳衞、翊衞三府中郎將以下，如左右衞率府。

translations.literal: From Colonels downward in the Personal, Merit, and Assist Guard offices, the same as in the Left and Right Guard Command Offices.
translations.idiomatic: From the Colonels down, the Personal, Merit, and Assist Guard offices matched the Left and Right Guard Command Offices.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，史二人。

translations.literal: There were one clerk and two scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one clerk and two scribes.

sentences.zh: 倉曹，府一人，史二人；

translations.literal: Granary Bureau — one office assistant, two scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Bureau had one office assistant and two scribes;

sentences.zh: 兵曹，府二人，史三人；

translations.literal: Military Bureau — two office assistants, three scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau had two office assistants and three scribes;

sentences.zh: 冑曹，府、史各二人。

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau — two office assistants and two scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Helmet Bureau had two office assistants and two scribes.

sentences.zh: 亭長一人，掌固二人。

translations.literal: One station chief and two gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: There was one station chief and two gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 太子左右淸道率府率各一人，副率各二人。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Left and Right Clearway Guard Commands: one Commander each, two Vice Commanders each.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's Left and Right Clearway Guard Commands each had one Commander and two Vice Commanders.

sentences.zh: 掌晝夜巡警。

translations.literal: They managed day-and-night patrols.
translations.idiomatic: They conducted patrols around the clock.

sentences.zh: 凡諸曹及外府直盪番上者隸焉。

translations.literal: All bureaus and straight-line escort guards of the outer offices on rotation were subordinate thereto.
translations.idiomatic: Every bureau and every straight-line escort guard of the outer offices rotating to duty came under their authority.

sentences.zh: 皇太子出入，則以淸游隊先導，後拒隊爲殿。

translations.literal: When the crown prince went in and out, the clear-roving company led the way and the rear-guard company brought up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince entered or left the palace, the clear-roving company went ahead as vanguard and the rear-guard company closed the procession.

sentences.zh: 長史各一人，録事參軍事各一人，從八品上；

translations.literal: Chief Administrators — one each; Recording Secretaries — one each, upper secondary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each command had one Chief Administrator and one Recording Secretary of upper secondary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 倉曹參軍事、兵曹參軍事、胄曹參軍事各一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: Granary Bureau Secretaries, Military Bureau Secretaries, and Helmet Bureau Secretaries — one each, lower secondary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: one Granary Bureau Secretary, one Military Bureau Secretary, and one Helmet Bureau Secretary each of lower secondary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 左右司階各一人，左右中候各二人，左右司戈各一人，左右執戟各三人。

translations.literal: Left and Right Stairway Officers — one each; Left and Right Middle Escorts — two each; Left and Right Halberd Officers — one each; Left and Right Halberd Bearers — three each.
translations.idiomatic: one Left and one Right Stairway Officer, two Left and Right Middle Escorts, one Left and Right Halberd Officer, and three Left and Right Halberd Bearers each.

sentences.zh: 親衞、勳衞、翊衞三府中郎將以下，如左右衞率府。

translations.literal: From Colonels downward in the Personal, Merit, and Assist Guard offices, the same as in the Left and Right Guard Command Offices.
translations.idiomatic: From the Colonels down, the Personal, Merit, and Assist Guard offices matched the Left and Right Guard Command Offices.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，史二人，亭長二人，掌固二人。

translations.literal: There were one clerk, two scribes, two station chiefs, and two gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one clerk, two scribes, two station chiefs, and two gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 倉曹，府一人，史二人；

translations.literal: Granary Bureau — one office assistant, two scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Bureau had one office assistant and two scribes;

sentences.zh: 兵曹，府二人，史三人；

translations.literal: Military Bureau — two office assistants, three scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau had two office assistants and three scribes;

sentences.zh: 冑曹，府二人，史二人。

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau — two office assistants, two scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Helmet Bureau had two office assistants and two scribes.

sentences.zh: 細引押仗五十人。

translations.literal: Fine-guidance staff escorts — fifty.
translations.idiomatic: There were fifty fine-guidance staff escorts.

sentences.zh: 太子左右監門率府率各一人，副率各二人。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Left and Right Gate-keeping Guard Commands: one Commander each, two Vice Commanders each.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's Left and Right Gate-keeping Guard Commands each had one Commander and two Vice Commanders.

sentences.zh: 掌諸門禁衞。

translations.literal: They managed gate security and guard.
translations.idiomatic: They controlled gate security and palace guard.

sentences.zh: 凡財物、器用，出者有籍。

translations.literal: All property and implements taken out were recorded in the register.
translations.idiomatic: Every item of property or equipment removed had to be entered in the register.

sentences.zh: 長史各一人，録事參軍事各一人，正九品上；

translations.literal: Chief Administrators — one each; Recording Secretaries — one each, upper ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each command had one Chief Administrator and one Recording Secretary of upper ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事各一人，正九品下，兼領倉曹；

translations.literal: Military Bureau Secretaries — one each, lower ninth rank, concurrently heading the Granary Bureau;
translations.idiomatic: one Military Bureau Secretary each of lower ninth rank, who also headed the Granary Bureau;

sentences.zh: 冑曹參軍事各一人，正九品下；

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau Secretaries — one each, lower ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: and one Helmet Bureau Secretary each of lower ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 監門直長七十八人，從七品下。

translations.literal: Gate-keeping duty chiefs — seventy-eight, lower secondary seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were seventy-eight gate-keeping duty chiefs of lower secondary seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 唐改宮門將曰監門率，直事曰直長。

translations.literal: Under the Tang, Palace Gate Generals were renamed Gate-keeping Commanders, and duty officers were renamed duty chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, Palace Gate Generals became Gate-keeping Commanders and gate duty officers became duty chiefs.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，史二人，亭長一人，掌固二人。

translations.literal: There were one clerk, two scribes, one station chief, and two gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one clerk, two scribes, one station chief, and two gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 兵曹，府二人，史二人；

translations.literal: Military Bureau — two office assistants, two scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau had two office assistants and two scribes;

sentences.zh: 冑曹，府二人，史三人。

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau — two office assistants, three scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Helmet Bureau had two office assistants and three scribes.

sentences.zh: 太子左右内率府率率各一人，副率各一人。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Left and Right Inner Guard Commands: one Commander each, one Vice Commander each.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's Left and Right Inner Guard Commands each had one Commander and one Vice Commander.

sentences.zh: 掌千牛供奉之事。

translations.literal: They managed the Thousand-Ox attendants' service of honor.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw the Thousand-Ox attendants who served in the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇太子坐日，領千牛升殿。

translations.literal: On days when the crown prince took his seat, they led the Thousand-Ox guards up to the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On days when the Crown Prince held audience, they led the Thousand-Ox guards up to the hall.

sentences.zh: 射于射宮，則千牛奉弓矢立東階，西面；

translations.literal: When he shot at the archery hall, the Thousand-Ox guards held bows and arrows and stood on the eastern steps, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: When he practiced archery at the archery hall, the Thousand-Ox guards stood on the eastern steps facing west, holding bows and arrows;

sentences.zh: 率奉弓，副率奉矢、決拾。

translations.literal: the Commander held the bow, the Vice Commander held the arrows, thumb ring, and arm guard.
translations.idiomatic: the Commander carried the bow while the Vice Commander carried the arrows, thumb ring, and arm guard.

sentences.zh: 北面張弓，左執弣，右執簫以進，副率以弓拂矢而進，各退立於位。

translations.literal: Facing north, they strung the bow — the left hand holding the grip, the right the bow tip as they advanced; the Vice Commander brushed the arrows with the bow as he advanced; each then withdrew to his station.
translations.idiomatic: Facing north they strung the bow, the left hand on the grip and the right on the bow tip as they stepped forward; the Vice Commander swept the arrows with the bow as he advanced; then each withdrew to his post.

sentences.zh: 旣射，左内率啓其中否。

translations.literal: Once the shooting was finished, the Left Inner Commander reported whether the arrow had hit.
translations.idiomatic: After the shot, the Left Inner Commander announced whether the arrow had struck the target.

sentences.zh: 長史各一人，録事參軍事各一人，正九品上；

translations.literal: Chief Administrators — one each; Recording Secretaries — one each, upper ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each command had one Chief Administrator and one Recording Secretary of upper ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事各一人，正九品下，兼領倉曹；

translations.literal: Military Bureau Secretaries — one each, lower ninth rank, concurrently heading the Granary Bureau;
translations.idiomatic: one Military Bureau Secretary each of lower ninth rank, who also headed the Granary Bureau;

sentences.zh: 冑曹參軍事各一人，正九品下；

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau Secretaries — one each, lower ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: and one Helmet Bureau Secretary each of lower ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 千牛各四十四人，從七品上。

translations.literal: Thousand-Ox guards — forty-four each, upper secondary seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each command had forty-four Thousand-Ox guards of upper secondary seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 唐置兵曹，改司使左右復曰千牛備身，主射左右復曰備身左右，弓箭備身去弓箭之名。

translations.literal: The Tang established Military Bureau Secretaries and changed Attendant Directors of the Left and Right back to Thousand-Ox bodyguards; Archery Attendants of the Left and Right back to bodyguard attendants; and bow-and-arrow bodyguards dropped the bow-and-arrow designation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang a Military Bureau Secretary was added; Attendant Directors of the Left and Right were again called Thousand-Ox bodyguards; Archery Attendants of the Left and Right became bodyguard attendants; and bow-and-arrow bodyguards lost the bow-and-arrow prefix.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改千牛備身曰奉裕。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2, Thousand-Ox bodyguards were renamed Providers of Abundance.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 Thousand-Ox bodyguards were renamed Providers of Abundance.

sentences.zh: 開元中，千牛備身、備身左右，幷爲千牛。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan, Thousand-Ox bodyguards and bodyguard attendants were combined as Thousand-Ox guards.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era Thousand-Ox bodyguards and bodyguard attendants were merged into a single Thousand-Ox guard corps.

sentences.zh: 有備身二十八人，主仗四十人，録事一人，史二人。

translations.literal: There were twenty-eight bodyguard attendants, forty master-of-arms guards, one clerk, and two scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included twenty-eight bodyguard attendants, forty master-of-arms guards, one clerk, and two scribes.

sentences.zh: 兵曹，府一人，史二人；

translations.literal: Military Bureau — one office assistant, two scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau had one office assistant and two scribes;

sentences.zh: 冑曹，府一人，史一人。

translations.literal: Helmet Bureau — one office assistant, one scribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Helmet Bureau had one office assistant and one scribe.

sentences.zh: 校勘記0.85em|columns=2王府官傅一人，從三品。

translations.literal: [Collation note] Princely household officials — Tutor, one, upper secondary third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Princely household officials: one Tutor of upper secondary third rank.

sentences.zh: 掌輔正過失。

translations.literal: They assisted in correcting faults.
translations.idiomatic: He guided the prince and corrected his faults.

sentences.zh: 諮議參軍事一人，正五品上。

translations.literal: Advisory Secretaries — one, upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Advisory Secretary of upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌訏謀議事。

translations.literal: They managed deliberation and counsel on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He offered counsel and deliberated on princely affairs.

sentences.zh: 友一人，從五品下。

translations.literal: Companions — one, lower secondary fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Companion of lower secondary fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌侍游處，規諷道義。

translations.literal: They attended in leisure and recreation, offering remonstrance on moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the prince in his daily rounds, offering moral guidance and remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 侍讀，無定員。

translations.literal: Reading Instructors — no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Instructors had no fixed establishment.

sentences.zh: 文學一人，從六品上。

translations.literal: Literary Officers — one, upper secondary sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Literary Officer of upper secondary sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌校典籍，侍從文章。

translations.literal: They collated the classics and attended in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He collated the library classics and assisted the prince in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 東西閤祭酒各一人，從七品上。

translations.literal: East and West Pavilion Libationers — one each, upper secondary seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each side of the pavilion had one Libationer of upper secondary seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 掌禮賢良、導賓客。

translations.literal: They managed courtesies toward worthy men and guided guests.
translations.idiomatic: They received worthy visitors and conducted guest protocol.

sentences.zh: 自祭酒以下為王官。

translations.literal: From the Libationers downward were princely household officials.
translations.idiomatic: Every post from Libationer downward ranked as a princely household appointment.

sentences.zh: 武德中，置師一人、常侍二人、侍郎四人，皆掌表啟書疏，贊相禮儀；

translations.literal: During Wude, one Preceptor, two Regular Attendants, and four Vice Directors were established, all managing memorials and correspondence and assisting in ritual protocol;
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude period the court added one Preceptor, two Regular Attendants, and four Vice Directors, all charged with drafting memorials and letters and assisting in court ceremonial;

sentences.zh: 舍人四人，掌通傳引納。

translations.literal: Four Gentlemen-in-Attendance managed transmission, conveyance, and introduction.
translations.idiomatic: Four Gentlemen-in-Attendance handled messages and guided visitors in and out.

sentences.zh: 謁者二人，舍人二人，諮議參軍事、友，皆正五品下；

translations.literal: Two Ushers, two Gentlemen-in-Attendance, an Advisory Secretary, and a Companion — all lower fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: There were two Ushers, two Gentlemen-in-Attendance, an Advisory Secretary, and a Companion, all of lower fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 文學、祭酒，皆正六品下。

translations.literal: Literary Officer and Libationer — all lower sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Literary Officer and the Libationers held lower sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 高宗、中宗時，相王府長史以宰相兼之，魏、雍、衞王府以尚書兼之，徐、韓二王為刺史，府官同外官，資望愈下。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Gaozong and Zhongzong, the Chief Administrator of the Prince of Xiang's household was concurrently held by a Chancellor; the Wei, Yong, and Wei princely households by Ministers; the Princes of Xu and Han served as prefects — household officials equaled outer officials, and prestige grew ever lower.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Gaozong and Zhongzong a Chancellor doubled as Chief Administrator of the Prince of Xiang's household, while Ministers held the same post for the Wei, Yong, and Wei establishments; when the Princes of Xu and Han became prefectural governors, household staff were treated like regular territorial officials and the posts' prestige sank further.

sentences.zh: 永淳以前，王未出閤則不開府。

translations.literal: Before Yongchun, if a prince had not left the pavilion he did not open a household.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Yongchun era a prince who had not yet been released from the Eastern Palace did not receive a separate princely household.

sentences.zh: 天授二年，置皇孫府官。

translations.literal: In Tianshou 2, princely household officials for the emperor's grandsons were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshou 2 the court created household offices for imperial grandsons.

sentences.zh: 玄宗諸子多不出閤，王官益輕而員亦減矣。

translations.literal: Most of Emperor Xuanzong's sons did not leave the pavilion; princely appointments grew lighter and staff numbers were reduced as well.
translations.idiomatic: Because most of Emperor Xuanzong's sons never left the Eastern Palace, princely appointments lost status and their establishments were cut back.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，改師曰傅，開元二年廢，尋復置，廢常侍、侍郎、謁者、舍人。

translations.literal: In Jingyun 2 Preceptor was changed to Tutor; abolished in Kaiyuan 2, then soon restored; Regular Attendants, Vice Directors, Ushers, and Gentlemen-in-Attendance were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 2 the Preceptor was retitled Tutor; the post was abolished in Kaiyuan 2 but soon reinstated, while Regular Attendants, Vice Directors, Ushers, and Gentlemen-in-Attendance were eliminated.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，改諸王侍讀曰奉諸王講讀，大中初復舊。

translations.literal: In Kaicheng 1, Princes' Reading Instructors were renamed Attendants Lecturing the Princes; at the start of Dazhong the old title was restored.
