translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 1 Reading Instructors to the Princes became Attendants Lecturing the Princes; the original title was restored at the beginning of the Dazhong era.

sentences.zh: 長史一人，從四品上；

translations.literal: Chief Administrator — one, upper secondary fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: There was one Chief Administrator of upper secondary fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 司馬一人，從四品下。

translations.literal: Vice Administrator — one, lower secondary fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and one Vice Administrator of lower secondary fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 皆掌統府僚，紀綱職務。

translations.literal: Both managed the household staff and maintained the discipline of duties.
translations.idiomatic: Both oversaw the household staff and kept official business in order.

sentences.zh: 掾一人，掌通判功曹、倉曹、戶曹事，屬一人，皆正六品上，掌通判兵曹、騎曹、法曹、士曹事。

translations.literal: One Registrar managed joint adjudication of Merit Bureau, Granary Bureau, and Household Bureau affairs; one Assistant — both upper sixth rank — managed joint adjudication of Military Bureau, Cavalry Bureau, Justice Bureau, and Works Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Registrar of upper sixth rank oversaw the Merit, Granary, and Household Bureaus; one Assistant of the same rank oversaw the Military, Cavalry, Justice, and Works Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，掌覆省書教，記室參軍事二人，掌表啟書疏，錄事參軍事一人，皆從六品上，掌付事、句稽，省署鈔目。

translations.literal: One Chief Clerk managed review of written orders; two Secretariat Secretaries managed memorials and correspondence; one Recording Secretary — all upper secondary sixth rank — managed assignment of affairs, audit, and oversight of office copies.
translations.idiomatic: One Chief Clerk reviewed official directives; two Secretariat Secretaries handled memorials and letters; and one Recording Secretary, all of upper secondary sixth rank, assigned tasks, audited accounts, and checked office registers.

sentences.zh: 錄事一人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Recording Secretary — one, lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one recording secretary of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 功曹參軍事掌文官簿書、考課、陳設，倉曹參軍事掌祿稟、廚膳、出內、市易、畋漁、芻藳，戶曹參軍事掌封戶、僮僕、弋獵、過所，兵曹參軍事掌武官簿書、考課、儀衞、假使，騎曹參軍事掌廄牧、騎乘、文物、器械，法曹參軍事掌按訊、決刑，士曹參軍事掌土功、公廨，自功曹以下各一人，正七品上。

translations.literal: Merit Bureau Secretary managed civil roster records, performance review, and ceremonial display; Granary Bureau Secretary managed salary distribution, kitchen meals, expenditures, market trade, hunting and fishing, and fodder; Household Bureau Secretary managed sealed households, servants, hunting permits, and travel passes; Military Bureau Secretary managed military roster records, performance review, ceremonial guard, and temporary assignments; Cavalry Bureau Secretary managed stables, riding mounts, ceremonial regalia, and equipment; Justice Bureau Secretary managed interrogation and judgment of punishments; Works Bureau Secretary managed earthworks and official buildings — from Merit Bureau downward one each, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Merit Bureau Secretary kept civil personnel records, ran evaluations, and arranged ceremonial display; the Granary Bureau Secretary supervised rations, kitchens, disbursements, market transactions, hunting and fishing, and fodder; the Household Bureau Secretary handled sealed households, servants, hunting licenses, and travel passes; the Military Bureau Secretary maintained military rosters, evaluations, guard formations, and temporary assignments; the Cavalry Bureau Secretary oversaw stables, mounts, ritual accoutrements, and equipment; the Justice Bureau Secretary conducted interrogations and pronounced punishments; the Works Bureau Secretary directed public construction — each bureau had one secretary of upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 參軍事二人，正八品下；

translations.literal: Secretaries — two, lower eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Two Secretaries of lower eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 行參軍事四人，從八品上。

translations.literal: Acting Secretaries — four, upper secondary eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and four Acting Secretaries of upper secondary eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 皆掌出使雜檢校。

translations.literal: All managed dispatch on missions and miscellaneous inspections.
translations.idiomatic: All handled special missions and ad hoc inspections.

sentences.zh: 典籤二人，從八品下，掌宣傳書教。

translations.literal: Document Attendants — two, lower secondary eighth rank, managing transmission of written orders.
translations.idiomatic: Two Document Attendants of lower secondary eighth rank conveyed official orders.

sentences.zh: 武德中，改功曹以下書佐、法曹行書佐、士曹佐皆曰參軍事，長兼行書佐曰行參軍，廢城局參軍事。

translations.literal: During Wude, Clerks below Merit Bureau, Justice Bureau Acting Clerks, and Works Bureau Clerks were all renamed Secretaries; chiefs who concurrently held Acting Clerk posts were called Acting Secretaries; Fort Bureau Secretaries were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude period clerks in the Merit Bureau and below, acting clerks in the Justice Bureau, and clerks in the Works Bureau were all retitled Secretaries; chiefs who also performed acting clerk duties became Acting Secretaries, and the Fort Bureau secretariat was abolished.

sentences.zh: 又有鎧曹參軍事二人，掌儀衞兵仗；

translations.literal: There were also two Armor Bureau Secretaries managing ceremonial guard arms;
translations.idiomatic: The household also had two Armor Bureau Secretaries in charge of ceremonial guard weapons;

sentences.zh: 田曹參軍事一人，掌公廨、職田、弋獵；

translations.literal: one Fields Bureau Secretary managing official buildings, official fields, and hunting;
translations.idiomatic: one Fields Bureau Secretary overseeing offices, allotted fields, and hunting grounds;

sentences.zh: 水曹參軍事二人，掌舟船、漁捕、芻草。

translations.literal: two Water Bureau Secretaries managing boats, fishing, and fodder grass.
translations.idiomatic: and two Water Bureau Secretaries responsible for boats, fishing, and fodder.

sentences.zh: 皆正七品下。

translations.literal: All lower seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: All held lower seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 家史二人，百司問事謁者一人，正七品下。

translations.literal: Household Clerks — two; Bureau Affairs Usher — one, lower seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two household clerks and one Bureau Affairs Usher of lower seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 司閤一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Gate Manager — one, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: One Gate Manager of lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，廢鎧曹、田曹、水曹。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, Armor Bureau, Fields Bureau, and Water Bureau were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era the Armor, Fields, and Water Bureaus were abolished.

sentences.zh: 武后時，家吏以下皆廢。

translations.literal: Under Empress Wu, household clerks and below were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's reign household clerks and all posts beneath them were eliminated.

sentences.zh: 主簿、記室有史二人；

translations.literal: Chief Clerk and Secretariat each had two clerks;
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Clerk and Secretariat each had two clerks;

sentences.zh: 錄事、功曹、倉曹、兵曹、騎曹、法曹、士曹，各府一人、史二人；

translations.literal: Recording, Merit, Granary, Military, Cavalry, Justice, and Works — one office attendant and two clerks each;
translations.idiomatic: the Recording, Merit, Granary, Military, Cavalry, Justice, and Works bureaus each had one office attendant and two clerks;

sentences.zh: 戶曹府、史，各二人。

translations.literal: Household Bureau — two office attendants and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: and the Household Bureau two attendants and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 自典籤以上為府官，郡王、嗣王不置長史。

translations.literal: From Document Attendant upward were household officials; Commandery Princes and Successor Princes did not appoint Chief Administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Posts from Document Attendant up counted as household officials; Commandery Princes and Successor Princes had no Chief Administrator.

sentences.zh: 親事府典軍二人，正五品上；

translations.literal: Personal Service Office Commanders — two, upper fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Personal Service Office had two Commanders of upper fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 副典軍二人，從五品上。

translations.literal: Vice Commanders — two, upper secondary fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two Vice Commanders of upper secondary fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 皆掌校尉以下守衞、陪從，兼知鞍馬。

translations.literal: All managed guard and retinue from Captain downward, and also oversaw saddlery and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They commanded the guard and retinue ranks below Captain and also supervised horses and tack.

sentences.zh: 校尉五人，從六品上；

translations.literal: Captains — five, upper secondary sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Five Captains of upper secondary sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 旅帥，從七品下；

translations.literal: Company Commanders, lower secondary seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: Company Commanders of lower secondary seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 隊正，從八品下，隊副，從九品下。

translations.literal: Squad Leaders lower secondary eighth rank, Squad Deputies lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Squad Leaders of lower secondary eighth rank and Squad Deputies of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 皆掌領親事、帳內陪從。

translations.literal: All commanded personal attendants and tent retinue in escort.
translations.idiomatic: All led personal attendants and inner-tent escorts.

sentences.zh: 自旅帥以下，視親事多少乃置。

translations.literal: From Company Commander downward, posts were established according to the number of personal attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Company Commanders and ranks below them were appointed in proportion to how many personal attendants were enrolled.

sentences.zh: 帳內府典軍二人，正五品上；

translations.literal: Inner Tent Office Commanders — two, upper fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Tent Office had two Commanders of upper fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 副典軍二人，從五品上。

translations.literal: Vice Commanders — two, upper secondary fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two Vice Commanders of upper secondary fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 自校尉以下，員、品如親事府。

translations.literal: From Captain downward, quotas and ranks were as in the Personal Service Office.
translations.idiomatic: From Captain downward ranks and staffing matched the Personal Service Office.

sentences.zh: 初，典軍以武官及流外為之，領執仗、帳內等。

translations.literal: Initially Commanders were drawn from military officers and extramural appointees, commanding halberd-bearers, inner tent personnel, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: At first Commanders were selected from military officers and extrabureau staff, leading halberd-bearers, inner-tent guards, and similar personnel.

sentences.zh: 秦王、齊王府置左右六護軍府、左右親軍府、左右帳內府。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi households established Left and Right Six Guard Offices, Left and Right Personal Guard Offices, and Left and Right Inner Tent Offices.
translations.idiomatic: The households of the Princes of Qin and Qi each maintained six Guard Offices on the left and right, Personal Guard Offices on both flanks, and Inner Tent Offices on both flanks.

sentences.zh: 左一、右一護軍府，護軍各一人，副護軍各二人，長史、錄事參軍事，倉曹、兵曹、鎧曹參軍事，各一人，統軍各五人，別將各一人。

translations.literal: Left One and Right One Guard Offices: one Guard General each, two Vice Guard Generals each, one Chief Administrator, Recording Secretary, Granary, Military, and Armor Bureau Secretaries each, five Army Controllers each, one Separate General each.
translations.idiomatic: In the First Left and First Right Guard Offices each side had one Guard General, two Vice Guard Generals, a Chief Administrator and Recording Secretary, one secretary each for the Granary, Military, and Armor Bureaus, five Army Controllers, and one Separate General.

sentences.zh: 左二、右二護軍府，左三、右三護軍府，減統軍三人，別將六人。

translations.literal: Second Left and Second Right Guard Offices, Third Left and Third Right Guard Offices — three fewer Army Controllers and six fewer Separate Generals.
translations.idiomatic: The Second and Third Guard Offices on left and right had three fewer Army Controllers and six fewer Separate Generals.

sentences.zh: 左右親軍府，統軍各一人，長史各一人，錄事參軍事，兵曹、鎧曹參軍事，左別將，右別將，各一人。

translations.literal: Left and Right Personal Guard Offices: one Army Controller each, one Chief Administrator each, Recording Secretary, Military and Armor Bureau Secretaries, one Left Separate General and one Right Separate General each.
translations.idiomatic: Each Personal Guard Office had one Army Controller, one Chief Administrator, a Recording Secretary, Military and Armor Bureau secretaries, and one Separate General on the left and one on the right.

sentences.zh: 帳內府職員，與護軍府同。

translations.literal: Inner Tent Office staff was the same as Guard Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Tent Office staffing matched that of the Guard Offices.

sentences.zh: 又有庫直，隸親事府；

translations.literal: There were also Armory Guards subordinate to the Personal Service Office;
translations.idiomatic: There were also Armory Guards under the Personal Service Office;

sentences.zh: 驅咥直，隸帳內府。

translations.literal: Tent Escort Guards subordinate to the Inner Tent Office.
translations.idiomatic: and Tent Escort Guards under the Inner Tent Office.

sentences.zh: 選材勇為之。

translations.literal: Men of talent and courage were selected for these posts.
translations.idiomatic: Only men noted for ability and valor were chosen.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，庫直以下皆廢。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, Armory Guards and below were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era Armory Guards and all lesser posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 親事府有府一人，史二人；

translations.literal: Personal Service Office: one office attendant, two clerks;
translations.idiomatic: The Personal Service Office had one attendant and two clerks;

sentences.zh: 執仗親事十六人，執弓仗；

translations.literal: sixteen halberd-bearing personal attendants, bearing halberds and regalia;
translations.idiomatic: sixteen personal attendants bearing halberds and ceremonial arms;

sentences.zh: 執乘親事十六人，掌供騎乘；

translations.literal: sixteen mount-bearing personal attendants, managing provision of riding mounts;
translations.idiomatic: and sixteen mounted attendants who provided horses for riding;

sentences.zh: 親事三百三十人。

translations.literal: Personal attendants — 330.
translations.idiomatic: Personal attendants numbered 330 in all.

sentences.zh: 帳內府有府一人，史一人，帳內六百六十七人。

translations.literal: Inner Tent Office: one office attendant, one clerk, inner tent personnel — 667.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Tent Office had one attendant, one clerk, and 667 inner-tent guards.

sentences.zh: 親王國令一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: Prince's Domain Magistrate — one, lower secondary seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: A Prince's Domain had one Magistrate of lower secondary seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 大農一人，從八品下。

translations.literal: Grand Agriculturist — one, lower secondary eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and one Grand Agriculturist of lower secondary eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌判國司。

translations.literal: They managed adjudication of the domain administration.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw the administration of the prince's fief.

sentences.zh: 尉一人，正九品下；

translations.literal: Commandant — one, lower ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: One Commandant of lower ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Assistant — one, lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and one Assistant of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 學官長、丞各一人，掌教授內人；

translations.literal: Education Section Chiefs and Assistants one each, managing instruction of inner household personnel;
translations.idiomatic: The Education Section had one chief and one assistant who taught members of the inner household;

sentences.zh: 食官長、丞各一人，掌營膳食；

translations.literal: Food Section Chiefs and Assistants one each, managing provision of meals;
translations.idiomatic: the Food Section had one chief and one assistant who managed meals;

sentences.zh: 廄牧長、丞各二人，掌畜牧；

translations.literal: Stable and Pasture Section Chiefs and Assistants two each, managing livestock;
translations.idiomatic: the Stable and Pasture Section had two chiefs and two assistants who oversaw livestock;

sentences.zh: 典府長、丞各二人，掌府內雜事。

translations.literal: Household Store Section Chiefs and Assistants two each, managing miscellaneous inner household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and the Household Store Section had two chiefs and two assistants who handled miscellaneous domestic affairs.

sentences.zh: 長皆正九品下，丞皆從九品下。

translations.literal: Chiefs all lower ninth rank; Assistants all lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Section chiefs held lower ninth rank and assistants lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 有典衞八人，掌守衞、陪從。

translations.literal: There were eight Guard Supervisors managing guard duty and escort.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Guard Supervisors provided security and attended the prince in procession.

sentences.zh: 舍人四人，錄事一人，府四人，史八人。

translations.literal: Gentlemen-in-Attendance four, Recording Secretary one, office attendants four, clerks eight.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included four Gentlemen-in-Attendance, one recording secretary, four attendants, and eight clerks.

sentences.zh: 公主邑司令一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: Princess Fief Magistrate — one, lower secondary seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: A Princess's fief had one Magistrate of lower secondary seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，從八品下。

translations.literal: Assistant — one, lower secondary eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and one Assistant of lower secondary eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌公主財貨、稟積、田園。

translations.literal: They managed the princess's goods, stored provisions, fields, and gardens.
translations.idiomatic: They managed the princess's property, stores, fields, and gardens.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，正九品下；

translations.literal: Chief Clerk — one, lower ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: One Chief Clerk of lower ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 錄事一人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Recording Secretary — one, lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and one recording secretary of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 督封租、主家財貨出入。

translations.literal: They supervised fief rents and controlled the household's goods coming in and going out.
translations.idiomatic: They collected fief rents and kept accounts of household income and expenditure.

sentences.zh: 有史八人，謁者二人，舍人二人，家史二人。

translations.literal: There were eight clerks, two ushers, two gentlemen-in-attendance, and two household clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The office employed eight clerks, two ushers, two gentlemen-in-attendance, and two household recorders.

sentences.zh: 外官天下兵馬元帥、副元帥，都統、副都統，行軍長史，行軍司馬、行軍左司馬、行軍右司馬，判官，掌書記，行軍參謀，前軍兵馬使、中軍兵馬使、後軍兵馬使，中軍都虞候，各一人。

translations.literal: Outer officials: Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven, Vice Commander-in-Chief, Supreme Commander, Vice Supreme Commander, Campaign Chief Administrator, Campaign Vice Administrator, Left Campaign Vice Administrator, Right Campaign Vice Administrator, Adjudicator, Secretary, Campaign Advisor, Forward Army Military Commissioner, Central Army Military Commissioner, Rear Army Military Commissioner, Central Army Chief Inspector — one each.
translations.idiomatic: Among field appointments there were one each of Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven, Vice Commander-in-Chief, Supreme Commander, Vice Supreme Commander, Campaign Chief Administrator, Campaign Vice Administrator, Left and Right Campaign Vice Administrators, Adjudicator, Secretary, Campaign Advisor, Forward, Central, and Rear Army Military Commissioners, and Central Army Chief Inspector.

sentences.zh: 元帥、都統、招討使，掌征伐，兵罷則省。

translations.literal: Commanders, Supreme Commanders, and Pacification Commissioners managed campaigns; when troops were disbanded the offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Field marshals, supreme commanders, and pacification commissioners directed campaigns and were disbanded once the armies stood down.

sentences.zh: 都統總諸道兵馬，不賜旌節。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander commanded the armed forces of all circuits but was not granted banners and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme commander coordinated troops from every circuit but received no commission of authority.

sentences.zh: 高祖起兵，置左右領軍大都督，各總三軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised troops, Left and Right Army-leading Grand Commandants were established, each commanding three armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu first took up arms he appointed Left and Right Army-leading Grand Commandants, each commanding three armies.

sentences.zh: 及定京師，置左右元帥、太原道行軍元帥、西討元帥，皆親王領之。

translations.literal: When the capital was secured, Left and Right Marshals, Taiyuan Circuit Campaign Marshal, and Western Expedition Marshal were established, all led by imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: After securing the capital he created Left and Right Marshals, a Taiyuan Circuit campaign marshal, and a Western Expedition marshal, all led by imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，置天下兵馬元帥，都統朔方、河東、河北、平盧節度使。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven was established, supreme commander over the Shuofang, Hedong, Hebei, and Pinglu military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era the court created the post of Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven to coordinate the Shuofang, Hedong, Hebei, and Pinglu frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 招討、都統之名，始於此。

translations.literal: The titles Pacification Commissioner and Supreme Commander began here.
translations.idiomatic: This was the origin of the titles pacification commissioner and supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 大曆八年，罷天下兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: In Dali 8 Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 8 the Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven was abolished.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，以李希烈反，置諸軍行營兵馬都元帥；

translations.literal: In Jianzhong 4, because Li Xilie rebelled, Grand Marshal of All Campaign Headquarters Forces was established;
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 4, after Li Xilie rebelled, the court appointed a Grand Marshal of All Campaign Headquarters Forces;

sentences.zh: 興元元年，置副都統。

translations.literal: In Xingyuan 1 Vice Supreme Commander was established.
translations.idiomatic: and in Xingyuan 1 a vice supreme commander was added.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，置靈、夏六道元帥。

translations.literal: During Huichang, marshals for the six Ling and Xia circuits were established.
translations.idiomatic: During Huichang marshals were appointed for the six Ling and Xia frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 黃巢之難，置諸道行營都都統。

translations.literal: During the Huang Chao disaster, Supreme Commander of All Circuit Campaign Headquarters was established.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huang Chao uprising the court created a supreme commander over all circuit campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 天復三年，置諸道兵馬元帥，尋復改曰天下兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: In Tianfu 3, Commander-in-Chief of Circuit Forces was established; soon after it was again changed to Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 3 the court reinstated a commander-in-chief of circuit forces, soon retitled Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬，掌弼戎政。

translations.literal: Campaign Vice Administrator managed assisting military administration.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign vice administrator advised on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 居則習蒐狩，有役則申戰守之法，器械、糧糒、軍籍、賜予皆專焉。

translations.literal: In repose they practiced hunts and inspections; when there was service they expounded methods of warfare and defense; weapons, provisions, army registers, and grants were all their exclusive charge.
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime he drilled the men through hunts and reviews; in wartime he laid out strategy and tactics; and weapons, rations, muster rolls, and grants fell entirely under his purview.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，改贊治曰治中。

translations.literal: In Wude 1, Assistant Administrator was changed to Central Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1 the title Assistant Administrator was changed to Central Administrator.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，曰司馬，下州亦置焉。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, it was called Vice Administrator; inferior prefectures also established the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne the title became Vice Administrator, and it was instituted even in lower-tier prefectures.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，置洛州司馬。

translations.literal: In Xianqing 2, Vice Administrator of Luozhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 2 the court established a Vice Administrator for Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 武后大足元年，東都、北都、雍、荊、揚、益州，置左右司馬。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's first year of Dazu, at the Eastern Capital, Northern Capital, Yong, Jing, Yang, and Yi prefectures, Left and Right Vice Administrators were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazu under Empress Wu, the court appointed Left and Right Vice Administrators for the Eastern and Northern Capitals and the prefectures of Yong, Jing, Yang, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年省。

translations.literal: In Shenlong 2 they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: They were abolished in Shenlong 2.

sentences.zh: 太極元年，雍、洛四大都督府增司馬一人，亦分左右。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiji, for the four great area command headquarters of Yong and Luo, one Vice Administrator was added each, also divided into Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiji 1 the four great command headquarters of Yong and Luo each gained one additional Vice Administrator, likewise split into left and right posts.

sentences.zh: 掌書記，掌朝覲、聘問、慰薦、祭祀、祈祝之文與號令升絀之事。

translations.literal: The Secretary managed documents for imperial audiences, embassies, condolences and recommendations, sacrifices, prayers, and matters of orders, promotions, and demotions.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretary drafted documents for court audiences, diplomatic missions, condolences and recommendations, sacrifices and prayers, and handled orders governing promotions and demotions.

sentences.zh: 行軍參謀，關豫軍中機密。

translations.literal: The Campaign Advisor was concerned with and participated in army secrets.
translations.idiomatic: The Campaign Advisor handled confidential military affairs.

sentences.zh: 景龍元年，置掌書記。

translations.literal: In Jinglong 1 the Secretary was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 1 the court established the post of Secretary.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年，罷行軍參謀，尋復置。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 12 the Campaign Advisor was abolished; soon after it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 12 the Campaign Advisor was abolished but soon reinstated.

sentences.zh: 節度使、副大使知節度事、行軍司馬、副使、判官、支使、掌書記、推官、巡官、衙推各一人，同節度副使十人，館驛巡官四人，府院法直官、要籍、逐要親事各一人，隨軍四人。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner, Vice Ambassador Managing Military Affairs, Campaign Vice Administrator, Deputy Commissioner, Adjudicator, Branch Commissioner, Secretary, Investigating Officer, Circuit Inspector, Yamen Promoter — one each; ten posts equivalent to Vice Military Commissioner; four Postal Station Circuit Inspectors; one each of Prefecture Office Legal Examiner, Priority Registrar, and Personal Attendant on Priority Matters; four Campaign Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The establishment included one each of Military Commissioner, Vice Ambassador Managing Military Affairs, Campaign Vice Administrator, Deputy Commissioner, Adjudicator, Branch Commissioner, Secretary, Investigating Officer, Circuit Inspector, and Yamen Promoter; ten posts equivalent to the Vice Military Commissioner; four postal-station circuit inspectors; one each of legal examiner, priority registrar, and personal attendant; and four campaign attendants.

sentences.zh: 節度使封郡王，則有奏記一人；

translations.literal: If the Military Commissioner was enfeoffed as Prince of a Commandery, then there was one Memorial Recorder;
translations.idiomatic: When a military commissioner held the title Prince of a Commandery, he also had one Memorial Recorder;

sentences.zh: 兼觀察使，又有判官、支使、推官、巡官、衙推各一人；

translations.literal: If concurrently Observation Commissioner, there were also one each of Adjudicator, Branch Commissioner, Investigating Officer, Circuit Inspector, and Yamen Promoter;
translations.idiomatic: if he also served as Observation Commissioner, there was one each of Adjudicator, Branch Commissioner, Investigating Officer, Circuit Inspector, and Yamen Promoter;

sentences.zh: 又兼安撫使，則有副使、判官各一人；

translations.literal: If additionally Pacification Commissioner, then one each of Deputy Commissioner and Adjudicator;
translations.idiomatic: if he additionally served as Pacification Commissioner, one Deputy Commissioner and one Adjudicator were added;

sentences.zh: 兼支度、營田、招討、經略使，則有副使、判官各一人；

translations.literal: If concurrently Supply, Garrison-Farming, Pacification-Escort, or Frontier Strategy Commissioner, then one each of Deputy Commissioner and Adjudicator;
translations.idiomatic: if he also held the titles of supply, garrison-farming, pacification-escort, or frontier strategy commissioner, one deputy commissioner and one adjudicator were added;

sentences.zh: 支度使復有遣運判官、巡官各一人。

translations.literal: The Supply Commissioner additionally had one each of Transport Adjudicator and Circuit Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The supply commissioner also had one transport adjudicator and one circuit inspector.

sentences.zh: 節度使掌總軍旅，顓誅殺。

translations.literal: The Military Commissioner managed all military forces and held exclusive authority over executions.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioner commanded all troops and held sole authority over capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 初授，具帑抹兵仗詣兵部辭見，觀察使亦如之。

translations.literal: Upon first appointment, with formal attire and weapons in hand, they went to the Ministry of War for a farewell audience; Observation Commissioners did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: On first appointment they presented themselves at the Ministry of War in full regalia for a farewell audience, and observation commissioners followed the same rite.

sentences.zh: 辭日，賜雙旌雙節。

translations.literal: On the day of farewell, paired banners and paired credentials were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of departure the court bestowed paired banners and paired credentials.

sentences.zh: 行則建節、樹六纛，中官祖送，次一驛輒上聞。

translations.literal: When traveling they displayed the credential, raised six military banners, eunuchs saw them off, and after each post station they reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they displayed their commission and raised six military banners; eunuchs escorted them from the capital, and after every post station they reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 入境，州縣築節樓，迎以鼓角，衙仗居前，旌幢居中，大將鳴珂，金鉦鼓角居後，州縣齎印迎于道左。

translations.literal: Upon entering the jurisdiction, prefectures and counties built credential towers, welcomed them with drums and horns, yamen guards went ahead, banners and pennants were in the center, senior generals sounded jade clappers, bronze gongs and drums and horns followed behind, and prefectures and counties brought their seals to greet them on the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: On entering their jurisdiction, prefectures and counties erected credential towers and welcomed them with drums and horns — yamen guards leading, banners at the center, senior generals sounding jade clappers, bronze gongs and horns bringing up the rear, while local officials met them on the road bearing their seals.

sentences.zh: 視事之日，設禮案，高尺有二寸，方八尺，判三案，節度使判宰相，觀察使判節度使，團練使判觀察使。

translations.literal: On the day of assuming office, a ceremonial table was set, one foot two inches high and eight feet square, with three adjudication tables: the Military Commissioner adjudicated before the Chancellor, the Observation Commissioner before the Military Commissioner, and the Training Commissioner before the Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took office a ceremonial table was set one foot two inches high and eight feet square, with three adjudication tables — the military commissioner before the chancellor, the observation commissioner before the military commissioner, and the training commissioner before the observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三日洗印，視其刓缺。

translations.literal: On the third day the seal was washed and its wear and damage inspected.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the seal was washed and inspected for wear.

sentences.zh: 歲以八月考其治否，銷兵為上考，足食為中考，邊功為下考。

translations.literal: Each year in the eighth month their governance was evaluated: reducing troops was highest rating, sufficient food middle rating, frontier achievements lowest rating.
translations.idiomatic: Each August their performance was reviewed — demobilizing troops counted as the highest mark, securing adequate provisions as middling, and frontier exploits as the lowest.

sentences.zh: 觀察使以豐稔為上考，省刑為中考，辦稅為下考。

translations.literal: For Observation Commissioners, abundant harvest was highest rating, reduced punishments middle rating, tax collection lowest rating.
translations.idiomatic: Observation commissioners were rated highest for abundant harvests, middling for lighter punishments, and lowest for collecting taxes.

sentences.zh: 團練使以安民為上考，懲姦為中考，得情為下考。

translations.literal: For Training Commissioners, securing the people was highest rating, punishing wrongdoers middle rating, achieving justice lowest rating.
translations.idiomatic: Training commissioners earned top marks for securing the populace, middling marks for punishing wrongdoers, and lowest marks for achieving justice in cases.

sentences.zh: 防禦使以無虞為上考，清苦為中考，政成為下考。

translations.literal: For Defense Commissioners, being free from alarm was highest rating, enduring hardship middle rating, completing governance lowest rating.
translations.idiomatic: Defense commissioners were rated highest when the region was free from alarm, middling for enduring hardship, and lowest for completing their administrative tasks.

sentences.zh: 經略使以計度為上考，集事為中考，脩造為下考。

translations.literal: For Frontier Strategy Commissioners, planning and calculation was highest rating, gathering affairs middle rating, construction and repair lowest rating.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier strategy commissioners received top marks for planning, middling marks for gathering affairs, and lowest marks for construction and repair.

sentences.zh: 罷秩則交廳，以節度使印自隨，留觀察使、營田等印，以郎官主之。

translations.literal: When leaving office they handed over the yamen; the Military Commissioner seal went with them, while Observation Commissioner, Garrison-Farming, and other seals were left, administered by a palace official.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving office they surrendered the yamen — the military commissioner kept his own seal, while observation, garrison-farming, and other seals were left behind under a palace official's charge.

sentences.zh: 銷節樓、節堂，以節院使主之，祭奠以時。

translations.literal: The credential tower and credential hall were retired, administered by the Credential Office Commissioner, with sacrifices performed on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The credential tower and hall were closed down under a credential-office manager, with sacrifices performed at the proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 入朝未見，不入私第。

translations.literal: Before having been received in audience at court, they did not enter a private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Until they had been received in audience at court, they did not enter a private residence.

sentences.zh: 京兆、河南牧，大都督，大都護，皆親王遙領。

translations.literal: The Intendants of Jingzhao and Henan, Area Commanders, and Grand Protector Generals were all nominally held by imperial princes from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The intendants of Jingzhao and Henan, area commanders, and grand protector generals were all nominally held by imperial princes who remained at court.

sentences.zh: 兩府之政，以尹主之；

translations.literal: The governance of the two capitals was managed by the Intendants;
translations.idiomatic: The two capitals were governed by their intendants;

sentences.zh: 大都督府之政，以長史主之；

translations.literal: The governance of great area command headquarters was managed by the Chief Administrators;
translations.idiomatic: great area command headquarters by their chief administrators;

sentences.zh: 大都護府之政，以副大都護主之，副大都護則兼王府長史。

translations.literal: The governance of great protectorate headquarters was managed by the Deputy Grand Protector General; the Deputy Grand Protector General concurrently served as the princely household Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: and great protectorate headquarters by the deputy grand protector general, who also doubled as the princely household chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 其後有持節為節度、副大使知節度事者，正節度也。

translations.literal: Later there were those who held credentials as Military Commissioner or Vice Ambassador Managing Military Affairs — these were the regular Military Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Later those who held a commission as military commissioner or vice ambassador managing military affairs became the regular military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 諸王拜節度大使者，皆留京師。

translations.literal: Imperial princes appointed Military Commissioner Ambassadors all remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes appointed military commissioner ambassadors all remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 觀察使、副使、支使、判官、掌書記、推官、巡官、衙推、隨軍、要籍、進奏官，各一人。

translations.literal: Observation Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Branch Commissioner, Adjudicator, Secretary, Investigating Officer, Circuit Inspector, Yamen Promoter, Campaign Attendant, Priority Registrar, Memorial Presenter — one each.
translations.idiomatic: The observation commissioner's staff included one each of deputy commissioner, branch commissioner, adjudicator, secretary, investigating officer, circuit inspector, yamen promoter, campaign attendant, priority registrar, and memorial presenter.

sentences.zh: 團練使、副使、判官、推官、巡官、衙推，各一人。

translations.literal: Training Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Adjudicator, Investigating Officer, Circuit Inspector, Yamen Promoter — one each.
translations.idiomatic: The training commissioner had one each of deputy commissioner, adjudicator, investigating officer, circuit inspector, and yamen promoter.

sentences.zh: 防禦使、副使、判官、推官、巡官，各一人。

translations.literal: Defense Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Adjudicator, Investigating Officer, Circuit Inspector — one each.
translations.idiomatic: The defense commissioner had one each of deputy commissioner, adjudicator, investigating officer, and circuit inspector.

sentences.zh: 觀察處置使，掌察所部善惡，舉大綱。

translations.literal: Observation and Disposition Commissioner managed inspecting the good and bad in the jurisdiction and setting the broad outline.
translations.idiomatic: The observation and disposition commissioner inspected the virtue and misconduct of his jurisdiction and set policy in broad outline.

sentences.zh: 凡奏請，皆屬於州。

translations.literal: All memorials and petitions belonged to the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: All memorials and petitions were routed through the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，遣大使十三人巡省天下諸州，水旱則遣使，有巡察、安撫、存撫之名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, thirteen grand ambassadors were dispatched to inspect all prefectures under heaven; in cases of flood or drought envoys were also sent, with the titles Inspection, Pacification, and Relief.
translations.idiomatic: In early Zhenguan the court dispatched thirteen grand ambassadors to inspect every prefecture; in years of flood or drought it also sent envoys titled for inspection, pacification, or relief.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，以五品以上二十人為十道巡察使，按舉州縣，再周而代。

translations.literal: In Shenlong 2, twenty officials of fifth rank and above were made ten-circuit Inspection Commissioners, investigating prefectures and counties, rotating after two rounds.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 2 twenty fifth-rank-and-above officials were appointed as ten-circuit inspection commissioners to investigate prefectures and counties, rotating after two complete tours.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，置都督二十四人，察刺史以下善惡，置司舉從事二人，秩比侍御史。

translations.literal: In Jingyun 2, twenty-four Area Commanders were established to inspect the good and bad of prefects and below; two Judicial Attendants for Promotion were established, rank equal to Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 2 the court appointed twenty-four area commanders to review prefects and subordinate officials, with two judicial attendants of attendants' censor rank to assist in investigations.

sentences.zh: 揚、益、幷、荊四州為大都督，汴、兗、魏、冀、蒲、綿、秦、洪、潤、越十州為中都督，皆正三品；

translations.literal: Yang, Yi, Bing, and Jing prefectures were Superior Area Commands; Bian, Yan, Wei, Ji, Pu, Mian, Qin, Hong, Run, and Yue prefectures were Middle Area Commands — all upper third rank;
translations.idiomatic: Yang, Yi, Bing, and Jing were superior area commands; Bian, Yan, Wei, Ji, Pu, Mian, Qin, Hong, Run, and Yue were middle area commands — all of upper third rank;

sentences.zh: 齊、鄜、涇、襄、安、潭、遂、通、梁、夔十州為下都督，從三品。

translations.literal: Qi, Fu, Jing, Xiang, An, Tan, Sui, Tong, Liang, and Kui prefectures were Inferior Area Commands, secondary third rank.
translations.idiomatic: and Qi, Fu, Jing, Xiang, An, Tan, Sui, Tong, Liang, and Kui were inferior area commands of secondary third rank.

sentences.zh: 當時以為權重難制，罷之，唯四大都督府如故。

translations.literal: At the time it was thought their authority was weighty and hard to control, so they were abolished; only the four great area command headquarters remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Their powers were soon judged too heavy to control, and the posts were abolished — only the four great command headquarters remained.

sentences.zh: 置十道按察使，道各一人。

translations.literal: Ten-circuit Inspection Commissioners were established, one for each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The court then established ten-circuit inspection commissioners, one per circuit.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，曰十道按察採訪處置使，至四年罷，八年復置十道按察使，秋、冬巡視州縣，十年又罷。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 2 they were called Ten-Circuit Inspection and Investigation Disposition Commissioners; abolished in the fourth year, restored as Ten-Circuit Inspection Commissioners in the eighth year, inspecting prefectures and counties in autumn and winter, abolished again in the tenth year.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 2 they were retitled ten-circuit inspection and investigation disposition commissioners; abolished in year 4, restored as ten-circuit inspection commissioners in year 8 to tour prefectures and counties in autumn and winter, and abolished again in year 10.

sentences.zh: 十七年復置十道、京都、兩畿按察使，二十年曰採訪處置使，分十五道，天寶末，又兼黜陟使，乾元元年，改曰觀察處置使。

translations.literal: Restored in the seventeenth year as Ten-Circuit, Capital, and Two-Capital Inspection Commissioners; in the twentieth year called Investigation and Disposition Commissioners, divided into fifteen circuits; at the end of Tianbao they also concurrently served as Promotion and Demotion Commissioners; in the first year of Qianyuan changed to Observation and Disposition Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 they returned as ten-circuit, capital, and two-capital inspection commissioners; in year 20 became investigation and disposition commissioners across fifteen circuits; at the end of Tianbao they also served as promotion-and-demotion commissioners; and in Qianyuan 1 the title became observation and disposition commissioner.

sentences.zh: 西都、東都、北都牧各一人，從二品。

translations.literal: Western Capital, Eastern Capital, and Northern Capital Governors — one each, secondary second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Western, Eastern, and Northern Capitals each had one Governor of secondary second rank.

sentences.zh: 西都、東都、北都、鳳翔、成都、河中、江陵、興元、興德府尹各一人，從三品。

translations.literal: Western Capital, Eastern Capital, Northern Capital, Fengxiang, Chengdu, Hezhong, Jiangling, Xingyuan, and Xingde Prefecture Intendants — one each, secondary third rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Western, Eastern, and Northern Capitals and the prefectures of Fengxiang, Chengdu, Hezhong, Jiangling, Xingyuan, and Xingde each had one Intendant of secondary third rank.

sentences.zh: 掌宣德化，歲巡屬縣，觀風俗、錄囚、恤鰥寡。

translations.literal: They spread virtue and transformed through instruction, each year touring subordinate counties, observing customs, recording prisoners, and caring for widows and orphans.
translations.idiomatic: They spread imperial virtue, toured subordinate counties each year, observed local customs, reviewed prisoners, and cared for widows and orphans.

sentences.zh: 親王典州，則歲以上佐巡縣。

translations.literal: When an imperial prince held a prefecture, senior assistants toured the counties each year.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial prince nominally held a prefecture, senior assistants made the annual county tours.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，雍州置牧一人，以親王為之，然常以別駕領州事。

translations.literal: In Wude 1, one Governor was established for Yong Prefecture, held by an imperial prince, but ordinarily a Deputy Prefect managed prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1 Yong Prefecture gained a governor's post held by an imperial prince, though a deputy prefect usually managed day-to-day affairs.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，改尹曰長史。

translations.literal: During Yonghui, Intendant was changed to Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui the title Intendant was changed to Chief Administrator.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗伐高麗，置京城留守，其後車駕不在京都，則置留守，以右金吾大將軍為副留守；

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Taizong campaigned against Goguryeo, a capital garrison was established; afterward whenever the imperial carriage was absent from the capital a garrison was established, with the Right Gold Crow Grand General as Deputy Garrison Commander;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong first campaigned against Goguryeo a capital garrison was established; thereafter whenever the emperor left the capital a garrison was appointed, with the Right Gold Crow Grand General serving as deputy garrison commander;

sentences.zh: 開元元年，改京兆、河南府長史復為尹，通判府務，牧缺則行其事；

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 1, the Chief Administrators of Jingzhao and Henan prefectures were again changed to Intendants, jointly adjudicating prefecture affairs; when the Governor's post was vacant they performed its duties;
translations.idiomatic: in Kaiyuan 1 the chief administrators of Jingzhao and Henan were restored to the title Intendant and jointly managed prefecture affairs, acting in the governor's place when that post was vacant;

sentences.zh: 十一年，太原府亦置尹及少尹，以尹為留守，少尹為副留守：謂之三都留守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Taiyuan Prefecture also established an Intendant and Deputy Intendant, the Intendant serving as Garrison Commander and the Deputy Intendant as Deputy Garrison Commander — called the Three Capitals Garrison Commanders.
translations.idiomatic: and in year 11 Taiyuan also received an intendant and deputy intendant, the intendant serving as garrison commander and the deputy as deputy garrison commander — together called the Three Capitals garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 三都大都督府有典獄十八人，問事十二人，白直二十四人；

translations.literal: The three capitals' great area command headquarters had eighteen Prison Supervisors, twelve Interrogators, and twenty-four Day-and-Night Duty Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: The three capitals' great command headquarters employed eighteen prison supervisors, twelve interrogators, and twenty-four day-and-night duty attendants;

sentences.zh: 典獄以防守囚繫，問事以行罰。

translations.literal: Prison Supervisors guarded and defended prisoners; Interrogators carried out punishments.
translations.idiomatic: prison supervisors guarded detainees, and interrogators carried out punishments.

sentences.zh: 中府、上州，典獄十四人，問事八人，白直二十人；

translations.literal: Middle prefectures and upper prefectures: fourteen Prison Supervisors, eight Interrogators, twenty Day-and-Night Duty Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Middle prefectures and upper prefectures had fourteen prison supervisors, eight interrogators, and twenty day-and-night duty attendants;

sentences.zh: 下府、中州，典獄十二人，問事六人，白直十六人；

translations.literal: Lower prefectures and middle prefectures: twelve Prison Supervisors, six Interrogators, sixteen Day-and-Night Duty Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: lower prefectures and middle prefectures had twelve prison supervisors, six interrogators, and sixteen day-and-night duty attendants;

sentences.zh: 下州，典獄八人，問事四人，白直十人。

translations.literal: Lower prefectures: eight Prison Supervisors, four Interrogators, ten Day-and-Night Duty Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: and lower prefectures had eight prison supervisors, four interrogators, and ten day-and-night duty attendants.

sentences.zh: 自三都以下，皆有執刀十五人。

translations.literal: From the three capitals downward, all had fifteen Sword Bearers.
translations.idiomatic: From the three capitals downward, every jurisdiction had fifteen sword bearers.

sentences.zh: 少尹二人，從四品下。

translations.literal: Deputy Intendants — two, lower secondary fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Deputy Intendants of lower secondary fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌貳府州之事，歲終則更次入計。

translations.literal: They assisted in prefecture and prefectural-capital affairs; at year's end they took turns entering the capital to report accounts.
translations.idiomatic: They assisted in managing prefectural affairs and took turns each year traveling to the capital to render accounts.

sentences.zh: 司錄參軍事二人，正七品上。

translations.literal: Chief Recording Secretaries — two, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Chief Recording Secretaries of upper seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 錄事四人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Recording Secretaries — four, upper secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Four recording secretaries of upper secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 功曹、倉曹、戶曹、田曹、兵曹、法曹、士曹參軍事各二人，皆正七品下。

translations.literal: Merit Bureau, Granary Bureau, Household Bureau, Fields Bureau, Military Bureau, Justice Bureau, and Works Bureau Secretaries — two each, all lower seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two secretaries each served the Merit, Granary, Household, Fields, Military, Justice, and Works Bureaus, all of lower seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 參軍事六人，正八品下。

translations.literal: Secretaries — six, lower eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were six Secretaries of lower eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 六府錄事參軍事以下減一人。

translations.literal: For the six prefectural capitals, Recording Secretaries and below were reduced by one each.
translations.idiomatic: In the six prefectural capitals the recording secretaries and all posts below were reduced by one.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍事，掌正違失，莅符印。

translations.literal: The Recording Secretary managed correcting errors, received the seal and tally.
translations.idiomatic: The recording secretary corrected procedural errors and held charge of the seal and tally.

sentences.zh: 武德初，改州主簿曰錄事參軍事，開元元年，改曰司錄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, the Prefecture Chief Clerk was changed to Recording Secretary; in Kaiyuan 1 it was changed to Chief Recording Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wude the prefecture chief clerk became recording secretary; in Kaiyuan 1 the title became chief recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 有史十人。

translations.literal: There were ten clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The office employed ten clerks.

sentences.zh: 大都督府有史四人，中府有史三人，下府、都護府、上州、中州、下州各有史二人。

translations.literal: Great area command headquarters had four clerks; middle prefectures three; lower prefectures, protectorate headquarters, upper prefectures, middle prefectures, and lower prefectures each had two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Great command headquarters had four clerks, middle prefectures three, and lower prefectures, protectorate headquarters, and upper, middle, and lower prefectures two each.

sentences.zh: 功曹司功參軍事，掌考課、假使、祭祀、禮樂、學校、表疏、書啟、祿食、祥異、醫藥、卜筮、陳設、喪葬。

translations.literal: Merit Bureau Merit Secretary managed performance review, temporary assignments, sacrifices, ritual and music, schools, memorials and petitions, correspondence, salary provisions, auspicious and strange omens, medicine, divination, display arrangements, and funerals.
translations.idiomatic: The Merit Bureau Secretary oversaw performance reviews, temporary assignments, sacrifices, ritual and music, schools, memorials and petitions, correspondence, salary provisions, omens, medicine, divination, ceremonial display, and funerals.

sentences.zh: 武德初，司功、司倉、司戶、司兵、司法、司士書佐皆為司功等參軍事，有府四人、史十人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, Merit, Granary, Household, Military, Justice, and Works Bureau Writing Assistants all became Merit Bureau Secretaries and the like; there were four office attendants and ten clerks.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wude the writing assistants of the Merit, Granary, Household, Military, Justice, and Works Bureaus became bureau secretaries; the staff included four office attendants and ten clerks.

sentences.zh: 大都督府有府三人、史六人；

translations.literal: Great area command headquarters had three office attendants and six clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Great command headquarters had three office attendants and six clerks;

sentences.zh: 中府有府二人、史三人；

translations.literal: Middle prefectures had two office attendants and three clerks;
translations.idiomatic: middle prefectures two office attendants and three clerks;

sentences.zh: 下府有府一人、史三人。

translations.literal: Lower prefectures had one office attendant and three clerks.
translations.idiomatic: and lower prefectures one office attendant and three clerks.

sentences.zh: 大都護府有府一人、史二人。

translations.literal: Great protectorate headquarters had one office attendant and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Protectorates of the highest rank employed one attendant and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 上府有府、史各二人。

translations.literal: Upper prefectures had two office attendants and two clerks each.
translations.idiomatic: Each upper prefecture staffed two attendants and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 上州有佐二人、史五人；

translations.literal: Upper prefectures had two assistants and five clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Upper prefectures had two assistants and five clerks;

sentences.zh: 中州減史二人。

translations.literal: Middle prefectures reduced clerks by two.
translations.idiomatic: middle prefectures two fewer clerks.

sentences.zh: 倉曹司倉參軍事，掌租調、公廨、庖廚、倉庫、市肆。

translations.literal: Granary Bureau Granary Secretary managed land tax and corvée assignments, official buildings, kitchens, granaries, and market stalls.
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Bureau Secretary managed land tax and corvée assignments, official buildings, kitchens, granaries, and market stalls.

sentences.zh: 有府五人，史十三人。

translations.literal: There were five office attendants and thirteen clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau employed five office attendants and thirteen clerks.

sentences.zh: 大都督府有府四人，史六人。

translations.literal: Great area command headquarters had four office attendants and six clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Great command headquarters had four office attendants and six clerks.

sentences.zh: 中府、下府，各有府三人，史五人。

translations.literal: Middle and lower prefectures each had three office attendants and five clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Middle and lower prefectures each maintained three attendants and five clerks.

sentences.zh: 都護府有府、史各二人。

translations.literal: Protectorate headquarters had two office attendants and two clerks each.
translations.idiomatic: Protectorate headquarters employed two attendants and two clerks apiece.

sentences.zh: 上州有佐二人，史五人；

translations.literal: Upper prefectures had two assistants and five clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Upper prefectures had two assistants and five clerks;

sentences.zh: 中州、下州減史二人。

translations.literal: Middle and lower prefectures reduced clerks by two.
translations.idiomatic: middle and lower prefectures two fewer clerks.

sentences.zh: 戶曹司戶參軍事，掌戶籍、計帳、道路、過所、蠲符、雜傜、逋負、艮賤、芻藳、逆旅、婚姻、田訟、旌別孝悌。

translations.literal: Household Bureau Household Secretary managed household registers, census accounts, roads, travel passes, tax exemptions, miscellaneous corvée, arrears, commoners and bondsmen, fodder, inns, marriage, field lawsuits, and marking out filial piety and fraternity.
translations.idiomatic: The Household Bureau Secretary managed household registers, census accounts, roads, travel passes, tax exemptions, miscellaneous corvée, arrears, commoners and bondsmen, fodder, inns, marriage, field lawsuits, and commendations for filial piety and fraternity.

sentences.zh: 有府八人，史十六人，帳史二人，知籍，按帳目捉錢。

translations.literal: There were eight office attendants, sixteen clerks, and two ledger clerks who knew the registers and tracked accounts to collect money.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau had eight office attendants, sixteen clerks, and two ledger clerks who maintained the registers and tracked accounts to collect revenue.

sentences.zh: 大都督府有府四人，史七人，帳史二人；

translations.literal: Great area command headquarters had four office attendants, seven clerks, and two ledger clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Great command headquarters had four office attendants, seven clerks, and two ledger clerks;

sentences.zh: 中府有府三人，史五人，帳史一人；

translations.literal: Middle prefectures had three office attendants, five clerks, and one ledger clerk;
translations.idiomatic: middle prefectures three office attendants, five clerks, and one ledger clerk;

sentences.zh: 下府有府二人，史五人，帳史一人。

translations.literal: Lower prefectures had two office attendants, five clerks, and one ledger clerk.
translations.idiomatic: and lower prefectures two office attendants, five clerks, and one ledger clerk.

sentences.zh: 上州有佐四人，史六人，帳史一人；

translations.literal: Upper prefectures had four assistants, six clerks, and one ledger clerk;
translations.idiomatic: Upper prefectures staffed four assistants, six clerks, and one ledger clerk;

sentences.zh: 中州有佐三人，史五人，帳史一人；

translations.literal: Middle prefectures had three assistants, five clerks, and one ledger clerk;
translations.idiomatic: middle prefectures three assistants, five clerks, and one ledger clerk;

sentences.zh: 下州有佐二人，史四人，帳史一人。

translations.literal: Lower prefectures had two assistants, four clerks, and one ledger clerk.
translations.idiomatic: and lower prefectures two assistants, four clerks, and one ledger clerk.

sentences.zh: 都護府有府、史各二人，帳史一人。

translations.literal: Protectorate headquarters had two office attendants, two clerks, and one ledger clerk each.
translations.idiomatic: Each protectorate headquarters had two attendants, two clerks, and one ledger clerk.

sentences.zh: 田曹司田參軍事，掌園宅、口分、永業及蔭田。

translations.literal: Fields Bureau Fields Secretary managed gardens and estates, allotted fields, hereditary fields, and inherited fields.
translations.idiomatic: The Fields Bureau Secretary managed gardens and estates, allotted fields, hereditary fields, and inherited fields.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，初置司田參軍事，唐隆元年省，上元二年復置。

translations.literal: In Jinglong 3, Fields Bureau Secretary was first established; abolished in Tanglong 1; restored in Shangyuan 2.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 3 the court first established the Fields Bureau Secretary; the post was abolished in Tanglong 1 and restored in Shangyuan 2.

sentences.zh: 有府四人，史十人。

translations.literal: There were four office attendants and ten clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau employed four office attendants and ten clerks.

sentences.zh: 大都督府有府二人，史六人；

translations.literal: Great area command headquarters had two office attendants and six clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Great command headquarters had two attendants and six clerks;

sentences.zh: 中府有府、史各二人；

translations.literal: Middle prefectures had two office attendants and two clerks each;
translations.idiomatic: middle prefectures two attendants and two clerks apiece;

sentences.zh: 下府有府一人，史二人。

translations.literal: Lower prefectures had one office attendant and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: and lower prefectures one attendant and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 上州有佐二人，史五人；

translations.literal: Upper prefectures had two assistants and five clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Upper prefectures had two assistants and five clerks;

sentences.zh: 中州、下州減史二人。

translations.literal: Middle and lower prefectures reduced clerks by two.
translations.idiomatic: middle and lower prefectures two fewer clerks.

sentences.zh: 兵曹司兵參軍事，掌武官選、兵甲、器仗、門禁、管鑰、軍防、烽候、傳驛、畋獵。

translations.literal: Military Bureau Military Secretary managed selection of military officers, armor and weapons, equipment, gate security, key management, military defense, beacon stations, courier posts, and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau Secretary managed selection of military officers, armor, weapons, equipment, gate security, keys, garrison defense, beacon stations, courier relays, and hunting.

sentences.zh: 有府六人，史十四人。

translations.literal: There were six office attendants and fourteen clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau employed six office attendants and fourteen clerks.

sentences.zh: 大都督府有府四人，史八人；

translations.literal: Great area command headquarters had four office attendants and eight clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Great command headquarters had four office attendants and eight clerks;

sentences.zh: 中府有府三人，史六人；

translations.literal: Middle prefectures had three office attendants and six clerks;
translations.idiomatic: middle prefectures three attendants and six clerks;

sentences.zh: 下府有府二人，史五人。

translations.literal: Lower prefectures had two office attendants and five clerks.
translations.idiomatic: and lower prefectures two attendants and five clerks.

sentences.zh: 都護府有府三人，史四人。

translations.literal: Protectorate headquarters had three office attendants and four clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Each protectorate headquarters had three attendants and four clerks.

sentences.zh: 上州有佐二人，史五人；

translations.literal: Upper prefectures had two assistants and five clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Upper prefectures had two assistants and five clerks;

sentences.zh: 中州減史二人。

translations.literal: Middle prefectures reduced clerks by two.
translations.idiomatic: middle prefectures two fewer clerks.

sentences.zh: 法曹司法參軍事，掌鞠獄麗法、督盜賊、知贓賄沒入。

translations.literal: Justice Bureau Judicial Secretary managed interrogating cases and applying law, supervising bandits and thieves, and knowing confiscation of bribes and stolen goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Justice Bureau Secretary conducted interrogations and applied the law, supervised banditry and theft, and handled confiscation of bribes and illicit goods.

sentences.zh: 有府六人，史十四人。

translations.literal: There were six office attendants and fourteen clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau employed six office attendants and fourteen clerks.

sentences.zh: 大都督府有府三人，史八人；

translations.literal: Great area command headquarters had three office attendants and eight clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Great command headquarters had three office attendants and eight clerks;

sentences.zh: 中府有府三人，史六人；

translations.literal: Middle prefectures had three office attendants and six clerks;
translations.idiomatic: middle prefectures three attendants and six clerks;

sentences.zh: 下府有府二人，史五人。

translations.literal: Lower prefectures had two office attendants and five clerks.
translations.idiomatic: and lower prefectures two attendants and five clerks.

sentences.zh: 上州有佐四人，史七人；

translations.literal: Upper prefectures had four assistants and seven clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Upper prefectures had four assistants and seven clerks;

sentences.zh: 中州有佐一人，史四人；

translations.literal: Middle prefectures had one assistant and four clerks;
translations.idiomatic: middle prefectures one assistant and four clerks;

sentences.zh: 下州有佐一人，史三人。

translations.literal: Lower prefectures had one assistant and three clerks.
translations.idiomatic: and lower prefectures one assistant and three clerks.

sentences.zh: 士曹司士參軍事，掌津梁、舟車、舍宅、工藝。

translations.literal: Works Bureau Works Secretary managed fords and bridges, boats and carts, dwellings and estates, and crafts.
translations.idiomatic: The Works Bureau Secretary managed bridges and crossings, transport, housing, and crafts.

sentences.zh: 有府五人，史十一人。

translations.literal: There were five office attendants and eleven clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau employed five office attendants and eleven clerks.

sentences.zh: 大都督府有府四人，史八人；

translations.literal: Great area command headquarters had four office attendants and eight clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Great command headquarters had four office attendants and eight clerks;

sentences.zh: 中府、下府有府三人，史六人。

translations.literal: Middle and lower prefectures had three office attendants and six clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Middle and lower prefectures each maintained three attendants and six clerks.

sentences.zh: 上州有佐二人，史五人；

translations.literal: Upper prefectures had two assistants and five clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Upper prefectures had two assistants and five clerks;

sentences.zh: 中州有佐一人，史四人。

translations.literal: Middle prefectures had one assistant and four clerks.
translations.idiomatic: and middle prefectures one assistant and four clerks.

sentences.zh: 參軍事掌出使、贊導。

translations.literal: Secretaries managed missions abroad and ceremonial guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Secretaries handled diplomatic missions and protocol guidance.

sentences.zh: 武德初，改行書佐曰行參軍，尋又改曰參軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, Acting Document Assistant was changed to Acting Secretary; soon after changed again to Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude period the title Acting Document Assistant became Acting Secretary, and was soon retitled Secretary.

sentences.zh: 初有亟使十五人，後省。

translations.literal: Initially there were fifteen urgent dispatchers; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At first there were fifteen urgent couriers; the post was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 文學一人，從八品上。

translations.literal: Literary Officer — one, upper secondary eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Literary Officer of upper secondary eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌以五經授諸生。

translations.literal: Managed teaching the Five Classics to students.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed students in the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 縣則州補，州則授於吏部。

translations.literal: At the county level the prefecture filled the post; at the prefecture level appointment came from the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: County appointments came from the prefecture; prefectural appointments came from the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 然無職事，衣冠恥之。

translations.literal: However, there were no official duties, and the gentry were ashamed of the post.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the post carried no real duties, and educated men regarded it with contempt.

sentences.zh: 武德初，置經學博士、助教、學生。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, Classics Doctor, Assistant Instructor, and students were established.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude period the court established Classics Doctors, assistant instructors, and students.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，改博士曰文學。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended the throne, Doctor was changed to Literary Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong took the throne the title Classics Doctor was changed to Literary Officer.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，廢中州、下州文學。

translations.literal: In Yuanhe 6, Literary Officers in middle and lower prefectures were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 6 the court abolished Literary Officers in middle and lower prefectures.

sentences.zh: 京兆等三府，助教二人，學生八十人。

translations.literal: Jingzhao and the other two capitals had two assistant instructors and eighty students.
translations.idiomatic: The three capital prefectures each had two assistant instructors and eighty students.

sentences.zh: 大都督府、上州，各助教一人；

translations.literal: Great area command headquarters and upper prefectures each had one assistant instructor;
translations.idiomatic: Great command headquarters and upper prefectures had one assistant instructor each;

sentences.zh: 中都督府，學生五十人；

translations.literal: Middle area command headquarters had fifty students;
translations.idiomatic: middle command headquarters fifty students;

sentences.zh: 下府、下州，各四十人。

translations.literal: Lower prefectures and lower prefectures each had forty persons.
translations.idiomatic: and lower command headquarters and lower prefectures forty students each.

sentences.zh: 醫學博士一人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Medical Doctor — one, upper secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Medical Doctor of upper secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌療民疾。

translations.literal: Managed treating the people's illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: He treated the people's illnesses.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，置醫學，有醫藥博士及學生。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan 3, medicine studies were established, with Pharmaceutical Doctor and students.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 3 the court established medical schools with pharmaceutical doctors and students.

sentences.zh: 開元元年，改醫藥博士為醫學博士，諸州置助教，寫本草、百一集驗方藏之。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 1, Pharmaceutical Doctor was changed to Medical Doctor; assistant instructors were established in all prefectures; Materia Medica and the Collection of One Hundred Verified Formulas were copied and stored.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 1 the Pharmaceutical Doctor was retitled Medical Doctor, assistant instructors were placed in every prefecture, and copies of the Materia Medica and the Collection of One Hundred Verified Formulas were deposited in storehouses.

sentences.zh: 未幾，醫學博士、學生皆省，僻州少醫藥者如故。

translations.literal: Before long, Medical Doctors and students were all abolished; remote prefectures lacking medicine remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Medical Doctors and students were all cut, and remote prefectures still had little access to medicine as before.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，復置醫學生，掌州境巡療。

translations.literal: In year 27, medical students were restored, managing itinerant treatment within the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 medical students were restored to treat the people throughout the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，復置醫學博士。

translations.literal: In Yongtai 1, Medical Doctor was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 the Medical Doctor post was restored.

sentences.zh: 三都、都督府、上州、中州各有助教一人。

translations.literal: The three capitals, area command headquarters, upper prefectures, and middle prefectures each had one assistant instructor.
translations.idiomatic: The three capitals, command headquarters, upper prefectures, and middle prefectures each had one medical assistant instructor.

sentences.zh: 三都學生二十人，都督府、上州二十人，中州、下州十人。

translations.literal: The three capitals had twenty students; area command headquarters and upper prefectures twenty; middle and lower prefectures ten.
translations.idiomatic: The three capitals had twenty medical students; command headquarters and upper prefectures twenty; middle and lower prefectures ten.
