sentences.zh: 都督掌督諸州兵馬、甲械、城隍、鎮戍、糧稟，總判府事。

translations.literal: Area Commander managed supervising troops and horses of all prefectures, armor and weapons, city walls and moats, garrison posts, grain rations, and adjudicated all headquarters affairs in general.
translations.idiomatic: The Area Commander supervised troops, armor, fortifications, garrisons, and grain supplies across the prefectures under his command and held general authority over headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 武德初，邊要之地置總管以統軍，加號使持節，蓋漢刺史之任。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, in strategically important border areas Area Superintendents were established to command armies, with the added title Credential Holder — roughly the duties of Han dynasty Inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude period the court placed area superintendents in key border regions to command troops, giving them the title Credential Holder — essentially reviving the Han Inspector's role.

sentences.zh: 有行臺，有大行臺。

translations.literal: There were mobile headquarters and grand mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: There were both mobile headquarters and grand mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 其員有尚書省令一人，正二品，掌管內兵民，總判省事。

translations.literal: Its staff included one Chief of the Secretariat — upper second rank — managing internal military and civilian affairs and adjudicating all secretariat business in general.
translations.idiomatic: Its staff included one Secretariat Chief of upper second rank who directed internal military and civilian affairs and held overall authority over the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有僕射一人，從二品，掌貳令事。

translations.literal: There was one Vice Director — secondary second rank — managing assisting the chief's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Vice Director of secondary second rank who assisted the chief.

sentences.zh: 自左右丞以下，諸司郎中略如京省。

translations.literal: From Left and Right Assistant Directors downward, the directors of various bureaus were roughly like those of the capital secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From the Left and Right Assistant Directors downward, bureau directors were organized much like those at the capital.

sentences.zh: 又有食貨監一人，丞二人，掌膳羞、財物、賓客、帳具、音樂、醫藥；

translations.literal: There were also one Provisions Supervisor and two assistants, managing delicacies, goods, guests, tent furnishings, music, and medicine;
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Provisions Supervisor with two assistants who managed food, supplies, guests, tent furnishings, music, and medicine;

sentences.zh: 有農圃監一人，丞四人，掌倉廩、園圃、薪炭、芻藳、運漕；

translations.literal: One Agriculture and Gardens Supervisor and four assistants, managing granaries, gardens, fuel and charcoal, fodder, and transport by canal;
translations.idiomatic: an Agriculture and Gardens Supervisor with four assistants who managed granaries, gardens, fuel, fodder, and canal transport;

sentences.zh: 有武器監一人，丞二人，掌兵械、廄牧；

translations.literal: One Weapons Supervisor and two assistants, managing military equipment and stables;
translations.idiomatic: a Weapons Supervisor with two assistants who managed arms and stables;

sentences.zh: 有百工監一人，丞四人，掌舟車、營作。

translations.literal: One Hundred Crafts Supervisor and four assistants, managing boats and carts and construction work.
translations.idiomatic: and a Hundred Crafts Supervisor with four assistants who managed transport and construction.

sentences.zh: 監皆正八品下，丞正九品下。

translations.literal: Supervisors were all lower eighth rank; assistants lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors held lower eighth rank and their assistants lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 七年，改總管曰都督，總十州者為大都督。

translations.literal: In year 7, Area Superintendent was changed to Area Commander; one commanding ten prefectures became Great Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 the Area Superintendent was retitled Area Commander, and one commanding ten prefectures became Great Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，去大字，凡都督府有刺史以下如故，然大都督又兼刺史，而不檢校州事。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan 2, the character "great" was removed; all area command headquarters retained prefects and below as before, yet the great area commander also held the post of prefect without inspecting prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 2 the "great" designation was dropped; command headquarters still had prefects and lower officials as before, but the great area commander also served as prefect without actually supervising prefectural administration.

sentences.zh: 其後都督加使持節，則為將，諸將亦通以都督稱，唯朔方猶稱大總管。

translations.literal: Afterward when area commanders were given Credential Holder, they became generals; generals also were commonly called area commanders; only Shuofang still used the title Great Area Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when area commanders received the Credential Holder title they became military generals; generals in turn were commonly called area commanders, though Shuofang still used the old title Great Area Superintendent.

sentences.zh: 邊州別置經略使，沃衍有屯田之州，則置營田使。

translations.literal: Border prefectures separately established Frontier Commissioners; prefectures with fertile expansion and garrison farming established Garrison Farming Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Border prefectures received separate frontier commissioners, and prefectures with productive garrison lands received garrison farming commissioners.

sentences.zh: 武后聖曆元年，以夏州都督領鹽州防禦使。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's Shengli 1, the Xiazhou Area Commander was made to hold concurrently the Yanzhou Defense Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's Shengli 1 the Xiazhou Area Commander was also appointed Defense Commissioner of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反，諸郡當賊衝者，皆置防禦守捉使。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, all commanderies in the path of the rebels established Defense and Garrison Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, every commandery in the rebels' path established defense and garrison commissioners.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，置團練守捉使、都團練守捉使，大者領州十餘，小者二三州。

translations.literal: In Qianyuan 1, Training and Garrison Commissioners and Supreme Training and Garrison Commissioners were established; the larger ones commanded more than ten prefectures, the smaller two or three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1 the court established Training and Garrison Commissioners and Supreme Training and Garrison Commissioners; the larger posts commanded more than ten prefectures, the smaller two or three.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，廢防禦使，唯山南西道如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong took the throne, Defense Commissioners were abolished, only Southwestern Shannan Circuit remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Defense Commissioners were abolished everywhere except Southwestern Shannan Circuit, which remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 元載秉政，思結人心，刺史皆得兼團練守捉使。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai held power, seeking to win hearts, all prefects were permitted to concurrently hold the post of Training and Garrison Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuan Zai dominated the government and sought to win popular support, every prefect was allowed to serve concurrently as Training and Garrison Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 楊綰為相，罷團練守捉使，唯澧、朗、峽、興、鳳如故。

translations.literal: When Yang Wan became chancellor, Training and Garrison Commissioners were abolished, only Li, Lang, Xia, Xing, and Feng remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Wan became chancellor, Training and Garrison Commissioners were abolished, except in Li, Lang, Xia, Xing, and Feng prefectures, which kept the posts.

sentences.zh: 建中後，行營亦置節度使、防禦使、都團練使。

translations.literal: After Jianzhong, mobile headquarters also established Military Commissioners, Defense Commissioners, and Supreme Training Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jianzhong era, field headquarters likewise appointed Military Commissioners, Defense Commissioners, and Supreme Training Commissioners.

sentences.zh: 大率節度、觀察、防禦、團練使，皆兼所治州刺史。

translations.literal: Generally Military, Surveillance, Defense, and Training Commissioners all concurrently served as prefect of the prefecture they administered.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, Military, Surveillance, Defense, and Training Commissioners all held concurrent appointment as prefect of the prefecture under their charge.

sentences.zh: 都督府則領長史，都護府則領都護，或亦別置都護。

translations.literal: Area command headquarters were headed by a chief secretary; protectorate headquarters by a protector-general, or a protector-general might be separately appointed.
translations.idiomatic: An area command headquarters was led by a chief secretary and a protectorate headquarters by a protector-general, though a protector-general might also be appointed separately.

sentences.zh: 都督府有掾，有屬，有記室參軍事，有典籤，武德中省。

translations.literal: Area command headquarters had clerks, subordinates, secretaries, and document custodians; these were abolished during Wude.
translations.idiomatic: Area command headquarters once employed clerks, subordinates, secretaries, and document custodians, but these posts were abolished in the Wude era.

sentences.zh: 市令一人，從九品上。

translations.literal: One Market Director, upper secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Market Director of upper secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌交易，禁姦非，通判市事。

translations.literal: Managed commerce, prohibited illicit conduct, and in general judged market affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised trade, banned illicit dealings, and oversaw market administration in general.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十七年廢市令。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan 17 the Market Director was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Market Director was abolished in Zhenguan 17.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年復置。

translations.literal: In Chuigong 1 it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The post was restored in Chuigong 1.

sentences.zh: 都督府、三都、諸州，各有市丞一人，佐一人，史二人，帥三人，分行檢察；

translations.literal: Area command headquarters, the three capitals, and all prefectures each had one market assistant, one aide, two clerks, and three chiefs, who conducted inspections in separate routes;
translations.idiomatic: Area command headquarters, the three capitals, and every prefecture each had one market assistant, one aide, two clerks, and three chiefs who carried out inspections on separate rounds;

sentences.zh: 倉督二人，顓涖出納；

translations.literal: two granary overseers, solely managing receipts and disbursements;
translations.idiomatic: two granary overseers who handled receipts and disbursements exclusively;

sentences.zh: 史二人。

translations.literal: two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: and two clerks.

sentences.zh: 下州省丞。

translations.literal: Lower prefectures omitted the assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Lower prefectures did without the market assistant.

translations.idiomatic: Great Protectorate Headquarters: one Grand Protector-General of secondary second rank;

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，始參用庶姓。

translations.literal: In Jingyun 2 commoners were first employed among them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 2 men of common birth were first appointed to these posts.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，改刺史曰太守。

sentences.zh: 八載，諸郡廢別駕，下郡置長史一員。

sentences.zh: 上元二年，諸州復置別駕。

sentences.zh: 德宗時，復省。

translations.literal: During Emperor Dezong's reign they were again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Dezong they were abolished once more.

sentences.zh: 元和、長慶之際，兩河用兵，裨將有功者補東宮王府官，久次當進及受代居京師者，常數十人，訴宰相以求官；

translations.literal: At the time of Yuanhe and Changqing, with warfare in the two He regions, meritorious staff officers were appointed to Eastern Palace and princely household posts; those long overdue for promotion and those awaiting replacement while residing in the capital often numbered several dozen, petitioning the chancellor for office;
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe and Changqing periods, as the two He regions saw constant warfare, meritorious staff officers were given posts in the Eastern Palace and princely households; dozens of men long overdue for promotion or awaiting reassignment while staying in the capital would petition the chancellor for appointments;

sentences.zh: 文宗世，宰相韋處厚建議，復置兩輔、六雄、十望、十緊州別駕。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wenzong's reign, Chancellor Wei Chuhou proposed restoring Vice Prefects for the two auxiliary capitals, six great prefectures, ten prestigious prefectures, and ten critical prefectures.

sentences.zh: 縣令掌導風化，察冤滯，聽獄訟。

translations.literal: The county magistrate supervised moral transformation, examined lingering wrongs and delays, and heard lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate guided local customs, investigated unresolved grievances and delays, and adjudicated lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 凡民田收授，縣令給之。

translations.literal: For all commoners' fields received and granted, the county magistrate issued them.
translations.idiomatic: For all allotment and reclamation of commoners' fields, the county magistrate made the grants.

sentences.zh: 每歲季冬，行鄉飲酒禮。

translations.literal: Each year at the end of winter, the village drinking ceremony was performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of each winter the county held the village drinking ceremony.

sentences.zh: 籍帳、傳驛、倉庫、盜賊、隄道，雖有專官，皆通知。

translations.literal: Household registers, courier relays, granaries, bandits and thieves, and embankment roads — though each had dedicated officers, all were reported to the magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Household registers, courier relays, granaries, banditry, and embankment roads each had their own officers, yet the magistrate was kept informed of them all.

sentences.zh: 縣丞為之貳，縣尉分判衆曹，收率課調。

translations.literal: The assistant served as second to the magistrate; bailiffs divided judgment among the various bureaus and collected taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant served as the magistrate's deputy; bailiffs divided authority among the bureaus and collected taxes and corvée levies.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，改書佐曰縣尉，尋改曰正。

translations.literal: In Wude 1, Writing Assistants were retitled bailiffs; soon after they were retitled Rectifiers.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1 writing assistants became bailiffs; soon afterward the title was changed to Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 諸縣置主簿，以流外為之。

translations.literal: All counties established chief clerks, filled by men from outside the regular hierarchy.
translations.idiomatic: Every county had a chief clerk, appointed from outside the regular hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 京縣、上縣、丞皆一人；

translations.literal: Capital Counties and Upper Counties each had one assistant;
translations.idiomatic: In Capital Counties and Upper Counties there was one assistant each;

translations.literal: Capital Vicinity Counties and Upper Counties each had four Rectifiers.
translations.idiomatic: and Capital Vicinity Counties and Upper Counties four bailiffs apiece.

sentences.zh: 七年，改縣正復曰尉。

translations.literal: In year 7, county Rectifiers were again retitled bailiffs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year county Rectifiers were again renamed bailiffs.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，諸縣置錄事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, all counties established recorders.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan period every county gained a recorder.

sentences.zh: 開元，上縣萬戶、中縣四千戶以上，增尉一人。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan, for upper counties of ten thousand households and middle counties of four thousand households or more, one bailiff was added.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan, upper counties of ten thousand households and middle counties of four thousand or more each received an additional bailiff.

sentences.zh: 京兆、河南府諸縣，戶三千以上置市令一人，戶一萬以上置義倉督三人。

translations.literal: In the counties of Jingzhao and Henan prefectures, those with three thousand households or more had one Market Director; those with ten thousand households or more had three Charity Granary overseers.
translations.idiomatic: In the counties under Jingzhao and Henan, those with three thousand households or more had one Market Director, and those with ten thousand or more had three Charity Granary overseers.

sentences.zh: 其後畿縣戶不及四千，亦置尉二人，萬戶增一人。

translations.literal: Later, for Capital Vicinity Counties with fewer than four thousand households, two bailiffs were also established; for every ten thousand households one was added.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Capital Vicinity Counties with fewer than four thousand households also received two bailiffs, with one added for every ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 凡縣有司功佐、司倉佐、司戶佐、司兵佐、司法佐、司士佐、典獄、門事等，畿縣減司兵，上縣有司戶、司法而已。

translations.literal: All counties had Merit, Granary, Household, Military, Justice, and Works Bureau assistants, prison supervisors, gate attendants, and the like; Capital Vicinity Counties omitted the Military Bureau assistant, and Upper Counties had only Household and Justice Bureau assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Every county staffed Merit, Granary, Household, Military, Justice, and Works Bureau assistants, prison supervisors, gate attendants, and the like; Capital Vicinity Counties dropped the Military Bureau assistant, and Upper Counties retained only Household and Justice Bureau assistants.

sentences.zh: 凡縣皆有經學博士、助教各一人，京縣學生五十人，畿縣四十人，中縣以下各二十五人。

translations.literal: All counties had one Classics Doctor and one assistant instructor each; Capital Counties had fifty students, Capital Vicinity Counties forty, and middle counties and below twenty-five each.
translations.idiomatic: Every county had one Classics Doctor and one assistant instructor; Capital Counties enrolled fifty students, Capital Vicinity Counties forty, and middle counties and below twenty-five each.

sentences.zh: 鎮將、鎮副、戍主、戍副，掌捍防守禦。

translations.literal: Garrison Generals, Garrison Vice Generals, Garrison Commanders, and Garrison Vice Commanders managed defense and guarding.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Generals, Garrison Vice Generals, Garrison Commanders, and Garrison Vice Commanders held the line and organized the defense.

sentences.zh: 凡上鎮二十，中鎮九十，下鎮一百三十五；

translations.literal: Upper garrisons numbered twenty, middle garrisons ninety, and lower garrisons one hundred thirty-five;
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty upper garrisons, ninety middle garrisons, and one hundred thirty-five lower garrisons;

sentences.zh: 上戍十一，中戍八十六，下戍二百四十五。

translations.literal: upper garrison posts eleven, middle garrison posts eighty-six, and lower garrison posts two hundred forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: eleven upper garrison posts, eighty-six middle garrison posts, and two hundred forty-five lower garrison posts.

sentences.zh: 倉曹參軍事，掌儀式、倉庫、飲膳、醫藥、付事、句稽、省署鈔目、監印、給紙筆、市易、公廨。

translations.literal: The Granary Bureau Secretary managed ritual display, granaries, food and drink, medicine, assignment of affairs, audit, oversight of office copies, watching the seal, supplying paper and brushes, market transactions, and official buildings.
translations.idiomatic: The Granary Bureau Secretary oversaw ceremonial display, granaries, provisions, medicine, task assignment, auditing, office registers, seal custody, paper and writing supplies, market transactions, and official quarters.

sentences.zh: 中鎮則兵曹兼掌。

translations.literal: At middle garrisons the Military Bureau Secretary also handled these duties.
translations.idiomatic: At middle garrisons the Military Bureau Secretary handled these duties as well.

sentences.zh: 兵曹參軍事，掌防人名帳、戎器、管鑰、馬驢、土木、讁罰之事。

translations.literal: The Military Bureau Secretary managed garrison troop rosters, weapons, keys, horses and donkeys, construction and earthworks, and disciplinary penalties.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Bureau Secretary kept garrison troop rosters, managed weapons, keys, horses and donkeys, construction and earthworks, and disciplinary penalties.

sentences.zh: 上鎮有錄事一人，史一人，倉曹佐一人、史二人，兵曹佐、史各二人，倉督一人、史二人。

translations.literal: Upper garrisons had one recording clerk, one clerk, one Granary Bureau assistant and two clerks, two Military Bureau assistants and two clerks, and one granary overseer and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Upper garrisons employed one recording clerk, one clerk, one Granary Bureau assistant with two clerks, two Military Bureau assistants with two clerks, and one granary overseer with two clerks.

sentences.zh: 中鎮，錄事一人，兵曹佐一人、史四人，倉督一人、史二人。

translations.literal: Middle garrisons: one recording clerk, one Military Bureau assistant and four clerks, and one granary overseer and two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Middle garrisons had one recording clerk, one Military Bureau assistant with four clerks, and one granary overseer with two clerks.

sentences.zh: 下鎮，錄事一人，兵曹佐一人、史二人，倉督一人、史一人。

translations.literal: Lower garrisons: one recording clerk, one Military Bureau assistant and two clerks, and one granary overseer and one clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Lower garrisons had one recording clerk, one Military Bureau assistant with two clerks, and one granary overseer with one clerk.

sentences.zh: 凡軍鎮，五百人有押官一人，千人有子總管一人，五千人又有府三人、史四人。

translations.literal: For all army garrisons, five hundred men had one escort officer; one thousand men had one sub-commander; five thousand men also had three office attendants and four clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In every army garrison five hundred men had one escort officer, one thousand had one sub-commander, and five thousand also had three office attendants and four clerks.

sentences.zh: 上戍，佐一人、史二人；

translations.literal: Upper garrison posts: one assistant and two clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Upper garrison posts had one assistant and two clerks;

sentences.zh: 中戍，史二人；

translations.literal: middle garrison posts: two clerks;
translations.idiomatic: middle garrison posts two clerks;

sentences.zh: 下戍，史一人。

translations.literal: lower garrison posts: one clerk.
translations.idiomatic: and lower garrison posts one clerk.

sentences.zh: 唐廢戍子，每防人五百人為上鎮，三百人為中鎮，不及者為下鎮；

translations.literal: The Tang abolished garrison-son posts; every five hundred defense troops formed an upper garrison, three hundred a middle garrison, and fewer a lower garrison;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang abolished the garrison-son posts; every five hundred defense troops made an upper garrison, three hundred a middle garrison, and fewer a lower garrison;

sentences.zh: 五十人為上戍，三十人為中戍，不及者為下戍。

translations.literal: fifty men formed an upper garrison post, thirty a middle garrison post, and fewer a lower garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: fifty men made an upper garrison post, thirty a middle garrison post, and fewer a lower garrison post.

sentences.zh: 開元十五年，朔方五城各置田曹參軍事一人，品同諸軍判司，專莅營田。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 15, each of the Five Cities of Shuofang established one Fields Bureau Secretary, with rank equal to army bureau secretaries, devoted exclusively to garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 each of the Five Cities of Shuofang received one Fields Bureau Secretary, with rank equal to army bureau secretaries, devoted exclusively to garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 永泰後，諸鎮官頗增減開元之舊。

translations.literal: After Yongtai, garrison offices were greatly increased or reduced from the Kaiyuan establishment.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongtai era garrison offices were greatly expanded or cut back from the Kaiyuan establishment.

sentences.zh: 五岳、四瀆，令各一人，正九品上，掌祭祀。

translations.literal: The Five Sacred Peaks and Four Rivers each had one Director, upper regular ninth rank, managing sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Sacred Peaks and Four Rivers each had one Director of upper regular ninth rank who oversaw sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 有祝史三人，齋郎各三十人。

translations.literal: There were three Invocation Officers and thirty Fasting Attendants at each site.
translations.idiomatic: Each site had three Invocation Officers and thirty Fasting Attendants.

sentences.zh: 上關，令一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: Upper Pass: one Director, lower secondary eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Upper Pass: one Director of lower secondary eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: two assistants, lower regular ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants of lower regular ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 中關，令一人，正九品下；

translations.literal: Middle Pass: one Director, lower regular ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Middle Pass: one Director of lower regular ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，從九品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 下關，令一人，亦從九品下。

translations.literal: Lower Pass: one Director, also lower secondary ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lower Pass: one Director, likewise of lower secondary ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌禁末游，察姦慝。

translations.literal: They prohibited idle wandering and detected treachery.
translations.idiomatic: They barred idle wandering and detected treachery.

sentences.zh: 凡行人車馬出入，據過所為往來之節。

translations.literal: For all travelers, horses, and carts entering or leaving, travel passes served as the credential for coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: All travelers, horses, and carts entering or leaving were checked against travel passes as credentials for passage.

sentences.zh: 凡關二十有六，京四面關有驛道者為上關，無驛道者為中關，餘為下關。

translations.literal: Passes numbered twenty-six in all; passes on the four sides of the capital with courier routes were upper passes, those without courier routes middle passes, and the rest lower passes.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty-six passes in all: capital passes on courier routes ranked as upper passes, those without courier routes as middle passes, and the remainder as lower passes.

sentences.zh: 丞掌付事、句稽、監印、省署鈔目，通判關事。

translations.literal: Assistants managed assignment of affairs, audit, watching the seal, and oversight of office copies, exercising joint authority over pass affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Assistants assigned tasks, audited accounts, watched the seal, and checked office registers, exercising joint authority over pass affairs.

sentences.zh: 上關，錄事一人，府二人，史四人，典事六人。

translations.literal: Upper passes: one recording clerk, two office attendants, four clerks, and six general attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Upper passes had one recording clerk, two office attendants, four clerks, and six general attendants.

sentences.zh: 中關，錄事一人，府二人，史二人，典事四人。

translations.literal: Middle passes: one recording clerk, two office attendants, two clerks, and four general attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Middle passes had one recording clerk, two office attendants, two clerks, and four general attendants.

sentences.zh: 下關，府一人，史、典事各二人。

translations.literal: Lower passes: one office attendant, two clerks, and two general attendants each.
translations.idiomatic: Lower passes had one office attendant, two clerks, and two general attendants each.

sentences.zh: 典事掌巡薙及雜當。

translations.literal: General attendants managed patrol weeding and miscellaneous duties.
translations.idiomatic: General attendants handled patrol weeding and miscellaneous duties.

sentences.zh: 初，諸關置都尉，亦有它官奉敕監者。

translations.literal: At first, all passes had Commandants established, and there were also other officials appointed by imperial order to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: At first every pass had a Commandant, and other officials were also appointed by imperial order to supervise.

sentences.zh: 上津置尉一人，掌舟梁之事；

translations.literal: Upper fords had one warden managing bridge and ferry affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Upper fords had one warden who managed bridges and ferries;

sentences.zh: 府一人，史二人，津長四人。

translations.literal: one office attendant, two clerks, and four ford chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: with one office attendant, two clerks, and four ford chiefs.

sentences.zh: 下津，尉一人，府一人，史二人，津長二人。

translations.literal: Lower fords: one warden, one office attendant, two clerks, and two ford chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Lower fords had one warden, one office attendant, two clerks, and two ford chiefs.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，廢津尉，上關置津吏八人。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui period ford wardens were abolished, and upper passes established eight ferry clerks.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui period ford wardens were abolished and upper passes were given eight ferry clerks.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，中關置津吏六人，下關四人，無津者不置。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, middle passes established six ferry clerks and lower passes four; where there was no ford, none were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 middle passes received six ferry clerks and lower passes four; where no ford existed, none were appointed.
